Our police officers currently do not have body- worn cameras, their electronic control devices are 10 to 14 years old, and their in-car cameras have an average age of 7 years old. The requested items link together to capture data which is then electronically transferred directly to the state attorney's office in a timely manner rather than transferring evidence via DVD like our officers are currently doing. Currently, our State Attorney's office only accepts electronic evidence via Evidence.com or DVD. The requested funding would give our police access to Evidence.com. This will incre
1017.purpose: The specific goal is to improve public and officer safety, increase transparency and accountability, and enhance the quality of evidence collected during law enforcement encounters by equipping officers with body-worn cameras, in-car video systems, and less lethal electronic control devices. The requested items link together to capture data which is then electronically transferred to the state attorney's office rather than transferring evidence via DVD like our officers are currently doing. This
1017.activities: The funds will support the purchase, training, deployment, and ongoing management of the body-worn cameras, in car-cameras, and electronic control devices. The funds will provide our law enforcement officers with tools to enhance public safety, increase transparency and accountability, improve evidence collection, and improve the delivery of evidence to the state attorney's office.
1017.direct_services: The direct services provided to citizens will be increased safety during encounters, unbiased video evidence to support complaints or court cases, protection of individual rights, and greater confidence in the fairness and accountability of law enforcement.
1017.population: The target population served by this project is anyone who comes in contact with law enforcement in the City of Satellite Beach. This ranges from elderly persons, persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, homeless, developmentally disabled, physically disabled, drug users, students of all ages, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, drug offenders, and victims of crime. We expect the number individ
1017.outcome: The expected benefits and outcomes of this project are a reduction in injuries to subjects officers have arrested, a reduction in injury reports to our officers, an increase in positive interactions with our law enforcement officers, an observation of an increase of evidence being delivered to the State Attorney's office in a timely manner. These outcomes can be measured through the observation of law enforcement report data, in-car and body worn camera data, and an increase in successfully prosecuted criminal cases originating in the City of Satellite Beach.

2824.description: This project will bolster current and projected enrollment growth at the Blount Center, which has increased to 3,300 students, including 464% growth since 2020 and is estimated to reach 5,000-7,000 annually. SF will create a Workforce Innovation and Training Center to better serve local businesses by supporting upskilling and reskilling efforts for both the unemployed and underemployed and by providing new instructional and customized training spaces for credit and non- credit programming. SF’s Foundation, who has supported previous site phases by giving SF $5.56M of property to the college, will also contribute an additional $4M to this project.
2824.purpose: The goal of this project is to increase access to higher education and support existing growth of the campus, including for nearby rural areas, while helping to drive economic development in collaboration with workforce partners, employers and employees. It is intended to become a workforce innovation hub for businesses and those unemployed or underemployed. Credit earning enrollment has increased 464% at this location since 2020, with non-credit training tripling over this period of time due to
2824.activities: Academic instruction and short-term credentialing through class, training, seminars, boot camps, workshops and other related upskilling and reskilling opportunities for those who are unemployed or underemployed; programs will also allow for businesses to develop by using versatile, technology-rich teaching space.
2824.direct_services: Once completed, the college will provide credit and non-credit academic offerings and associated support services in the new facility designed to meet local workforce needs. Instructional and training spaces will function to increase and enhance short-term training, certificates, upskilling/reskilling, stackable credentials, and entrepreneurship opportunities.
2824.population: The target populations for this project would include college students, adults who are unemployed or underemployed, and employers seeking employees or employers seeking to train existing employees. It will also provide additional access to students from surrounding rural areas of the service district.
2824.outcome: Increased support for local businesses by offering opportunities to educate and train existing and prospective employees. The spaces will help facilitate the development of the workforce and business by doubling the number of non-degree industry certifications awarded within five years, from 447 to 900. This will be measured by analyzing space utilization as well as tracking and assessing data related to student enrollment, performance, job placement and entry level wages.

2822.description: The current restrooms were built 50+ years ago and do not comply with ADA requirements. Renovations to the existing Men's & Women's group restrooms located on the west side of the building and renovations and an expansion of the existing Men's & Women's group restrooms located on the east side and lobby area. Both sets of bathrooms will become larger and ADA compliant. This facility is the only large use facility on campus. The center hosts graduations, banquets, community and sporting events and serves as a hub for Florida Lineman during storm preparation and recovery. Renovations and construction are essential to provide up to date restroom facilities for students, community, and for our lineman, ensuring the center remains a resilient hub for disaster response and a vital resource for Columbia County and the region.
2822.purpose: The funds will be used to renovate the Howard Conference Center, adding ADA-compliant restrooms to ensure safe and accessible facilities for individuals with disabilities. This will enable the center to continue to be a staging site for lineman during hurricanes, host job fairs for the community, graduations, cultural events & sporting, while servicing those with mobility challenges.
2822.activities: The funds will be used to renovate the Howard Conference Center, adding ADA-compliant restrooms to ensure safe and accessible facilities for individuals with disabilities. This will enable the center to continue to be a staging site for lineman during hurricanes, host job fairs for the community, graduations, cultural & sporting events, while servicing those with mobility challenges.
2822.direct_services: Any citizen visiting Florida Gateway College and the Howard Center who is disabled will now be able to utilize a new bathroom for ADA use. In addition, new bathrooms will also be constructed for the students and visitors of the Howard Center. The 50+ year old bathrooms will be demolished for the new construction bathrooms.
2822.population: Physically disabled, elderly, and including students this project will serve tens of thousands of people each year in Columbia County. Tens of thousands of individuals will be in this facility throughout the year.
2822.outcome: The expected benefit is that the physically disabled, elderly, and our students will have proper bathrooms to use in a multi-purpose facility of which is the only multi-purpose facility of it's kind on the Florida Gateway College campus and Columbia County.

1185.description: The purpose of the project is to replace the North Banana River Drive South Bridge (#704014), a single span bridge built in 1965. The bridge, at approximately 18.5ft in length crosses navigable Canal #3 which is connected to the Banana River. With noticeable deterioration of the structure and supporting walls, it has been determined that rehabilitation costs will continue to rise making replacement of the bridge necessary. The bridge connects residents and local businesses to SR-528, SR-A1A and SR-520.
1185.purpose: The requested funding will replace a bridge crossing a navigable canal connected to the Banana River and connects residents to SR-528, SR-A1A, and SR-520. The North Banana River Drive South Bridge is one of a cluster of four bridges in Merritt Island that have reached their potential lifespan. Other bridges in the area also requiring replacement include Girard Blvd Bridge and the North Banana River Drive North Bridge. The West Central Ave Bridge (#704024) Replacement Project was awarded State FY
1185.activities: New drainage improvements and a new bridge span consisting of two (2) 12-foot travel lanes with 16-inch shoulders and two (2) 6-foot sidewalks will be constructed. The superstructure will consist of Florida Slab beams and 24 sq-inch prestressed concrete pile foundation elements.
1185.direct_services: New ADA compliant sidewalks will be provided to accommodate pedestrians and other active transportation options to aid in safely traversing the bridge.
1185.population: The replacement project targets the general population in the area and will serve approximately 5000 residents and local businesses
1185.outcome: The replacement of the North Banana River Drive South Bridge will provide various benefits to the community by providing safe accommodations for multi-modal transportation users and will also alleviate drainage issues occurring on the existing bridge span. Since the bridge has reached its lifespan, a new structure in place will allow residents to get to and from their homes without the potential for failure or collapse.

1177.description: With the recent announcement of the nearest hospital’s closure, our community—particularly residents in one of the poorest census tracts in the city—faces a significant healthcare access crisis. Our plan is to repurpose a vacant community center into a fully equipped medical facility offering primary care, urgent care, maternal health services, and preventive screenings. This investment would ensure that critical healthcare services remain accessible to those who need them most.
1177.purpose: With the recent announcement of the nearest hospital’s closure, our community—particularly residents in one of the poorest census tracts in the city—faces a significant healthcare access crisis. Our plan is to repurpose a vacant community center into a fully equipped medical facility offering primary care, urgent care, maternal health services, and preventive screenings. This investment would ensure that critical healthcare services remain accessible to those who need them most.
1177.activities: The funding will address healthcare disparities, improve public health outcomes, and foster economic development. It will reduce strain on emergency rooms at distant hospitals, lower long-term healthcare costs through preventive care, and create jobs within the local economy. Furthermore, revitalizing this vacant facility will strengthen the community and improve overall quality of life for Cocoa
1177.direct_services: The refurbished healthcare facility will provide Cocoa residents with essential services including primary care, urgent care, mental health support, and preventive screenings. It will improve health outcomes, reduce emergency room strain, and offer health education while creating local jobs and addressing long-standing disparities in one of the city’s most underserved areas.
1177.population: The general public to include residents in the immediate Diamond Square neighborhood.
1177.outcome: Improve physical and mental health, protect the general public from harm, create immediate job opportunities, and reduce substance abuse. All of which can be measured through utilization counts.

3608.description: The goal of this request is to acquire 75 acres of Tampabay water front Land in Pinellas County for the purposes of land and water conservation. All funding provided in this request shall be made available to the Southwest Florida Water Management District (SWFWMD) for the use of acquiring the land located in Pinellas County. Once the agency receives the funds for this request, funding provided in this request shall be transferred to SWFWMD within 30 days of the receipt of funds.
3608.purpose: to protect preservation land that the waterway connects to Tampabay & the Gulf of Mexico/America
3608.activities: to protect preservation land that the waterway connects to Tampabay & the Gulf of Mexico/America
3608.direct_services: By securing this property under state ownership, Florida will safeguard sensitive ecosystems from future development, preserve biodiversity, and maintain vital habitats for threatened and endangered species. The land serves as a natural buffer that improves water quality, enhances flood mitigation, and contributes to the recharge of local aquifers.
3608.outcome: Climate resilience is factored in by evaluating the property’s ability to store carbon, absorb storm impacts, and maintain ecological stability under future conditions.Lands that buffer urban areas, protect coastlines, or serve as migration refuges for species under climate stress receive additional benefit consideration.

1073.description: CCA will spawn, raise, and release a combined minimum of 150,000 redfish and spotted seatrout, development of emergent in need species housing, grow and plant a minimum of 1,000 mangroves, recycle and deploy 70 tons of oyster shell to help enrich the coastal waters of Florida. With more people moving to Florida everyday there is more strain on our water quality and inshore fisheries.
1073.purpose: CCA will work to help grow redfish, trout, tripletail, mangroves trees, and oysters to enrich the coastal waters of Florida. With more people moving to Florida everyday there is more strain on our inshore fisheries.
1073.activities: CCA will work to grow juvenile redfish, trout, and tripletail to release around Florida's coast. CCA will also grow mangroves and create oyster bars that will help with water quality and shoreline stabilization.
1073.direct_services: The citizens will see better inshore fisheries and the oyster and mangroves will help with water quality.
1073.population: The coastal fishing population of Florida.
1073.outcome: The expected outcome will be more fish in the water to catch which will bring more tourist and money to coastal communities.

2464.organization: Jewish Federation of Florida's Gulf Coast
2464.description: Enhanced security for Jewish federations offices, schools, businesses, and synagogues in Pinellas, Hernando and Pasco by partnering with Sheriff Offices, police departments, and employing a regional security director. Using advanced technology and layered systems, the program prevents and detects antisemitic acts, terrorism, and active shooters, improves first responder awareness, speeds emergency response, and strengthens regional preparedness.
2464.purpose: Enhanced security for Jewish federations offices, schools, businesses, and synagogues in Pinellas, Hernando and Pasco by partnering with Sheriff Offices, police departments, and employing a regional security director. Using advanced technology and layered systems, the program prevents and detects antisemitic acts, terrorism, and active shooters, improves first responder awareness, speeds emergency response, and strengthens regional preparedness.
2464.activities: Off-duty law enforcement provide visible deterrence and rapid response at all Jewish facilities, while a regional security director coordinates security, training, and emergency preparedness. Security systems, AEDs, and trauma kits enhance first responder collaboration and ensure timely, effective responses to active shooters, terrorism, and other emergencies.
2464.direct_services: Knowledge and confidence they are protected by trained and certified off-duty law enforcement officers. Law enforcement will be immediately notified active shooters, acts of terrorism, etc., and will be able to better prepare for such emergencies.
2464.population: General public, Elderly Persons, Preschool, Grade School, High School, and College students. Individuals expected to be served is 36,000+ members of the Jewish community.
2464.outcome: Improve physical health, Improve mental health, Enrich cultural experience, Protect the general public from harm (environmental, criminal, etc.). Use of AEDs as life-saving tools and attendance/number of certifications issued by the CPR training program. Attendance of Jewish events. Attendance of Jewish cultural events. Tracked use of technologies and monitoring of their success rate in emergency incidents. Decrease in documented antisemitic events in and around Jewish facilities. Increased attendance at Jewish facilities.

1648.description: The Comprehensive Utility Strategic Master Plan (CUSMP) guides the repair and rehabilitation of the City’s aging triplex pump stations, which are vital for transferring wastewater to treatment facilities. Pump station failure can lead to sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs), exposing neighborhoods to untreated wastewater containing dangerous bacteria, viruses, and parasites. Such overflows create immediate threats to public health by increasing the risk of gastrointestinal illness, respiratory infections, and skin conditions, and can also contaminate local water sources and the environment. By investing in modernizing all critical mechanical, electrical, and control systems within these stations, the City directly reduces the likelihood and impact of SSOs, thereby safeguarding community health and ensuring reliable, efficient wastewater service for all residents.
1648.purpose: The requested funds will be used to rehabilitate four of the City of Fort Lauderdale’s high-priority triplex pump stations, which are critical to the safe and reliable transfer of wastewater to the George T. Lohmeyer Regional Wastewater Facility. The goal is to modernize mechanical, electrical, and control systems in order to prevent sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs), protect public health, safeguard groundwater and surface waters, and enhance the City’s long-term utility resilience.
1648.activities: Activities funded by this appropriation will include the removal and replacement of pumps, valves, suction and discharge piping, electrical and ventilation systems, and protective coatings for wet wells. Structural repairs will also be completed where necessary, and all controls will be relocated outside of the pump stations to ensure accessibility during flood events.
1648.direct_services: The project will provide residents and businesses with reliable and uninterrupted wastewater collection and transfer services, ensuring that sewage is consistently routed to the treatment facility and disposed of properly. By reducing the likelihood of SSOs, citizens will benefit from fewer health risks, decreased neighborhood flooding linked to system failures, and cleaner local waterways.
1648.population: The target population includes residents, businesses, and visitors within the service areas of the four prioritized pump stations (B-11, A-31, A-22, and A-29), as well as the wider City of Fort Lauderdale community that depends on a resilient wastewater system. It is estimated that tens of thousands of residents and businesses will directly benefit from these improvements, with citywide benefits reaching over 180,000 residents and millions of annual visitors.
1648.outcome: The expected benefits include reduced sanitary sewer overflows, fewer costly emergency interventions, improved groundwater and surface water quality, enhanced flood resilience, and reduced long-term maintenance costs. Outcomes will be measured by tracking reductions in SSOs, system failures, and flood-related service disruptions compared with historical data.

2682.description: The waiting list for older adults needing home delivered meals continues to grow every day in Northeast Florida. Food is health. Without good nutrition, older adults run the risk of health conditions associated with malnutrition such as weakened immune systems, exacerbated heart disease and hypertension. Individuals' risks of increased hospitalizations and increased healthcare costs associated with poor dietary management. Much of these costs are past down to to the community, tax payors, health care systems and the government. These funds would help mitigate hunger among older adults in northeast Florida by providing home delivered meals to those in need in Northeast Florida.
2682.purpose: The nutrition risk of those served will be reduced by the provision of the home delivered meals funded under this project.
2682.activities: Nutritionally balanced home delivered meals will be provided to frail older adults on the waiting list. They will also benefit from the socialization and wellness checks provided by the staff and/or volunteers delivering the meals.
2682.population: Between 200 and 400 frail older adults on the waiting list will be served.
2682.outcome: The nutritional risk of those served will be reduced. This will be measured by their annual nutrition assessment and reassessment.

1025.description: State funds will be dedicated for the design, engineering, reconstruction, and beautification of Palm Beach Road. These improvements will enhance safety and mobility for motorists and pedestrians, upgrade street lighting, reduce flooding, and support economic development opportunities in this area of critical concern.
1025.purpose: State funds will be used to transform the heavily utilized corridor into a safe, attractive, and accessible multimodal roadway that supports economic activity and strengthens community pride.
1025.activities: The activities and services supported by these funds include reconstructing the roadway to enhance traffic safety and mobility, improving drainage to create an effective stormwater management system that reduces accidents, and upgrading signage and pavement markings to increase visibility and overall roadway safety.
1025.direct_services: The direct services will enhance transportation mobility for motorists and pedestrians.
1025.outcome: The expected benefits of this project include safer transportation mobility for motorists and pedestrians, improved street lighting, reduction of flooding issues, and help to promote economic development opportunities in an area of critical economic concern.

1110.description: Phase 1 will retrofit and modernize stormwater infrastructure within Basin D, a 145-acre neighborhood identified as a critical priority in the City’s Stormwater Master Plan. Improvements will reduce chronic flooding, protect homes, businesses, and community facilities, and improve water quality in discharges to Lake Okeechobee, A BMAP area. The project includes regrading swales and canals, replacing culverts and outfalls, and upgrading drainage conveyance systems. The work will improve ADA accessibility, safeguard public safety, and ensure uninterrupted public services in this historically financially disadvantaged municipality that is designated as a Rural Area of Opportunity.
1110.purpose: Goal is to improve quality of life, health, and safety; protection of property and the environment with completion of Basin D Phase 1 critical stormwater conveyance infrastructure that includes collection and transmission systems, canals, swales, culverts, outfalls, and related stormwater conveyance infrastructure that improves the environment and protects State water resources, Lake Okeechobee.
1110.activities: To seek contractual services through the City's procurement policies and regulations for project management, bidding, engineering during construction, on-site construction oversight, and construction of Basin D-Phase 1 stormwater systems. The City invested $409,300 for the design of this critical project.
1110.direct_services: Direct services to citizenry includes improved quality of life, health, safety with improved flood protection, safer transportation, reduced property damage and improved water quality through the modernization of the Basin D stormwater conveyance system. Improved stormwater management prevents pollutants entering ground, and surface waters.
1110.population: Target population includes the State as the project improves water quality protecting State water resources, Lake Okeechobee, the western Glades communities, businesses and visitors, and the general population of Belle Glade, which is a historically disadvantaged municipality that is designated as a Rural Area of Opportunity.
1110.outcome: Benefit is improved stormwater conveyance providing greater measure of water quality treatment & flood attenuation; protection of homes and businesses, instructional and recreational properties in a historically disadvantaged community that is designated as a Rural Area of Opportunity. These improvements will safeguard life, health and safety, preserve property values, provide safer transportation and enhance daily life. Success will be measured through inspections, water quality monitoring, and tracking of flood events.

2855.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2855.description: The project's strategic goal is to transform about 10-15 million pounds of surplus produce in the next 3-5 years into 7-12 million meals. The innovative packaging and dehydration process will extend the meals' shelf life without refrigeration, ensuring a consistent supply of nutrition even during emergency situations or off-season months. Working with Florida's farmers, Feeding Tampa Bay will scale innovative food processing, dehydration, and automated bagging systems to drastically increase the annual supply of high-quality, nutritious meals for food-insecure families across the state.
2855.purpose: The project's strategic goal is to transform surplus produce into vital, long-lasting, healthy food resources for the 10- county region which covers Citrus, Sumter, Hernando, Pasco, Pinellas, Hillsborough, Polk, Manatee, Highlands, and Hardee.
2855.activities: The recipients are those struggling with food-insecurity and lack access to healthy foods. This investment in new technology, particularly dehydration, extends the shelf life of produce for years without refrigeration, ensuring a consistent supply of healthy, nutrient-dense food options year-round. The automated bagging system provides a vital service to partner food pantries by processing produce into the community much faster and by actively rescuing excess and surplus produce, the project sup
2855.direct_services: This project will fund technology and innovation that provides several direct services to the one million deep community Feeding Tampa Bay serves. It primarily centers on increasing the availability and quality of nutritious food resources and improving distribution efficiency. In three to five years, it will process about 10-15 million pounds of surplus produce (7-12 million meals). By processing
2855.population: Feeding Tampa Bay serves one million individuals in our 10-county service area and distributes food and meals to over 400 partner organizations that help us fulfill our mission.
2855.outcome: Meal and Produce Volume: Track the total weight of surplus produce (in pounds) sourced from local farmers and processed by the new equipment versus the previous year's baseline - outlook: process about 10-15 million lbs of surplus produce in the next 3-5 yrs. Operational Efficiency: Measure the reduction in the time (hours/labor-minutes) required to process and bag a standard volume of fresh produce (e.g., one truckload or one massive tote) using the automated system compared to the previous manual labor process Track the time from when fresh produce enters the facility to when it is fully bagged and dispatched to partner pantries. Food Consistency and Partner Feedback: Document the confirme

1131.description: The Town of Cutler Bay seeks $100,000 to support the Cutler Bay Active Adults Services Program. The goal of this project is to assist the Town’s senior citizens in aging in place while enjoying an active lifestyle that will keep them connected with the local community. Funding from the State will be used to reduce social isolation and loneliness among older adults by increasing access to recreation and socialization services. Activities include community outings and regularly scheduled activities (crafting, photography, fitness, games) at the Town's Franjo Park Community Center.
1131.purpose: The goal of this project is to assist the Town’s senior citizens in aging in place while enjoying an active lifestyle that will keep them connected with the local community.
1131.activities: The project has two components: (1) Hosting at least one community outing per month, and (2) providing weekly community based recreation and educational presentations at the Town's Franjo Park Community Center. Center- based recreation may include crafting, exercise, swimming classes (at Cutler Ridge Park and Pool), computer skills/smartphone training, socialization, and educational presentations.
1131.direct_services: The Town's park and recreation staff will provide direct services in the form of coordinating and chaperoning community outings, and facilitating group activities offered at the Franjo Park Community Center and other park facilities. Samples activities include; arts and crafts, group exercise, technology demonstrations (i.e. how to use your smartphone, computer skills, photography), language class
1131.population: The Town will target 100 older adults aged 60+.
1131.outcome: The Project will improve physical/mental health outcomes and overall sense of wellbeing for older adults by creating opportunities to socialize with peers, increasing physical activity through community outings and exercise classes, and maintaining mental stimulation with games and educational activities (computer classes, photography, dominoes, etc). The measurement of success for this project will be for the Town to maintain or INCREASE its offerings to Seniors as evidenced by annual records/schedules of participation

1901.description: As the fastest growing state college in the Florida College System for two years in a row, physical space on campus is at a premium and existing available space has been prioritized for classrooms. By saving a 17,000 sq ft building currently identified for demolition, LSSC is able to renovate and repurpose this facility into a student-focused facility. This project will include renovation of the structure, asbestos abatement, HVAC updates, and improvements that would all the building to be used for student-focused functions.
1901.purpose: The project includes renovation of the structure, asbestos abatement, HVAC updates, and improvements that would allow the building to be used for: student life space for our fast-growing student population, construction of much- needed classroom space, space for our on-campus clubs and organizations, a venue for our emerging E-Sports teams, food service area for students, and office space for student life advisors and the Student Government Association.
1901.activities: These funds will support phase one of this project, bringing Building #6 up to current standards through essential infrastructure improvements: roof replacement, HVAC system upgrades, asbestos abatement, and interior wall removal. Subsequent phases will focus on building out specialized spaces designed to enhance academic programming and student engagement.
1901.direct_services: This renovation will directly serve Florida citizens by transforming our library into a comprehensive student success center. The enhanced facility will provide expanded classroom access and dedicated spaces for student organizations and activities. Our research confirms that engaged students achieve higher grades, persist through completion, and graduate on time, delivering better-prepared gradua
1901.population: The target population is Lake and Sumter Counties. As the fastest growing college in the FCS for two straight years, Lake-Sumter currently serves 11,500 students each year and continues to expand its enrollment to serve additional learners throughout the community.
1901.outcome: We believe that this project will support our improving enrollment and retention rates. We will measure success through our overall success metrics (semester-to-semester persistence, number of engaged students on campus, graduation rates, course pass rates). Additionally, we'll monitor space utilization rates and seek input from students in the Student Government Association. These metrics will demonstrate how invested state dollars directly translate to more Florida citizens earning degrees and entering the workforce prepared.

1439.description: Hurricane Helen caused extensive damage to the football field at Dorsett Stadium. The high winds ripped the newly installed guest bleachers and drug them across the playing surface. This caused deep gouges and ruts throughout the field and tore up the sprinkler system leaving it unsafe. A synthetic turf replacement will not only restore the field to pre storm condition but will also provide long term resiliency against future storms.
1439.purpose: The funds requested will restore and modernized the football field that was severely damaged by Hurricane Helene. It will ensure that students and the community can once again have access to a safe, functional and storm-resilient facility through installation of a durable turf surface.
1439.activities: The project will include the removal of the storm damaged natural grass field and installation of a turf playing surface. This will ensure that the athletic field can support athletic programs, physical education classes, extracurricular events and community activities year-round.
1439.direct_services: The project will provide students, families and community members with a safe and reliable venue for athletic programs, physical education, extracurricular events, and community gatherings. The upgraded turf field will expand opportunities for youth sports, school events and recreational use.
1439.population: The target population is our 997 middle and high school students who participate in athletics, physical education and extracurricular activities. In addition, the XXXX estimated number of local youth leagues and community groups annually.
1439.outcome: The expected outcome is the restoration and modernization of the football field into a safe, storm resilient turf facility. Benefits include reduced maintenance costs, increased facility availability for athletics, physical education and community events year round. Outcomes will be measured by: * Completion of project within the project timeline * Number of athletic events successfully hosted on the new surface * User feedback from students, staff and community groups

2856.description: "Building a Caregiver Community Wellness" initiative supports building renovations and the creation of a central hub for caregiver support. Developed by Share the Care, inc., this initiative is the first of its kind in Central Florida. The initiative will offer coordinated care services, caregiver training, behavioral health resources, mental wellness programs for caregivers, and an adult day health center for care recipients. Preventive and proactive care for both the caregiver and their loved one helps reduce emergency room visits, hospital readmissions, and the need for full-time nursing home care - resulting in significant cost savings for healthcare systems, families, and the veteran support community.
2856.purpose: The "Building a Caregiver Community Wellness" center includes new construction creating a focal point for caregiver support including care coordination, behavioral health services, mental health wellness, and an adult day health center. By enabling caregivers to provide home-based care, these programs can reduce the strain on more expensive healthcare settings, such as hospitals or long-term care facilities, resulting in significant cost savings for healthcare systems, families, and the Veteran
2856.activities: These family-focused services support home-based care for those caring for disabled adults, disabled veterans, people with dementia and Alzheimer’s and more. Services include Care Management, Adult Day Health Care, In-Home Respite Care, Short-Term Overnight Respite Care, Mental Health Counseling, Education, Home Modification and Non- Durable Medical Supplies.
2856.direct_services: The Building a Caregiver Community Wellness Project will be the first of it’s kind in Central Florida, serving as a hub for caregiver health and wellness. Programs will offer training, counseling, and access to necessary caregiver tools and techniques, enabling families to deliver more effective, safer, and higher-quality care.
2856.population: Non-paid family caregivers caring for a loved-one residing in their home. Caregivers include those caring for disabled adults, disabled veterans, people with dementia and Alzheimer’s and more. The majority of caregivers are from Orange and Seminole Counties but programs are open to all interested caregivers living in Central Florida. Virtual programing is open to all caregivers nationwide. In 2024 Share the Care served 2100 families.
2856.outcome: The Building a Caregiver Community Wellness center will help caregivers develop strategies for managing stress and coping with exhaustion. In-person programs will foster a sense of community so caregivers know they are not alone. These resources help caregivers maintain their loved-one at home longer, which is more affordable than institutional care. Respite programs serve 29 persons at the same cost as 1 person in a nursing home. The project will provide learning space for students in the fields of Case Management and Behavioral Health.

1035.organization: From Cradle to College Foundation, Inc.
1035.description: A statewide Preschool Emergency Alert Response Learning System, PEARLS, will provide training, options, and information on current and optional notification to protect Florida's youngest and most vulnerable children. A K-12 public school could be on lock-down due to life-threatening criminal activity such as an active shooter, while a preschool close by remains unaware of the imminent threat. Florida's early education centers are an integral part of our state's educational & economic structure - developing young minds while providing young children a safe environment so parents can work to care for their families and improve their futures. Investing in the security of these young children and their educators is critical based on the current escalation of violence in schools. PEARLS has been successfully providing direct training to our early educators since its inception in 2018, support
1035.purpose: PEARLS provides training for preschool environments to mitigate risk and save lives in emergency situations such as active shooter events. Optional implementation of a local notification system to alert preschools of imminent danger, as is currently done with K-12 schools, closing the existing training and notification gap, working to keep ALL of Florida's children safe. It is essential for these early education locations to use their environments and Proactive Planning to provide the safest env
1035.activities: The essential training will be provided through two methods, both in person training with early childhood educators in their workplace and live on-line trainings for those who cannot attend in person. Participants are provided with resources to assist as they analyze their environments and improve their planning for emergencies, a critical discussion that supports proper preparation for these tragic events. PEARLS will also utilize a Train the Trainer program and leverage collaborative partnersh
1035.direct_services: Training on highly relevant topics including planning and preparing for critical incidents and optional notification systems for schools. This training will be provided through both in-person and on-line formats and both English and Spanish to best serve Florida's citizens.
1035.population: Preschool children and staff - approximately 850,000 individuals in the State of Florida.
1035.outcome: The expected benefit of PEARLS is an increased life-saving awareness of current threatening events and informed choices for action that will mitigate risk and save lives. The program is designed to support preschools and empower them with knowledge and awareness that will prompt them to have a preemptive plan of action which includes multiple options. Planning and preparation make them ready to judiciously implement their plan based on the form of danger present and change the outcome of the event thus enhancing the safety of Florida's youngest children. The program's outcome will be measured by the evaluation forms completed by participants, its successful statewide training and participati

1036.description: The allocation of funds is sought to establish a Soar Lab north of the river in Manatee County to support ALICE (Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed) families with limited access to early learning. The Lab empowers parents to be their child's first literacy teacher, teaching reading strategies, vocabulary, and connecting to resources. Unlike traditional spaces, it engages families with FELDS (Florida Early Learning and Developmental Standards) through play and discovery. This location will ensure equitable access to high-quality learning experiences for underserved communities.
1036.purpose: The allocation of funds is requested to establish a second Soar Lab in Manatee County, north of the river, with the primary objective of providing targeted support to ALICE families who face significant barriers in accessing high-quality early learning opportunities. The lab offers a space for early learners and families to explore literacy, math, science, creativity, and sensory play. It will prepare children for Pre-K and Kindergarten through guided and independent activities with year-round h
1036.activities: The Soar in 4 Lab engages families to ensure classroom readiness and academic success. The Lab has interactive experiences and programming availability on evenings, weekends, and summer, providing accessibility to all families. Children build prekindergarten and kindergarten readiness skills through interactive spaces featuring art, tinkering, engineering, and outdoor discovery areas. Resources for families help support their involvement in early childhood education.
1036.direct_services: The Soar Lab will be a free, hands-on learning space for literacy, math, and science, open to the community. It will foster family engagement and school readiness through immersive environments that build foundational skills. The Lab offers extended hours, including Saturdays. Educators will model literacy-rich play. School district registration assistance will be provided.
1036.population: Soar will focus on vulnerable early learners and their families. The target population served through the Soar in 4 Lab is families with children ages birth through third grade. The lab will serve over 2,500 children and families annually.
1036.outcome: The interactive Lab will be located in an ALICE neighborhood and within walking distance for many families. This initiative will help bridge opportunity gaps by providing all families, especially ALICE families, with engaging educational experiences. The Lab will encourage families to actively engage with FELDS, unlike traditional museums and classrooms. This space will allow children to explore various concepts while scaffolding families to continue learning. Pre- and post surveys will be utilized to measure the outcomes.

2683.description: SR 200/A1A from I-95 to the Port of Fernandina Beach [on Amelia Island] is part of the State's Strategic Intermodal System (SIS). The intersection of CR 107 and SR 200/A1A is the eastern most signalized intersection before reaching Amelia Island, which currently operates at a level of service (LOS) F. FDOT has completed design of the widening along SR 200 at this intersection eastward. Recent study findings include widening CR 107 to add an additional turn lanes to improve operation and the level of service for the intersection to LOS D or better.
2683.purpose: Improve local and regional mobility, improve the overall transportation network in Nassau County and Northeast Florida, and improve Level of Service from F to D or better.
2683.activities: This project will begin right-of-way acquisition needed for the widening of CR107 to improve the intersection operation at CR107 and SR200/A1A which is part of the State of Florida's Strategic Intermodal System.
2683.direct_services: Improve local and regional mobility, improve the overall transportation network in Nassau County and Northeast Florida, and improve Level of Service from F to D or better.
2683.population: Over 45,000 vehicles per day travel through this intersection. Improvements will benefit the general public traveling in this area.
2683.outcome: This project will provide funding for right-of-way acquisition for the widening CR107 to improve the intersection operation at CR107 and SR200/A1A which is part of the State of Florida's Strategic Intermodal System.

1905.description: Provide care coordination for uninsured/underinsured patients high risk utilizers of acute care services including emergency dept, obs and/or inpatient admissions with goal of reducing unnecessary hospital utilization, by linking patients to community services and close care gaps related to social determinants of health. Providing uninsured clinic patients with imaging, lab, medical which allows our providers address care needs.
1905.purpose: Provide care coordination for uninsured/underinsured patients high risk utilizers of acute care services including emergency dept, obs and/or inpatient admissions with goal of reducing unnecessary hospital utilization, by linking patients to community services and close care gaps related to social determinants of health. Providing uninsured clinic patients with imaging, lab, medical which allows our providers address care needs. The most recent Community Health Needs Assessment recognized access
1905.activities: Provide care coordination for uninsured/underinsured patients high risk utilizers of acute care services including emergency dept, obs and/or inpatient admissions with goal of reducing unnecessary hospital utilization, by linking patients to community services and close care gaps related to social determinants of health. Providing uninsured clinic patients with imaging, lab, medical.
1905.direct_services: Provide care coordination for uninsured/underinsured patients high risk utilizers of acute care services including emergency dept, obs and/or inpatient admissions with goal of reducing unnecessary hospital utilization, by linking patients to community services and close care gaps related to social determinants of health. Providing uninsured clinic patients with imaging, lab, medical
1905.population: Uninsured and underinsured patients to include persons with poor mental and physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, homeless, physically disabled, drug users and drug offenders. We expect to serve close to 800 patients.
1905.outcome: Increase in patients establishing themselves at a community clinic, or other community program that meets their care needs. Decrease in ER utilization due to healthcare needs being met at primary care office. Volume of patients served, and Emergency Department Volume Reduction will be methodology to measure.

1906.description: East River High School’s Fire Academy, part of the First Responders Magnet Program, prepares students for careers in firefighting and EMS through certifications, hands-on training, and college credit toward a Fire Science A.S. degree via Valencia College. To enhance its CTE offerings, the school will repurpose a donated ambulance by installing its rear box as a permanent indoor EMS training lab. This space will simulate real-world compartment layouts and support skill development aligned with Florida’s workforce needs.
1906.purpose: The primary goal is to install the ambulance box inside the school to simulate real EMS environments. This will serve as a high-impact training lab for students pursuing careers in firefighting and emergency medical services, enhancing technical readiness and workforce alignment.
1906.activities: The installation enhances experiential learning by integrating real-world EMS layouts into daily instruction. Students gain practical skills in triage, equipment handling, and emergency response, bridging textbook knowledge with field application. Additionally, by immersing students in public service roles, the project fosters civic responsibility and cultural appreciation for first responders. It elevates the visibility and value of emergency services within the school community, cultivating re
1906.direct_services: By producing skilled graduates ready to enter high-demand fields, the project strengthens Florida’s labor market. It reduces training costs for employers and accelerates workforce entry, contributing to local and statewide economic resilience.
1906.population: Students emerge with certifications and field experience that qualify them for immediate employment in EMS, firefighting, and related trades. The program’s partnership with Valencia College further opens pathways to higher education and advanced roles.
1906.outcome: For individual students—many from underserved communities—this training lab offers a direct route to stable, well- paying careers. It empowers them with transferable skills, professional confidence, and economic independence through public service.

2129.description: Created in response to HB 1365 (2024), the Homeless Family Safe Parking Program (HFSP), provides 20 families with a secure, welcoming place to park and sleep in their vehicles overnight. Families will have access to showers, potable water, food, security, sanitation, counseling, and other supportive services offered to help them transition back to stable housing. The HFSP offers an innovative, effective solution to safely serve unsheltered families while permanent housing is identified. This appropriation will start the expansion of the existing program, as the County will continue to fund this program using non-state funds in future years.
2129.purpose: Families will be provided with a safe and secure area to park their vehicles overnight. Wrap around services will be provided to work with the families to move them into housing, including but not limited to case management, housing navigation to find a home, payment of move-in costs and other services to reduce barriers to housing.
2129.activities: In addition to the above, access from 6PM to 8AM daily to shower facilities, security, including a locking mechanism for the site, sanitation and trash pickup, access to potable water, food, and other amenities will be available seven (7) days a week.
2129.direct_services: Housing case management, tutoring, housing navigation, move in rental assistance, referrals to job training and other wrap around services specifically designed to reduce housing barriers.
2129.population: Families residing in their cars who have income to support housing. Estimated to serve 60 individuals (20 families) with the requested funds; 120 individuals (40 families) with the total combined budget.
2129.outcome: The expected outcome is to rapidly house homeless families in safe, affordable and decent housing. The outcome will be measured by a lease or other housing document substantiating permanent or transitional housing was obtained.

2132.description: The City of Oakland Park is seeking funding to transform a vacant lot near the downtown area into a vibrant, green space known as Glenwood Garden. This innovative project is designed to bridge geographic and cultural divisions through environmental sustainability and community engagement. By developing a high-quality green space with nature trails, gardens, and gathering areas, the project will offer residents a natural oasis that promotes physical activity and mental health.
2132.purpose: Like many older communities, Oakland Park’s historical development patterns and infrastructure have created both physical and social divides. Interstate 95 and railroad tracks bisect the City, while cultural and demographic differences, shaped by a legacy of historic discrimination and structural barriers, have contributed to limited shared public spaces. Although diverse communities thrive within Oakland Park, opportunities for meaningful connection across these divides remain limited. To addre
2132.activities: Glenwood Garden will serve as a high-quality, inclusive public space that encourages physical activity, community connection, and environmental stewardship, particularly for low-income families and children. The park will provide: • Safe spaces for walking, active play, and outdoor recreation, supporting healthier lifestyles • Gardening and educational programs that promote environmental awareness and hands-on learning • Cultural and community events that celebrate Oakland Park’s diversity and f
2132.direct_services: No direct services will be provided.
2132.population: The Glenwood Garden site is located within Block Group 3, Census Tract 506.02, a federally designated vulnerable area with a low-to-moderate income (LMI) rate of 68.10%, compared to 57.10% Citywide. This area has limited access to quality green space, making Glenwood Garden a strategic investment to address health disparities and promote equitable access to recreation. Glenwood Garden is meant to provide opportunities for meaningful connection across the divides of the entire City and will serve
2132.outcome: 1) Environmental Enhancement Restores native vegetation and improves air, water, and canopy quality. Measured by: i-Tree/GIS analysis, photo documentation, and soil/water sampling 2) Wildlife Habitat Creation Expands pollinator and bird habitats within the urban core. Measured by: Seasonal species counts and habitat assessments 3) Stormwater Management Improves infiltration and reduces runoff and flooding. Measured by: Infiltration tests, runoff monitoring, and modeling 4) Urban Cooling & Resilience Lowers heat island effects and enhances comfort. Measured by: Temperature monitoring and weather data comparison 5) Economic Revitalization Increases visitation and supports local business growth

1718.description: The proposed Rangeland Boulevard Extension is a critical infrastructure initiative aimed at enhancing regional mobility and local access, safety, emergency response and evacuation operations, and multimodal connectivity in central Pasco County. This project involves the construction of a new 3.4-mile urban roadway segment, designed as a four-to six-lane facility, extending from the current terminus of Rangeland Boulevard to the existing roundabout at Bexley Village Drive, located east of the Suncoast Parkway (SR 589).
1718.purpose: The funds requested will be used to complete the design and post-design services necessary to advance the Rangeland Boulevard Extension project to construction readiness. This includes developing detailed engineering plans, securing environmental permits, coordinating with utility providers, and supporting construction through technical oversight. The ultimate goal is to deliver a shovel-ready infrastructure project that will: - Improve regional mobility by creating a new east-west corridor in c
1718.activities: The design and post-design services will provide a set of Final Plans that will advance the project to construction readiness.
1718.direct_services: The project will provide: improved transportation access and public safety, evacuation route support, multi-modal travel options, and support for economic growth.
1718.population: Pasco County Citizens, over 1,000 citizens are expected to be served.
1718.outcome: This project will improve transportation conditions for commuters and families and will minimize travel times and alleviate traffic congestion. The project will provide contractors, engineers, and consultants immediate job opportunities. By generating direct job opportunities for consultants, contractors, suppliers, service providers, and other professionals, the project will have a positive impact on the local economy.

1063.description: The funds will help to construct Branches Allapattah, a fourth Branches community center, with a total cost of $12 million, at the current site of the Ebenezer United Methodist Church. Branches plans to partner with surrounding schools to initially serve 150 children in Grades K-12 and into postsecondary through its Grow, Climb and Climb Higher programs. Branches expects to scale enrollment to serve 300+ students within 5 years of opening as well as provide our Achieve financial wellness programs to 1,500+ residents.
1063.purpose: The funds will help to construct Branches Allapattah, the 4th Branches community center at the current site of the Ebenezer United Methodist Church at 2001 NW 35th St, Miami FL 33142. Branches plans to partner with surrounding schools to initially serve 150 children in Grades K through 12 and into postsecondary through its Grow, Climb and Climb Higher programs. Branches expects to scale enrollment to serve 300+ students within 5 years of opening as well as provide our Achieve financial wellness
1063.activities: Branches' Grow program serves elementary students through afterschool enrichment, preparing them for lifelong success through enrichment of their minds, bodies and hearts. Branches' Climb program serves middle and high school students by providing youth development services focused on the development of the students' individual assets in order to maximize opportunities for them to become better students and better people. The Climb Higher program provides support to all Branches students current
1063.direct_services: Branches' Grow program serves elementary students through afterschool enrichment, preparing them for lifelong success through enrichment of their minds, bodies and hearts. Branches' Climb program serves middle and high school students by providing youth development services focused on the development of the students' individual assets in order to maximize opportunities for them to become better st

Branches plans to partner with surrounding schools to initially serve 150 children and youth in Grades K through 12 and into postsecondary through its Grow, Climb and Climb Higher programs.
