1063.outcome: Branches partners with families to help them build educational and financial assets. A few outcomes focused on improving quality of education through the Grow and Climb programs are: Elementary students that qualify for Differentiated Literacy Instruction improved reading skills, HS students achieve cumulative GPA of 2.5 to 4.0, Grades 11-12 achieve a Math and Reading score on the SAT of 1000 or above or improve score by 40 points, and Post-Secondary students graduate. Measurements include reviewing iSTEEP Oral Reading Fluency (ORF) or the Maze assessment, report cards, SAT results and proof of completion. A few outcomes focused on improving economic activity through Branches' Micro- Busines

1366.description: Citrus is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) for its psychiatry residency and child and adolescent psychiatry fellowship programs. Psychiatry is recognized as a primary care specialty in Section 409.909 F.S. and is considered a critical shortage area. Citrus’ psychiatry residents and fellows provide much needed primary care and behavioral health services to underserved populations. Because Citrus’ innovative residency and fellowship programs are housed in a Federally Qualified Health Center with ACGME institutional and program accreditation, and not a hospital, Citrus is not eligible for General Appropriations Act Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) funding. The funding requested will cover the costs of salaries and fringe benefits for psychiatry residents and child and adolescent psychiatry fellows and support the continued operation of these innova
1366.purpose: The appropriation will provide funding to cover the costs of salaries and benefits for Citrus Health Network’s psychiatry residents and child and adolescent psychiatry fellows. Psychiatry is recognized as a primary care specialty in Section 409.909 F.S. and is a critical shortage area. Citrus’s psychiatry residents and fellows provide much needed primary care behavioral health services to underserved populations.
1366.activities: Section 409.909 F.S. includes psychiatry among the list of primary care specialties that is experiencing a statewide supply and demand deficit. The requested funds will be used to train residents and fellows in ACGME accredited training programs. Because Citrus’ innovative residency and fellowship programs are housed in a Federally Qualified Health Center with ACGME institutional and program accreditation, and not a hospital, Citrus is not eligible for General Appropriations Act (GAA) Diagnosis
1366.direct_services: Psychiatry residents and child and adolescent psychiatry fellows provide psychological evaluations, medication management, and psychotherapy. Residents and fellows provide services in-person and via telehealth. They also conduct rotations in primary care and hospital settings.
1366.population: Psychiatry residents and child and adolescent psychiatry fellows at Citrus Health Network will be trained in a community setting that specializes in the treatment of the seriously mentally ill and indigent populations, including the homeless, uninsured, and underinsured. Since the inception of the program, psychiatry residents have served thousands of individuals.
1366.outcome: The expected benefit is to improve physical health and mental health based on the number of patients served by psychiatry residents and child and adolescent psychiatry fellows. The outcomes will be measured using information in Citrus' Electronic Health Record.

1159.description: Remediate and restore the City's former incinerator site of approximately 1.76 acres located at the Coral Gables Public Works Compound by removing hazardous materials and rehabilitating the area to serve as a vital regional resource for debris management and trash reclamation to benefit both the City and neighboring municipalities during disaster response and recovery efforts.
1159.purpose: Remediate and restore the City's former incinerator site of approximately 1.76 acres located at the Coral Gables Public Works Compound by removing hazardous materials and rehabilitating the area to serve as a vital regional resource for debris management and trash reclamation to benefit both the City and neighboring municipalities during disaster response and recovery efforts.
1159.activities: Removal, transportation and disposal of approximately 15K CU. YDS. of contaminated soil material from the City's former incinerator site located at the Coral Gables Public Works compound with address 2800 S.W. 72 Avenue, Miami- FL 33155.
1159.direct_services: As part of disaster recovery efforts, approx. 50K residents of the City will appreciate that the site has a potential to stage and achieve volume reduction of green matter collected from a natural disaster.
1159.population: A minimum of approximately 50K residents of the City of Coral Gables.
1159.outcome: Improve the site's environmental conditions by removing soil contaminants as well as enhance the site's groundwater quality and soil conditions.

3546.description: Need to complete Phase 2 Improvements to Farr Field Park, the City's largest outdoor recreational facility that will enhance community recreation, support regional sports tourism. Project addresses old infrastructure, i.e., press box, restrooms, concessions, in field renovation, safety fencing, seating and LED lighting to meet regulatory standards & qualifications. Project supports economic development, improves quality of life, health in this financially disadvantaged municipality that is located in a Rural Area of Opportunity.
3546.purpose: Goal is to improve City owned, largest outdoor recreational facilities, Farr Field Park, and to enhance community recreation, support regional sports tourism, economic development opportunities, improve the quality of life, and health in this Rural Area of Opportunity. Completion of design and improvements to Farr Field Park include addressing old antiquated press box, restrooms, concessions, infield renovation, safety fencing, ADA compliance, and LED lighting to meet regulatory standards & qual
3546.activities: To seek contractual services through the City's procurement policies & procedures for engineering, design, permitting, project management/administration, on-site construction observation, engineering oversight during construction and construction of new park improvements, i.e., press box, restrooms, concessions, infield renovation, safety fencing, ADA compliance, and LED lighting, etc.
3546.direct_services: Direct services include improving the quality-of-life & physical well-being, overall health of the community. Parks provide the potential for economic development, property value increases & enhance community cohesion. Farr Field Park is a dynamic community focal point and the improved recreational spaces, provide safer & modernized facilities & enhanced opportunities for local/regional sports eve
3546.population: Target population includes citizenry, residents, visitors, general public, the business community in this Financially Disadvantaged Municipality (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.), located in Hardee County, which is designated as a Rural Area of Economic Concern/Rural Area of Opportunity (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes) and surrounding communities including sports organizations, tourists, youth, visitors, retirees and residents throughout the State of Florida. Population expected to be served exceeds 25,000.
3546.outcome: Expected benefit is meeting the community's need with improved recreational amenities which improves health, quality of life, and wealth of the community. Farr Field Park is the City's largest recreational park and is a dynamic focal point for the community. The completed improvements provides for a way to promote economic development, attract visitors, increase tourism, which brings in additional revenues, enhances property values, increase of home buyers, and workers. Measurement is certification of the project, community feedback, and tracking of usage

1161.description: This project proposes dredging the Coral Gables Waterway in the section located approximately 100 feet north of the Ponce De Leon Boulevard bridge and 100 feet south of the US-1 bridge. By restoring channel depth and improving water flow, the dredging will restore the waterway's carrying capacity at a choke point, ensure continued boating access and improve the resiliency of the City’s stormwater management system.
1161.purpose: Dredging of waterway to improve surrounding drainage infrastructure. The improvements will also provide relief for a high-traffic corridor and adjacent neighborhoods vulnerable to flooding, ensuring safer conditions for residents, businesses, and commuters.
1161.activities: The requested funds will be used to procure a contractor for the removal of sediment and vegetation from the most critical portions of the Coral Gables Waterway within the City of Coral Gables.
1161.direct_services: The project will reduce the likelihood of flooding within the County and City due to the additional capacity in the waterway. Furthermore, the quality of the water in the waterway and Biscayne Bay will be enhanced by the reduction of nutrients that help support algae blooms. Lastly, the project will allow for the safe passage of recreational, Police and Fire vessels. This improvement will enhance
1161.population: The enhanced stormwater conveyance and reduction in nutrient loading that the project will provide will benefit Miami- Dade County residents and visitors in general. The additional waterway depth that the project will provide will benefit the users of the waterway and adjacent property owners.
1161.outcome: The anticipated benefits are a reduction in the frequency and severity of flooding within the County and City, less frequent algae blooms in the waterway and Biscayne Bay, and less frequent bottoming-out of vessels in the waterway. The frequency of flooding, algae blooms, and vessels bottoming-out can be noted and compared to historical averages.

1062.description: This Program will provide a range of bundled services to help people with disabilities be ready to work with critical skills needed by employers; help them to identify career paths and learn basic financial and other skills to ultimately achieve and sustain economic security and self-sufficiency. The goal of these services is to help individuals obtain and maintain employment, complete career ready post-secondary education and/or increase knowledge of basic financial skills concepts and behaviors. Long-term engagement in services ultimately allows them to earn, keep and grow assets while remaining employed, out of poverty and achieving self-sufficiency.
1062.purpose: Expand access to specialized post-secondary, rapid credential education programs and/or intensive and critically necessary employment supports for adults with disabilities.
1062.activities: Evidenced based “bundled” approach to providing short term post-secondary education leading to career opportunities; financial skills education; career employment counseling; case management and /or workplace supports to help adults with disabilities obtain and maintain employment, complete career ready post-secondary education and/or increase knowledge of financial stability concepts and behaviors. Long-term engagement in services ultimately allows them to earn, keep and grow assets and live fi
1062.direct_services: Short term post-secondary certificate programs; case management supports; basic financial literacy skills education; job/career exploration/counseling and employment development, placement, on the job coaching and follow along.
1062.outcome: Participants will engage in bundled service offerings and achieve one or more of the following outcomes: graduate from a short term, rapid credential post-secondary certificate program, increase financial literacy knowledge, obtain and maintain employment and/or increase access in the community.

1196.description: Monroe County seeks to acquire high-priority vacant, privately owned land in the Florida Keys to support three critical objectives: (1) prevent encroachment on Naval Air Station Key West to preserve national security readiness; (2) reduce legal liability from takings claims related to state-mandated development restrictions on environmentally sensitive lands; and (3) support future affordable housing development in the county with the highest land costs in Florida. By proactively acquiring and managing land, the County will further environmental protection, reduce legal risk, enhance housing access, and provide for military compatibility in one of the state's most vulnerable and strategically important regions. Current state programs are incompatible with these objectives or insufficient to address the demand.
1196.purpose: This project will achieve multiple critical goals, it will: protect the operational integrity of Naval Air Station Key West by preventing incompatible development nearby; reduce Monroe County's legal liability related to land-use restrictions on environmentally sensitive lands; and support the future development of affordable housing by securing land in the county with the highest land costs in Florida. Overall, this effort will strengthen national security, protect natural resources, and improv
1196.activities: Monroe County will carry out the following key activities and services, at our local cost: 1) Identify and Prioritize Parcels: Use planning data and interdepartmental coordination to identify vacant, privately owned parcels that are critical for military buffering, environmental conservation, and future affordable housing. 2) Conduct Due Diligence: Perform appraisals, title work, environmental assessments, and legal reviews to ensure acquisition readiness and compliance. 3) Acquire Strategic Pro
1196.direct_services: The project will directly benefit the public in several key ways: 1) Strengthen base operations; By preventing encroachment on Naval Air Station Key West, the project helps ensure the continued operation of a major employer and national defense asset, supporting regional economic stability. 2) Future Affordable Housing Opportunities: Acquired parcels suitable for residential development will be pr
1196.population: The target population includes: 1) Local Workforce and Residents: Especially low- to moderate-income individuals and families in need of affordable housing in Monroe County, where housing costs are among the highest in the state. 2) Military Personnel and Their Families: By protecting Naval Air Station Key West from encroachment, the project supports the needs of active-duty service members and their dependents. 3) Property Owners Affected by Land-Use Restrictions: Land acquisition will help res
1196.outcome: This project will produce these measurable and lasting outcomes: 1) Increased Land Availability for Affordable Housing: Acquired parcels suitable for development will be reserved for future affordable housing, directly addressing Monroe County's severe housing shortage. 2) Protection of Naval Air Station Key West: Strategic land acquisition will prevent incompatible development near the base, preserving military readiness and economic stability tied to the installation. 3) Environmental Conservation: Environmentally sensitive lands will be permanently protected from development, supporting the Florida Keys’ unique ecosystem and long-term resilience. 4) Reduced Legal and Financial Liability:

2865.description: HIP IMO is an integrated mathematical oncology-centric program that delivers interdisciplinary team science research experiences for high school students ages 16 and older. This unique summer program is designed for motivated aspiring scientists, preparing them for interdisciplinary cancer research careers. These funds will help provide scholarships for the students, technical equipment, and mentor effort coverage.
2865.purpose: HIP IMO is an integrated mathematical oncology-centric program that delivers interdisciplinary team science research experiences for high school students ages 16 and older. This unique summer program is designed for motivated aspiring scientists, preparing them for interdisciplinary cancer research careers. These funds will help provide scholarships for the students, technical equipment, and mentor effort coverage.
2865.activities: The funds will be used to facilitate the program, which offers a unique experience for high school students to engage in cancer research in mathematical oncology.
2865.direct_services: We will provide student enrichment through immersive training sessions in computer programming, cancer biology, and research ethics. We will also provide one-on-one mentoring for each student and provide the unique experience to conduct real cancer research that integrates mathematical oncology, a rising field. Our goal is to prepare the next- generation of interdisciplinary STEAM researchers.
2865.population: At-risk youth and high school students.
2865.outcome: Creates a hub for cutting-edge research, attracting additional funding, clinical trials and collaborations. Digital pathology is critical for analyzing large datasets and enabling advancements in personalized medicine through the development of novel AI and ML algorithms. Increased frequency and accuracy of cancer detection in Floridians; improved resources for cancer treatment

1772.description: The purpose of this project is to establish and rigorously validate the Florida Future-Ready Education (FFRE) Proof of Concept (POC), creating a state model for leveraging Agentic AI to deliver real-time, data-driven interventions at the classroom level. This funding will transform how the education system uses data, shifting from reactive, progress- monitoring to proactive, instant action, thereby securing measurable learning gains.
1772.purpose: The goal of this project is to establish the Florida Future-Ready Education (FFRE) Proof of Concept, creating a state model that leverages Agentic AI to provide real-time, data-driven classroom interventions. The funds will support efforts to transform the use of educational data from reactive progress monitoring to proactive, immediate action, resulting in measurable and sustained improvements in student learning outcomes.
1772.activities: Dedicated data engineering services to design, build, and deploy a secure, cloud-based Education Data Lake/Pipeline. Implementation of robust encryption, access control, and Identity and Access Management (IAM) systems. Develop and iteratively refine the custom Prescriptive Agents. Designing and deploying a simple, intuitive Teacher Dashboard and Student Portal to push real-time interventions.
1772.direct_services: The funding will provide direct services to two key citizen groups: Students and Parents/Guardians within the M-DCPS pilot network. The core benefit is personalized, just-in-time academic support, which has been proven to dramatically accelerate learning while providing parents with unprecedented transparency, immediate access, and tools to effectively support their child's education.
1772.population: Over 800 high school students throughout Miami-Dade County Public Schools are expected to be served.
1772.outcome: The Agentic AI system will reduce the Time to /intervention to an average of less than 48 hours (a 60% or greater reduction), ensuring students receive critical support before small learning gaps become major academic failures. This shift from retrospective review to real-time action is the core quality improvement. The level of benefit will be measured using a Hybrid Evaluation Model combining a quantitative, time-based metric (TTI) with a direct student achievement metric, utilizing a Quasi-Experimental Design (QED).

1451.description: The City of Midway requests funds to upgrade certain fire equipment. The requested equipment will replace all gas- powered equipment on all fire trucks. Not only will this become more cost effective but will also be safer to operate and less harmful fumes. This equipment will also operate even during disasters, such as hurricanes, when fuel shortages could be a possibility. These tools, some of which are commonly known as the "Jaws of Life" will drastically increase Midway Fire's highway rescue capabilities as well as provide equipment helpful during structure fires and structural collapse.
1451.purpose: To have the ability to respond to a variety of large and small emergencies with proper equipment will more efficiently serve the local citizens and the surrounding communities.
1451.direct_services: Ensuring rapid, well-equipped emergency response is critical to public safety. Upgrading to advanced rescue equipment will enhance response times, efficiency, and firefighter capabilities, directly improving the City's and County's ISO rating, strengthening fire protection, and increasing community safety.
1451.population: Approximately 46,000 citizens of Gadsden County. Additionally, we are responsible for about 20 mile of I-10.
1451.outcome: Protection of life and rapid response times. Outcomes will be measured by the number of calls reported to the State and the annual ISO evaluation.

A wet detention facility with a bypass weir in the main drainage channel will be used to direct the water. After treatment, water will be discharged back into an existing canal at a controlled rate. Ancillary improvements would include regrading the roadside, swales and ditches, upsizing of cross drain culverts, pond siting, pond construction and acquiring easements for access.
2445.purpose: Design and construction of the new storm system that will divert Black Branch into a pond for detention and treatment. A wet detention facility with a bypass weir in the main drainage channel will be used to direct the water. After treatment, water would be discharged back into existing canal at a controlled rate. Ancillary improvements would include regrading the roadside, swales and ditches, upsizing of cross drain culverts, pond siting, pond construction and acquiring easements for access.
2445.activities: Construction of the new system that will divert water away from Black Branch North. A wet detention facility with a bypass weir will be used to redirect the water. Improvements include re-grading of roadside swales and ditches, upsizing of cross drain culverts, pond siting and property acquisition, and acquiring easements to access drainage facilities for maintenance.

1456.organization: Gulf County Board of County Commissioners
1456.description: Gulf County Board of County Commissioners is requesting funding to establish a Regional Firefighting Training Facility designed to serve local fire departments, emergency responders, and mutual aid partners across the region. This facility will provide hands-on training to improve firefighter safety, readiness, and response capabilities. By centralizing training in Gulf County, the program will reduce travel costs for rural departments, standardizes training quality, and enhances regional emergency preparedness.
1456.purpose: Currently, Gulf County's firefighters must travel significant distances-often out of the county- for essential training, which limits opportunities and coordinated response practice. Smaller volunteer departments in fiscally constrained counties are especially disadvantaged. This local facility will help create a dedicated training site that allows for hands on training for the region. By centralizing training in Gulf County, the program will reduce travel costs for rural departments, standardiz
1456.activities: This facility will be dedicated exclusively to the training and certification of volunteer firefighters, beginning with a targeted recruitment and training program for high school seniors in partnership with the Gulf County School Board. Additionally, all nine Gulf County volunteer fire departments will also be able to train new recruits and hold necessary training exercises at the new facility.
1456.direct_services: The establishment of the Gulf County Regional Firefighter Training Facility represents a transformative opportunity to meet a pressing community need with long-term benefits for public safety, youth development, and regional resilience.
1456.population: The entire population of Gulf County will benefit from this training facility as more trained firefighter will benefit the County as a whole. The initial high school program will serve as a model for expansion into neighboring counties, with the long-term goal of creating a regional training hub for the tri-county area.

1338.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1338.description: These funds will provide the resources necessary to finalize research projects focusing on developing modernized, science-based fertilizer (nutrient) application rates. Determining the precise amounts of fertilizer needed for each crop reduces environmental footprints, boosts yields, and cuts production costs.
1338.purpose: Complete multi-year field research to update outdated fertilizer application rates across a range of food crops to equip agricultural producers with the resources needed to provide nutrition to their crops with precision and accuracy reducing environmental footprints, boosts yields, and cuts production costs.
1338.activities: Conduct research on fertilizer application including traditional academic research plots, working with growers in on- farm trials, and compilation of all available public data sources regarding nutrient applications. Develop database that can be continually updated.
1338.direct_services: Reduced impact to water quality, quantity, and the environment.
1338.population: Agricultural producers and the population through more efficient use of nutrients applied to crops as well as a reduction in environmental impacts.
1338.outcome: More efficient food production, better crop yields, and reduction in production costs. Education in the latest technologies in precision agriculture and up to date nutrient management. Also, reduced impact to water quality, quantity, and the environment through more efficient use of fertilizer. The measure will be determined by the economic impact to the agriculture industry as well water quality improvement.

Without funding, the Village would be forced to shift from proactive engagement to reactive services, relying more heavily on emergency aid, food programs, and mental health interventions.
