1141.purpose: The requested funds will support the Village’s senior program to improve quality of life for adults aged 60 and older by offering recreational, social, and educational activities and by providing support services and resources, including direct assistance for those with physical and cognitive impairments.
1141.activities: Funds will be used to deliver a range of recreational, social, and educational activities and to provide supportive services and resources that address the needs of older residents; programming will include activities that promote engagement, skill-building, and social connection, along with hands-on assistance for seniors facing mobility or cognitive challenges.
1141.direct_services: Citizens will receive direct, on-island services such as group recreational and educational programs, social engagement opportunities, and targeted support services—explicitly including direct assistance for seniors with physical and cognitive impairments—so that older adults can remain active, safe, and connected in their community.
1141.population: The project targets Village residents aged 60 and older; seniors make up over 20% of the Village population, and the program is designed to serve this concentrated older-adult community.
1141.outcome: Expected benefits include improved safety, increased physical and social activity, better mental and physical health outcomes, and reduced reliance on emergency and reactive services. Outcomes can be tracked through measures such as participant feedback and satisfaction, records of program participation, documentation of support services delivered, and comparisons over time of service utilization.

1461.description: A program of the Florida Dental Association Foundation, Florida Mission of Mercy (FLA-MOM) is the largest charitable dental clinic in the state. FLA-MOM is a large-scale, two-day, professional dental clinic that provides free care to patients, with the goal of serving the underserved and under-insured in Florida. Since 2014, FLA-MOM has provided $19.1 million in donated care to more than 17,000 patients with the help of more than 16,000 volunteers. FLA-MOM is held in a different Florida region each year. The 2027 FLA-MOM has a goal of treating of 2,000 patients in Leon County and surrounding areas in the Big Bend.
1461.purpose: A program of the Florida Dental Association Foundation, Florida Mission of Mercy (FLA-MOM) is the largest statewide charitable dental clinic in Florida. FLA-MOM is a large-scale, two-day, professional dental clinic that provides free care to patients, with the goal of serving the underserved and underinsured. Since 2014, FLA-MOM has provided $19.1 million in donated care to more than 17,000 patients. This public health dental program provides attainable dental care for vulnerable populations in
1461.activities: Services provided at FLA-MOM include oral health education, oral cancer & other health screenings, dental exams, cleanings, fillings, extractions, root canals, pediatric dental treatments, X-rays, and dentures and partials. Our program also connects patients with options for a dental home by providing a resource guide of local community dental programs and clinics.
1461.direct_services: Oral health education, oral cancer screenings, medical history review & blood pressure screening, panoramic X-ray, and dental exam by a licensed dentist. Dental treatments: extractions, restorations, cleanings, sealants, fluoride, root canals, partial or full dentures. All patients will receive a resource guide with the area's available dental services and dental home care products.
1461.population: The target population for FLA-MOM are those who are uninsured, elderly persons, persons with poor health, veterans, unemployed, economically disadvantaged persons, homeless, and school-aged children. 2000 patients are expected to be served.
1461.outcome: To relieve pain and infection, provide oral prosthetics for patients who are missing teeth, reduce the number of dental- related emergency department visits in Leon County and surrounding counties, provide patients with options for a dental home to receive preventive care. Patient demographic data will be tracked using event software developed specifically for FLA-MOM. Additionally, the collection/analysis of FLA-MOM Impact Study questionnaires will be used to determine the overall health and dental needs specific to Leon County and surrounding counties.

1092.description: An update and enhancement of the treatment plants dewatering process and equipment is necessary to become more resilient. A dryer sludge equates to less tons being hauled to the mainland and therefore fewer tons placed in landfills taking up valuable space and capacity for other waste needs. A firmer cake can also be favorable for future processes being explored by the City such as Pyrolysis that could reduce even further the tons being hauled to the mainland.
1092.purpose: A specific goal that funding could enhance is dryer, pressed, dewatered sludge. Dryer sludge requires less tonnages hauled off the island and delivered to the mainland.
1092.activities: Funds will be allocated to an awarded contractor to perform system enhancements within the City's Waste Water Treatment Plant .
1092.direct_services: When the Waste Water Treatment Plant is generating a dryer waste sludge, the hauling costs may lower thus providing savings to the rate payers.
1092.population: City of Key West System Rate Payers. 12,808 account holders (29,458) will be served.
1092.outcome: An expected and anticipated benefit should lead to less trucks on US 1 making a safer highway. A measure to be considered is a simple moisture test that will depict a dryer material.

1639.description: The Osceola Council on Aging Senior Connected Care program provides home and community-based services to senior citizens living in Osceola County. By expanding our adult day care, home delivered meals and home cleaning and repair services, many seniors in our community on waitlists can be serviced by much needed support to allow them to continue to remain living at home with dignity. Osceola Council on Aging prioritizes serving seniors who are homebound, socially isolated, and individuals with memory care needs who have over burdened caregivers.
1639.purpose: The Osceola Council on Aging Senior Connected Care program provides home and community-based services to senior citizens living in Osceola County. By expanding our adult day care, home delivered meals and home repair and cleaning services, many seniors in our community on waitlists can receive the much needed support to allow them to continue to remain living at home with independence and dignity.
1639.activities: Eligible homebound seniors residing in Osceola County will receive Adult daycare, home delivered meals, and home cleaning and repairs, as assessed, as needed. This includes social interaction with volunteers and staff.
1639.direct_services: Eligible low-income and disadvantaged seniors aged 60 and older who are homebound seniors residing in Osceola County will receive Adult daycare, home repair or home delivered meals, as assessed, as needed. They will also receive social interaction with volunteers and staff.
1639.population: Low-income and disadvantaged seniors age 60 and older who are homebound with overburdened caregivers, limited to no access to nutritious meals, and limited ability or access to needed home repairs or cleaning to ensure a safe living environment.
1639.outcome: Homebound individuals with memory care needs can get much needed socialization in a safe environment at the adult day health care center. Homebound seniors with very limited ability to cook meals can have access to nutritious meals and a wellness check to reduce social isolation and hospitalizations, and seniors without access to heavy cleaning, yard work, and home repairs can get the needed services. The outcomes will be measured by utilizing standardized Department of Elder Affairs assessment metrics and satisfaction surveys.

1594.organization: Osceola County Council on Aging, Inc.
1594.description: The requested funds will be utilized to provide over 40,000 meals to over 75 seniors residing in rural sections of Osceola County who are on the Meals on Wheels program wait-list. The Osceola Council on Aging Home Delivered Meals program prioritizes homebound seniors with limited or no access to meals, to help prevent their risk of malnutrition and social isolation. The need for home delivered meals for homebound seniors at risk is greater than the current level of funding.
1594.purpose: The requested funds will be utilized to provide over 40,000 meals to over 75 seniors residing in rural areas of Osceola County who are on the Meals on Wheels program wait-list. The Osceola Council on Aging Home Delivered Meals program prioritizes homebound seniors with limited or no access to nutritious meals, to help prevent their risk of malnutrition and social isolation.
1594.activities: Trained caring volunteers and staff members will provide in-person delivery of nutritious meals. All meals are planned by a registered dietitian to ensure a balanced meal that meets the state and federal guidelines for seniors, and the in- person delivery provides a much needed social connection to each senior.
1594.direct_services: Nutritious meals will be provided to homebound seniors by trained volunteers and staff, who will also provide social interaction and check on each senior's well-being during each meal delivery.
1594.population: Low-income and disadvantaged seniors age 60 and older who are homebound with limited access to nutritious meals. The goal is to serve at least 75 seniors continuously throughout the fiscal year.
1594.outcome: Delivering healthy balanced meals in-person to homebound seniors will reduce the risk of malnutrition, improve quality of health and provide much needed socialization to support independent living in the community. The outcome will be measured by utilizing standardized Department of Elder Affairs assessment metrics, number of meals delivered, and program enrollment duration.

2563.organization: Historic St. Johns Police Athletic League
2563.description: Diamond of Dreams is a stand-alone project of the Historic St. Johns County Police Athletic League organization that will provide an all-inclusive, accessible playground and adaptive multipurpose baseball field designed specifically for children with special needs, their families, and the community. Despite 17% of the PreK-12th grade student population being identified as having special needs, only one ADA-compliant baseball field and playground combination exists in our county which expands 601 square miles. The location of Diamond of Dreams targets the majority of our population at or below the poverty line. This project specifically invests in the well-being of families often excluded due to disability, socioeconomic status, or lack of access to inclusive recreational opportunities.
2563.purpose: The goal of Diamond of Dreams is to create an inclusive and supportive environment where children with special needs, along with their families, can play, socialize, and participate in sports activities that are tailored to their unique abilities. By fostering a safe and adaptive space, we aim to provide every child with the opportunity to experience the joy of being a part of a real sports team. From the adaptive baseball field to the specially designed playground, this project promotes physica
2563.activities: The primary purpose of these funds will be used to construct the specially designed playground, adaptive baseball field, and the inclement weather building. This project will remove barriers to recreation, provide opportunities for inclusive programs and events, and provide year-round outdoor activities for children with and without disabilities.
2563.direct_services: Diamond of Dreams project offers organized sports activities on an adaptive multipurpose baseball field, along with a specially designed playground for the special needs community in St. Johns County. The Diamond of Dreams playground and ballfield will meet the physical, sensory, and social needs of children with disabilities.
2563.population: According to the 2020 Department of Education report, 17% of the PreK-12th grade student populations have special needs. This does not account for the children younger than PreK or attending specialized schools. The project is situated in the portion of the county with the highest concentration of residents living below the poverty line. Without the targeted investment, many families will continue to face barriers that limit their children's ability to participate fully in community play. We exp
2563.outcome: The benefit this project will provide to the special needs community in St. Johns County is invaluable. The goal of Diamond of Dreams is to level the playing field for the special needs community and provide these incredible individuals with the opportunity to play with their friends, siblings, and family members in a safe space that meets their needs. The Diamond of Dreams adaptive baseball field will provide children with disabilities the opportunity to be a part of a team, wear a uniform, with a live crowd cheering them on. The social, emotional, physical, and developmental benefits are immeasurable.

2564.description: HorsePlay Therapy Center is a local 501(c)3 non-profit that provides physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy to children with special needs using hippotherapy and mental health services to veterans suffering with PTSD. HorsePlay currently leases an 11 acre property and have reached max capacity. Funds will be used to construct a new, larger facility in St Johns County that will provide 35,000 treatment sessions annually to children with special needs and veterans with PTSD. This project aligns with SB 112, which was passed last year, and Senate Leadership's goals related to autism and neuro-development.
2564.purpose: HorsePlay Therapy Center is a local 501(c)3 non-profit that provides physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy to children with special needs using hippotherapy and mental health services to veterans suffering with PTSD using equine-assisted therapy. HorsePlay currently leases an 11 acre property and have reached max capacity. Funds will be used to construct a new, larger facility in St Johns County that will provide 35,000 treatment sessions annually to children with special ne
2564.activities: In 2024, we provided nearly 12,000 treatment sessions. There are currently 140 individuals on our wait-list whom have not received services yet due to maxing out our current operational space. Upon completion of the facility, we will be able to provide 35,000 treatment sessions annually.
2564.direct_services: We specialize in serving children with special needs and veterans with PTSD. HorsePlay is staffed by licensed physical, occupational, speech, and mental health therapists, as well as trained volunteers. We provide a comprehensive medical model of hippotherapy for children and mental health therapy utilizing horses for veterans. NO CLIENT IS DENIED USING HORSES IN THEIR TREATMENT DUE TO FINANCES.
2564.population: We provide children with special needs under the age of 18 with physical, occupational, and speech therapy services. Additionally, in our RiseUp for Veterans program, we serve veterans with post traumatic stress disorder and other mental health illnesses. In 2024, we provided 11,224 treatment sessions for children and 551 treatment sessions with veterans. We currently have a waitlist of 140 individuals. We expect to be able to provide 35,000 treatment sessions annually upon the completion of the
2564.outcome: Our services are provided by licensed and skilled Speech-Language Pathologists, Occupational Therapists, Physical Therapists and mental health therapists as a health care service. Personalized treatment plans are crafted with individualized goals based on the child or veteran’s needs. Goals are measured at each treatment visit and formal evaluations with standardized assessments every 6 and 12 months. Additionally, impact surveys are provided once annually for families to report on their experience with HorsePlay Therapy Center

1095.description: The requested funds will enable the construction of a vital reverse osmosis facility on Crawl Key, Marathon, FL. This facility serves a dual purpose; first, it acts as a crucial backup water source during emergencies, safeguarding against disruptions causes by disasters or damaged transmission lines. Secondly, it addresses the pressing need for additional water supply due to population growth and restrictions on Biscayne aquifer withdrawals.
1095.purpose: The requested funds will directly support the establishment of a reverse osmosis facility on Crawl Key, Marathon, FL. This critical infrastructure will provide a reliable and secure water source, ensuring uninterrupted service to citizens during emergencies and times of increased demand due to population growth and aquifer limitations.
1095.activities: The funding will be used to design, bid, permit, and construct a new reverse osmosis facility to provide uninterrupted access to safe and reliable drinking water during emergencies and periods of heightened demand. This facility acts as a crucial lifeline in times of need, enhancing overall community resilience.
1095.direct_services: The funding will enable the operation of a new reverse osmosis facility, ensuring citizens have uninterrupted access to safe and reliable drinking water during emergencies and periods of heightened demand. This facility acts as a crucial lifeline in times of need, enhancing overall community resilience.
1095.population: Residents and visitors to the Florida Keys will all benefit from this project.
1095.outcome: Provision of a reliable and secure water source to provide uninterrupted service to visitors and residents during emergencies and increased demand.

2571.description: Construction of a 40,623 GSF facility in Daytona Beach to house certificate and AS degree programs in Aviation Airframe and Powerplant Mechanics. Trains students in FAA-approved program that fills a huge demand for aircraft mechanics. In partnership with Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, students will be able to articulate to the BS in Aviation Maintenance or go directly to work. Partially funded by Legislature in 2024-25.
2571.purpose: Construction of new facility located in Daytona Beach to house certificate and AS programs in FAA-approved Aviation Airframe and Powerplant Maintenance programs; train individuals for high-demand, high-wage jobs in the service area. Meets needs of local employers now showing 11% growth in aviation maintenance jobs the region.
2571.activities: Training programs in Aviation Airframe and Powerplant Mechanics will prepare students to enter the high-demand field of aircraft maintenance. Programs will include two college-credit certificates and an associate of science degree. Students will be able to articulate seamlessly into Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University's BS in Aviation Maintenance Science or go directly to work.
2571.direct_services: Educated workers who graduate ready to work in high demand, high paying jobs in the aviation and manufacturing industries, including those on the Space Coast. The program will continue to bring new businesses to the region and state. Job demand shows 11% growth in our region over the next eight years.
2571.population: The Airframe and Powerplant programs will provide high-demand, high-wage job opportunities to up to 400 students and will act as a component of Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University's BS in Aviation Maintenance. Student can go directly to work after earning the certificate or AS degree or can proceed to the BS program at ERAU. Average wage is approximately $30/hour.
2571.outcome: The benefit will be graduates in the high demand, high paying field of aviation mechanics. Enrollment and graduation rates are measured for all of DSC's programs.

1243.description: Funds are needed for an interdisciplinary team of scientists who can leverage advanced gene-editing technologies to address the need for rapid development and commercialization of genetically improved crops for food production. This technology introduces desirable traits such as disease and pest resistance, improved nutrition, and enhanced climate tolerance.
1243.purpose: Scientists will develop food crops that are more resistant to disease and pest, with improved nutrition, and enhanced climate tolerance—more quickly and precisely than traditional methods. They will also develop plants with greater yield, quality, nutritional content, flavor, and shelf life.
1243.activities: A multi-disciplined team of scientists to much more effectively employ biotechnology tools to increase the speed and accuracy of plant breeding.
1243.direct_services: This technology is being used to enhance crop resilience to pest, diseases, and environmental stress. It can be used to improve yield and quality, as well as nutritional content, flavor, and shelf life in food crops.
1243.outcome: Enhanced crop resilience to pests and diseases will reduce the need for chemicals, reducing stress to the environment and decreasing the cost of food production. Consumers will benefit from improved quality, nutritional content, flavor, and shelf life of food products.

1323.description: This project will improve the City of Maitland's Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system--a digital network used by its water and wastewater utilities to enhance analysis, security, and automation--leading to safer and more efficient operations benefiting the public.
1323.purpose: SCADA upgrades will improve security, service reliability, efficiency, and remote monitoring of critical public water and wastewater infrastructure. This will address the growing threat of cyber attacks by modernizing network equipment and communication systems with advanced authentication, encryption, and monitoring capabilities. It will also improve the city's ability to respond to system anomalies and service disruptions.
1323.activities: City information technology and utility staff will work with consultants to direct the planning, implementation, and ongoing monitoring of the upgraded SCADA system.
1323.direct_services: SCADA system enhancements will result in improved service, safer water and wastewater systems, and better response to cyber and on-premises attacks or intrusions.
1323.population: All 20,000 city residents and all businesses will benefit from the enhanced SCADA upgrades through the protection of public water and wastewater systems. Maitland's 3 potable water plants serve 14,000 customers with expected growth to 20,000 customers by 2038. Wastewater includes 42 lift stations and 65 miles of pipeline that transport 1.3 million gallons per day (about half maximum capacity).
1323.outcome: The benefits of this project are that the SCADA system enhancements will result in improved service, safer water and wastewater systems, and better response to cyber and on-premises attacks or intrusions. Outcomes will be measured with regular reporting, penetration testing, documentation of attempted system or facility attacks, and speed at which investigations or corrections are made.

2873.description: The Program Support Offices are an essential component of Phoenix House Florida’s broader initiative at 1800 Orient Road in Tampa, FL. This initiative establishes a step-down substance use treatment center for justice-involved individuals, providing an effective alternative to traditional incarceration. With construction of the treatment center nearly completed, the requested funds will equip and furnish the dedicated Program Support Offices to ensure smooth and efficient operations. These offices will accommodate human resources, staff training and development, and a centralized call center for timely pre-screening and admissions. By consolidating these critical functions, the Program Support Offices enhance operational efficiency, strengthen staff preparedness, and ensure seamless client transitions into care. Ultimately, the project delivers a cost-effective solution that promotes com
2873.purpose: The requested funds will cover startup costs for the Administrative Support Offices at 1800 Orient Road, completing Hillsborough County’s $5 million investment in the facility. These offices will house human resources, staff training, and a centralized call center for admissions and pre-screening, all of which are vital to operating the step-down and substance use treatment services. This funding ensures the facility can open on schedule and efficiently serve more than 340 justice-involved indiv
2873.activities: The funds will be used to complete the build-out and setup of the Support Offices so they can function as the operational hub for the 1800 Orient Road project. Activities supported include construction work, installation of IT and security systems, and preparing the space with appliances, signage, and relocated furnishings. These efforts will make the offices fully functional, allowing staff to carry out essential administrative duties that support the step-down and substance use treatment servi
2873.direct_services: The appropriation will fund the startup of the Support Offices, which directly support citizens by making the 1800 Orient Road step-down and substance use treatment center fully operational. Through these offices, individuals will be pre-screened and admitted into care, staff will be trained to deliver high-quality services, and secure systems will be in place to ensure safe and efficient operatio
2873.population: The target population for this project is justice-involved individuals in Hillsborough County who are referred to treatment either as a court-ordered alternative to incarceration or as a step-down from incarceration. These individuals often have substance use disorders or co-occurring mental health conditions and require structured treatment and step-down services to successfully reintegrate into the community. Approximately 150 people will be served per year, for a total of thousands served for
2873.outcome: By establishing the Support Offices, the project ensures that admissions, pre-screening, staff training, and administrative oversight are in place to support high-quality care. Outcomes will include expanded access to treatment, reduced recidivism, and improved reintegration into the community. These will be measured by tracking admissions, treatment completion rates, and re-arrest data within 3–12 months of discharge, along with progress in housing, employment, and stability reported through case management and follow-up surveys.

2143.description: Palm Beach State College (PBSC) is proud to offer a comprehensive suite of construction-related programs to meet the growing demand for skilled labor in Palm Beach County. These programs are part of our vision to create expanded vocational offerings, providing students, contractors, and the community with a state-of-the-art learning environment that fosters collaboration, innovation and workforce development. In doing so, PBSC seeks to create additional classroom space by either renovating existing classrooms or building additional classroom space to meet the needs of our students.
2143.purpose: The Construction Trades Innovation Center at PBSC will be a hub for innovation and collaboration between students, industry professionals, and community stakeholders. Students will benefit from hands-on learning opportunities and internships, preparing them for immediate workforce entry. Local contractors will have access to a pipeline of highly trained graduates ready to fill critical roles in their companies. The community will benefit from increased economic development and enhanced infrastru
2143.activities: PBSC continues to provide its established Building Construction Technology A.S. Degree, Building Construction Specialist CCC, and certificate programs in HVAC & R, Welding, Electrician, and Low Voltage Integration. We also offer robust apprenticeship programs in electricity and HVAC & Refrigeration. To expand our offerings further, PBSC will introduce a clock-hour carpentry program, a plumbing certificate program, and a new plumbing apprenticeship. We have an ATD in progress with the DOE current
2143.direct_services: An expansion of training services to the Palm Beach County residents, benefiting the population at large.
2143.population: High school students, college students, unemployed and those already employed seeking to upskill to the trades. We anticipate serving upwards of thousands of students going forward in expanding our programs in Lake Worth as well as in Palm Beach Gardens.
2143.outcome: We seek to train the next generation of tradespeople to supply our community and state with a talent pipeline to fill worker shortages and address the labor market demand.

2182.description: This project will mitigate and reduce localized flooding and standing rainwater, enhance protection of residential homes from flood events, increase drainage capacity, reducing the probability of mosquito-transmitted diseases to the public, and protecting of private property and life in Miami Lakes' residential neighborhoods. This is through design, permitting, and construction of new catch basins, manholes, drainage pipes, exfiltration trenches (French drains), milling and resurfacing of roadway, and signing and pavement markings.
2182.purpose: The specific goal is to construct the project for the purpose of mitigating and reducing localized flooding and standing rainwater, enhancing protection of residential homes from flood events, increasing drainage capacity, reducing the probability of mosquito-transmitted diseases to the public, and protecting of private property and life in Miami Lakes' residential neighborhoods
2182.activities: Permit and construction of a new drainage system including new catch basins, manholes, drainage pipes, exfiltration trenches (French drains), milling and resurfacing of roadway, and signing and pavement markings.
2182.direct_services: The direct service will be increased drainage capacity and reduced street flooding in the drainage basin which will lessen impact to property and protect access to over 570 residential homes and a local K-8 school.
2182.population: The target population is the surrounding residential community; this road serves as a north south connector and one of only two access roads to the community and a local elementary school. Increased drainage capacity in this area would directly benefit a local K-8 School and over 570 properties which is estimated to be approximately 1700 individuals
2182.outcome: Expected benefits include improved drainage, reduced localized flooding, increased drainage capacity, improved stormwater management, eliminated standing rainwater, reduced probability of mosquito-transmitted diseases to the public, reduced impact to property and life, enhanced environmental protection to the general public, improved transportation conditions, and improved groundwater and surface water quality. Outcome will be measured by field inspection and documentation of rainfall events. Project will create specific contractor, engineer, environmental, and consultant immediate job opportunities in stormwater and construction management measured by contractual agreements.

3532.description: Construction completion of the new Florida Wildlife Interactive Education Center (FWIEC) to include costs relating to the sitework, hardscaping, landscaping, associated infrastructure, parking, lighting, buildings, and ancillary structures. Also includes costs for highly interactive educational & advanced technology elements, artistic elements and artistic installation, start-up, and furniture, fixtures & equipment throughout the FWIEC. The FWIEC will be dedicated to educating residents from all of Florida, and of all ages, on the Florida Wildlife Corridor, & Florida's legacy of preservation, agriculture, ranching, and farming.
3532.purpose: The FWIEC will be dedicated to interactively educating residents from all of Florida, and of all ages, on the Florida Wildlife Corridor & Florida's history of preservation, agriculture, ranching and farming as well as to promote sustainable practices and economic growth in the region.
3532.activities: Will enrich cultural experience; Improve agricultural production/promotion/education; Improve quality of education. Community hub involving residents and visitors, offering workshops and training on sustainable farming practices showcasing different agricultural techniques & technologies. Will incorporate interactive and hands-on learning experiences from a multidisciplinary approach using technology integration, create outdoor classrooms and outdoor adventure activities, environmental clubs, ne
3532.direct_services: Organized events, festivals, workshops, presentations that showcase cultural celebrations and traditions, incorporating environmental themes. Create local partnerships to create joint exhibits to explore the interplay of culture and environment. Educational Programs tailored to school, locals, and visitors promoting Organic Farming practices, composting, drip irrigation, native planting, permacult
3532.population: The residents of Florida, Southwest Florida, and all visitors to Florida. Target population exceeds 800.
3532.outcome: Increase or improve economic activity, Increase tourism, create specific immediate job opportunities; enhance/preserve/improve environmental or fish and wildlife quality. The FWIEC will be actively involved in the preservation of critical ecosystems, endangered species, and mobilizing support for policies and initiatives that protect the environment. Encourage conservation efforts and promote responsible stewardship of natural resources. Will hire people from different ages encouraging our local community to participate. Encourage volunteer programs, intern and outreach programs. Requires additional staff for admin and all services.

1258.description: This project will provide the resources to expand education and training for Florida Civil Air Patrol volunteers in order to increase their proficiency, preparedness and knowledge so they can respond to, and effectively complete, all assigned tasks and missions as requested by all state agencies in support of the citizens of Florida by increasing the number of qualified (in all Emergency Services specialties) volunteers as well as provide the educational foundation for our youth (CAP cadets) in aerospace education, which includes STEM, flight training, leadership, and physical fitness. This project will also provide for the acquisition of needed equipment to support training and to complete assigned missions.
1258.purpose: Increase the number of qualified and proficient volunteer members (in all specialties) in order to successfully complete all assigned missions state-wide in support of the citizens of Florida. This includes senior and cadet members.
1258.activities: Education and training in all emergency services specialties for volunteer members (seniors and cadets) to qualify and to maintain proficiency in order to successfully complete all assigned missions in support of the citizens of Florida.
1258.direct_services: Emergency response by providing search and rescue (air and ground), pre and post emergency assessments and tracking. Post disaster support and recovery services (essential supplies-food, water, blood, etc.). Education and training for all volunteer citizens (Including cadets -middle and high schoolers) required to successfully work assigned missions.
1258.population: All citizens of the State of Florida that are impacted by emergencies including natural disasters.
1258.outcome: Florida Wing CAP will be prepared to expand the number of missions assigned and successfully completed by increasing the number of volunteers that are qualified and proficient to execute assigned emergency response missions and tasks. The number of qualified (all specialties) volunteer members available will be compared to the number from the previous year.

2579.description: In addition to serving Flagler's 2300 students through the Classical CORE program, the Institute provides a statewide P.D. Program for K-12 classical teachers through seminars, workshops, & courses for K-12 Classical school teachers. The institute is doubling the number of teachers served each year in our summer conference and has partnered with the FLDOE to develop classical teacher certification modules. The funds requested will serve the explosive growth in demand for these services.
2579.purpose: The Institute provides a statewide P.D. Program for K-12 classical teachers. Leveraging the learning resources of Flagler, it provides seminars, workshops, & courses for K-12 Classical school teachers. The institute is doubling the number of teachers served each year in our summer conference and has partnered with the FLDOE to develop classical teacher certification modules. The funds requested will serve the explosive growth in demand for these services.
2579.activities: Full-time faculty trained in the classical model of education. K12 Classical teachers statewide receive professional development through summer trainings, workshops, and Saturday seminars. K-12 classical summer camps for scholars and public lectures.
2579.direct_services: Full-time faculty teaching First Year Seminar course students. The development of a higher ed retention model based on the classical model of education. Workshops, conferences, public lectures, and guest scholars for K-12 teachers statewide. In partnership with the FLDOE, the creation and delivery of classical teacher certification courses.
2579.population: Florida K-12 Classical teachers and administrators, College students, K-12 Students. More than 1,000 individuals will be directly served using these funds, and thousands of K-12 classical students statewide will be indirectly served through professional development for their teachers - thus enhancing their educational experience.
2579.outcome: Enriched Cultural Experience through lectures and trainings, Improved Quality of Education through professional development for K12 teachers, and increased economic activity through new jobs created and increased teacher retention rates.

2580.description: The Student Nurse Intern Program creates a comprehensive learning environment between nursing education and real- world practice by providing a unique opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge, develop practical skills, and build confidence in a clinical setting. Programs goals include recruitment, retention, clinical competence, and reduced turnover. Funding would cover salaries of interns, dedicated program staff, the purchase of new educational software to enhance the program, and testing costs. The most recent class of SNIs resulted in 100% hire rate at Halifax Health, and 99% pass rate on the NCLEX exam.
2580.purpose: The purpose and goals that will be achieved are the successful recruitment, retention, increased clinical competence, and reduced turnover of skilled nurses.
2580.activities: Recruitment, orientation, education and mentorship are the activities and services provided to meet the intended purpose of these funds. The Student Nurse Intern Program creates a comprehensive learning environment to bridge the gap between nursing education and real-world practice by pairing nurses with experienced mentors and providing a unique opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge, develop practical skills, and build confidence in a clinical setting.
2580.direct_services: Direct services provided to citizens include more competent, experienced, and skilled nursing to patients in Volusia County through the 3 hospitals, 2 freestanding emergency departments, and multiple outpatient facilities throughout the Halifax Health system.
2580.population: All citizens of Volusia County that enter the facilities at Halifax Hospital Medical Center facilities each year, as well as the nursing students who will feel more competent to continue their chosen career.
2580.outcome: Recruitment, retention, and turnover data of nurses in the healthcare system, as well as testing of and data related to clinical competence.

2876.description: Since 1998, the Hillsborough County Juvenile Assessment Center (JAC) has served as the centralized intake, screening, and assessment facility for youth entering the juvenile justice system. The JAC operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week, providing critical services that ensure public safety and proper placement for youth. After more than 25 years of continuous operation, the facility has experienced significant wear and deterioration. Renovations are urgently needed to maintain safe, secure, and efficient operations. The requested funds will be used to complete essential facility upgrades to meet current building, safety, and operational standards.
2876.purpose: The Hillsborough County JAC is a critical public safety resource. The current building infrastructure has exceeded its life expectancy, resulting in escalating maintenance costs and safety concerns. Without renovation, the facility’s ability to operate safely and effectively is at risk.
2876.activities: The proposed renovation for the 12,000 square feet building will replace the building’s aging roof to prevent leaks and further damage, install a new energy-efficient HVAC system to ensure proper climate control and air quality, and upgrade outdated electrical and plumbing systems to meet current codes. Additionally, the installation of a whole- building generator to maintain continuous operations during power outages, replacement of all doors with secure magnetic locking systems, and installati
2876.direct_services: The Hillsborough County Juvenile Assessment Center (JAC) provides direct services to youth, families, and law enforcement agencies in the community by serving as the single point of entry for juveniles taken into custody. Through this facility, youth receive immediate intake, screening, and assessment services that determine their risks, needs, and appropriate placement within the juvenile justice
2876.population: The target population served by this project includes youth ages 10–17 who are taken into custody by law enforcement in Hillsborough County and referred to the Juvenile Assessment Center (JAC) for intake, screening, and assessment. The facility also serves the families of these youth, local law enforcement agencies, and partnering service providers involved in the juvenile justice process. On average, the Hillsborough County JAC processes approximately 4,000 to 5,000 youth annually. In addition
2876.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is a safer, more secure, and fully functional JAC that can continue providing uninterrupted intake, screening, and assessment services for youth. Renovating the facility will improve safety, energy efficiency, and compliance with current building and security standards while extending the building’s useful life and reducing maintenance costs. The project’s success will be measured by reductions in facility downtime, maintenance expenses, and safety incidents, and increasing the number of youth served annually. Data from facility maintenance logs, inspection reports, and operational records will be used to evaluate.

1482.description: Suwannee County was affected by three hurricanes: Idalia, Debby, and Helen. During each of these storms we were forced to close and evacuate multiple fire/rescue stations around Suwannee County. These funds would help replace one of the stations with an up-to-date storm ready facility that could remain open during natural disasters.
1482.purpose: The new facility will be built to current standards and be able to remain open during times of natural disasters.
1482.activities: The citizens will see a direct impact with response of fire & rescue duties during times of state of emergencies and on a day-to-day basis.
1482.direct_services: This station responds to calls for service over a large portion of the center of Suwannee County as well as the southern portion of the City of Live Oak. This station also responds to all house fires county wide.
1482.population: All citizens and visitors to Suwannee County. 44,000+ people
1482.outcome: The new fire station located in the center of Suwannee County will be built to current standards and be able to remain open during times of natural disasters. Its location protects a large portion of the center of Suwannee County as well as the southern portion of the City of Live Oak. This station also responds to all house fires county wide. This will be measured using metrics from 911 call data.

1213.description: As a long time provider of education, research, and innovation training for industry and the Department of War, a Secure Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) and test equipment at Florida Tech facilities will enable classified access to partnered small and medium size firms, enable innovation and project work in a classified space, and provide a platform for specialized training and wargaming capabilities. The SCIF and equipment utilization at Florida Tech will support Florida dual-use private capital, strengthen Florida's position as a location for national defense, and create workforce development partnerships.
1213.purpose: Completion of a Secure Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) at Florida Tech facilities will enable classified access to partnered small and medium size firms, enable innovation and project work in a classified space, and provide a platform for specialized training and wargaming capabilities. The SCIF and equipment utilization will support Florida dual-use private capital, strengthen Florida's position as a location for national defense, and create workforce development partnerships.
1213.activities: Workforce partnerships requiring classified communications and prototyping, industry access to enable secure Florida- based project work and innovation, as well as "clearance-ready" based training to support Florida's defense industrial base.
1213.direct_services: Providing small and mid-size partnered companies with cybersecure SCIF access, related classified training for workforce and students, as well as basic prototyping capabilities. Direct services will include providing access, hands- on training and hands-on prototyping for project work for partnered companies.
1213.population: Florida industry and government cohort partners requiring SCIF and prototyping access to include university/college students.
1213.outcome: Our nation has a critical shortage of those properly trained to deal with the cyber and resiliency threats presented by enemy nations. Access to SCIF and basic prototyping equipment for workforce groups, companies, and entrepreneurs to keep product development and test in Florida. Measurements will include number of workforce, students, faculty and partners exposed to cybersecurity and resiliency methods as well as number of workforce and industry with access to secure facilities and equipment for comms and prototyping.

1108.description: The requested funds will support a program that prepares Florida's K-12 students for careers in aerospace by inspiring interest in STEM, expanding career awareness, and developing the skills needed to enter the aerospace workforce. This initiative aims to help close the aerospace workforce gap and supply the industry with well-prepared, skilled professionals.
1108.purpose: The goal of this project is to close Florida's growing aerospace workforce gap by preparing K–12 students for future careers in the field. Funds will support a program that inspires interest in STEM, expands career awareness, and equips students with the knowledge and technical skills needed to enter and succeed in the aerospace industry.
1108.activities: High school students and educators will work with STEM Education Specialists to engage in aerospace-related coursework and hands-on activities. Students will meet face-to-face with major aerospace organizations about internships, apprenticeships, and job opportunities.
1108.direct_services: Direct services include hands-on STEM activities, facilitated networking sessions, career panels, and one-to-one introductions to aerospace professionals and recruiters, including those hiring students from high school CTE programs.
1108.population: Over 800 Miami-Dade County Public School high school students will be served.
1108.outcome: This initiative seeks to increase the education of the aerospace industry missions and programs, and awareness and career preparedness, of participants by 80%. This program seeks to inspire students to pursue careers in science, technology, engineering and math, and increase interest by >50%. Students and educators will be provided a survey regarding missions and programs, as well as career awareness and preparedness, prior to and after their exposure to the program. Survey results will provide qualitative and quantitative data.

3008.description: Collier County faces routine threats of severe weather, flooding, and storm surge. This project requests funds to identify points of vulnerability in the wastewater collection system to better protect from inundation. Inflow and infiltration of water into the sanitary sewer collections system causes undue stress and wear to infrastructure, reduces the system's ability to transfer wastewater from residential and commercial sources to treatment facilities, and risks causing the sewer system to overflow. This project will systematically identify sources of inflow and infiltration in service basins near Naples Bay and Haldeman Creek and address those problems at the source.
3008.purpose: Identify points of vulnerability in the wastewater collection system to better protect from inundation. Inflow and infiltration of water into the sanitary sewer collections system causes undue stress and wear to infrastructure, reduces the system's ability to transfer wastewater from residential and commercial sources to treatment facilities, and risks causing the sewer system to overflow. This project will systematically identify sources of inflow and infiltration and resolve those problems at
3008.activities: This project will systematically identify sources of inflow and infiltration and resolve those problems at the source. Once the points of vulnerability are identified immediate repairs will be made.
3008.direct_services: Identify points of vulnerability in the wastewater collection system to better protect from inundation. Inflow and infiltration of water into the sanitary sewer collections system causes undue stress and wear to infrastructure, reduces the system's ability to transfer wastewater from residential and commercial sources to treatment facilities, and risks causing the sewer system to overflow. This pr
3008.population: Sewer Basins near Naples Bay and Haldeman Creek serve approximately 10,000 residents and the larger south wastewater service area serves over 103,000.
3008.outcome: Collier County faces routine treats of severe weather, flooding and storm surge. By identifying points of vulnerability where infiltration can occur during such instance it reduces the risk of sewer system overflow. Inflow and infiltration of water into the sanitary sewer collections system causes undue stress and wear to infrastructure, reduces the system's ability to transfer wastewater from residential and commercial sources to treatment facilities, and risks causing the sewer system to overflow.

1115.organization: Community Child Care of Delray Beach , Inc.
1115.description: This project will replace an aging, unreliable vehicle with a new, state-licensed 24-passenger bus to ensure safe and dependable transportation for children and teens participating in Achievement Centers for Children & Families’ Early Learning, Out-of-School, Teen, and Summer Camp Programs. The bus will provide daily transportation to and from program sites and community enrichment activities, expanding accessibility for families in under served neighborhoods and ensuring consistent participation in educational, recreational, and developmental opportunities.
1115.purpose: Grant funds will be used to purchase a fully equipped, state-licensed 24-passenger bus to provide safe, reliable transportation for children in ACCF’s Early Learning, Out-of-School, Teen, and Summer Camp Programs. The bus will support daily access to education, after school care, enrichment, and community activities throughout Delray Beach and Palm Beach County.
1115.activities: The project will fund the purchase and outfitting of a compliant 24 passenger bus with required safety systems. This ensures ACCF meets licensing standards and maintains reliable transportation essential for its education and enrichment programs.
1115.direct_services: The new bus will provide safe daily transportation for children to and from ACCF's Early Learning, Out-of-School, and Teen Programs, connecting families in underserved neighborhoods with consistent access to quality education and community resources.
1115.population: The funds requested will serve more than 800 children and staff served by ACCF. This population includes economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, preschool students, grade school students, middle school students, high school students, and their families.
1115.outcome: Replacement of an aging, unreliable bus with a safe, licensed vehicle meeting all DCF and Palm Beach County standards. Up to 1,000 children and families annually benefit from reliable transportation access to educational, afterschool, and teen enrichment programs. Children safely transported to educational and enrichment programs with opportunities for daily nutrition and physical activity. Consistent access to safe, supportive environments reduces stress and anxiety for children and families. Reliable transportation allows parents and caregivers to work full schedules while children attend safe, quality programs.
