2690.description: The construction of the Nassau County Sheriff's Office K-9 Unit Regional Training Center. This project proposes the development of a state-of-the-art K9 training facility dedicated to enhancing law enforcement capabilities in suspect apprehension and narcotics detection. The facility will serve as a regional hub for specialized canine training, deployment, supporting local, state, and federal agencies in their mission to combat crime and drug trafficking. Through rigorous training programs and cutting-edge infrastructure, the center will produce highly skilled K9 teams capable of responding to complex law enforcement challenges and to construct additional improvements at the Public Safety Training Complex to support the continued expansion of the complex and further support public safety.
2690.purpose: To construct a purpose-built K9 facility with indoor and outdoor training environments tailored to K9 operations that will allow the NCSO to train and certify law enforcement K9s in suspect apprehension, narcotics detection, and handler safety.
2690.activities: Integrate advanced scent detection technologies and simulation environments. Provide ongoing education and certification for K9 handlers and support personnel. Foster interagency collaboration with regional, state and federal agencies and knowledge-sharing through joint training exercises.
2690.direct_services: Locating and apprehending dangerous fugitives, as well as tracking individuals with cognitive disabilities, autism, or those reported missing, are key functions of the K-9 unit. These specially trained dogs also play a vital role in detecting illegal narcotics, helping to keep harmful substances out of communities and schools. Effective detection training is critical in reducing drug-related overd
2690.population: This project will serve the broad and diverse community and surrounding regions to include elderly individuals, persons with poor mental health, at-risk youth, the developmentally and physically disabled individuals, drug users and offenders, students of all ages and victims of crime. These groups are impacted through enhanced public safety, faster response times, improved narcotics detection, and specialized training capabilities by trained K9 units. It is anticipated to reach thousands of indi
2690.outcome: Benefits include apprehension of dangerous criminals, locating and recovery of missing persons, detection and removal of illegal narcotics, reduction in drug-related incidents and improved emergency response and investigative efficiency. Methodology of outcomes will be arrest and apprehension records, number of missing persons located, quantities and types of narcotics detected and seized, overdose statistics, training benchmarks and certification records, reports from schools and public areas showing reduced drug presence.

2450.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2450.description: The project involves constructing an all-purpose educational facility that will expand our successful field trip complex, which hosted more than 30,000 students last year from across Florida as well as Georgia, Alabama, and Tennessee. This facility is essential for providing a safe environment for students during field trips, particularly during inclement weather, and will feature rotating exhibits that highlight the rich history of Florida agriculture. Additionally, the building will include permanent, sanitary restroom facilities to replace the temporary portable units currently in use.
2450.purpose: The purpose of adding an all-purpose facility is to ensure we can continue educating students about Florida agriculture and history in a safe, sanitary, and supportive environment.
2450.activities: The multi-use building will support a range of activities and services, including new agricultural exhibits, space for workshops and special events, a safe shelter during hazardous weather conditions, and permanent sanitary restroom facilities.
2450.direct_services: Citizens from across the state will have the opportunity to participate in a variety of programs designed to educate the public about Florida agriculture in an engaging and enjoyable setting. Core offerings include programs on Native American history, an archaeological dig experience, the British Period, and the arrival of Spanish ships in 1521.
2450.population: The primary target population is fourth-grade students from public, private, and home schools, as their curriculum focuses on Florida history—typically without an emphasis on agricultural heritage. However, students from all elementary, middle, and high school grade levels participate, and each program is tailored to be age-appropriate and educationally relevant.
2450.outcome: The expected outcome is to expand participation to schools that are not currently engaged in the programs while continuing to serve the more than 10,000 students who attend annually.

1494.description: Franklin County is requesting funding to provide the 50% non-Federal cost share for a shoreline modeling and sediment transport study focused on Bob Sike’s Cut and surrounding areas of St. George Island. This project is being advanced through a partnership with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) under its Planning Assistance to States program. The County seeks to procure professional engineering services to generate science-based data that will improve understanding of shoreline erosion, sediment movement, and inlet dynamics. These insights are critical for guiding future restoration, storm protection, and beach management strategies. The scope of work for this effort has been formally approved by USACE’s division office, ensuring technical rigor and alignment with Federal planning standards.
1494.purpose: The primary objective of this project is to develop a regional sediment budget and modeling tool to better understand inlet morphology and shoreline change affecting Franklin County’s barrier islands. These coastal systems are dynamic and vulnerable to erosion, storm impacts, and sea level rise. The total project budget is $600,000, structured as a 50/50 cost share between Federal and non-Federal sources. This funding will support all study phases, including data collection, modeling, analysis,
1494.activities: The main tasks are listed below: 1. Gather and assess existing information in the area, including native sediment characteristics, topographic and hydrographic surveys, shoreline positions, hydrodynamics and existing numerical modeling tools. 2. Develop updated shoreline changes and sediment budgets. 3. Determine approximate modeling suite and domain setup. 4. Calibrate and validate using historical data (waves, water levels, shoreline change and observed sediment transport). 5. Hindcast modelin
1494.direct_services: This project will provide citizens with improved coastal protection by supporting data-driven shoreline management and erosion mitigation. Residential development on St. George Island began in the 1980s, roughly two decades after the construction of the St. George Island Channel, which continues to influence sediment movement and shoreline vulnerability. In 2024, a restoration feasibility study wa
1494.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is a scientifically validated understanding of sediment transport, shoreline change, and inlet dynamics affecting St. George Island and adjacent coastal areas. This will directly inform erosion mitigation, storm protection, and long-term beach management strategies. The methodology centers on the development and application of the Coastal Modeling System (CMS), which will simulate how sediment particles move within the system. Modeling inputs will include hydrodynamics, existing bathymetry, native sediment characteristics, and historical hydrologic data. The model will be calibrated and validated using historical shoreline change and sediment transport re

2478.description: The AMPLIFY Clearwater Chamber Foundation respectfully requests $140,500 in non-recurring state funding to support the Young Entrepreneurs Academy (YEA!), a nationally recognized program for middle and high school students. Operated locally under the IGNITE Entrepreneurship Center, YEA! transforms students ages 11–18 into confident entrepreneurs as they create, pitch, and launch legally registered businesses. Each year, a cohort of 30 students works with business leaders, educators, & mentors to develop business plans, conduct market research, register companies, and present to a panel of investors for startup funding.
2478.purpose: The requested funds will ensure equitable access to the Young Entrepreneurs Academy (YEA!) by providing scholarships, supporting instruction and operations, and expanding outreach to more schools. Each year, 30 middle and high school students will develop business plans, pitch to investors, and launch legally registered businesses, gaining workforce skills in leadership, financial literacy, communication, and problem-solving while strengthening Florida’s future entrepreneurial and small business
2478.activities: Students complete a project-based entrepreneurship curriculum where they learn to identify business opportunities, conduct market research, write business plans, and understand core concepts like finance and marketing. Facilitators lead classes supported by site visits, guest speakers, and workshops. Each student is paired with a local business mentor and pitches at the annual YEA! Investor Panel for potential startup funding.
2478.direct_services: Clearwater will deliver a 20-week entrepreneurship program for middle & high school students, providing direct education & mentoring. Participants learn to create & launch real businesses through hands-on instruction, mentorship from local entrepreneurs, & access to investor funding. The program includes classroom learning, site visits, guest speakers, and coaching. Scholarships ensure equitable a
2478.population: Clearwater serves middle and high school students in Pinellas County, with a focus on engaging underserved and underrepresented youth who have limited access to entrepreneurship education. The program targets students in grades 6–12 who demonstrate an interest in business, innovation, and leadership. Each 20-week program cycle will serve approximately 30 students annually, providing them with hands-on instruction, mentorship, and the opportunity to develop and launch their own small businesses.
2478.outcome: YEA! will develop a new generation of young entrepreneurs equipped with the skills, confidence, & resources to start & sustain businesses in Florida. Students gain measurable improvements in financial literacy, leadership, problem- solving, communication, & workforce readiness, & launch real businesses that support local economic growth. Outcomes will be measured through pre- & post-assessments, tracking student business launches, mentor engagement, attendance/completion rates, & follow-up surveys.

1270.organization: The Arbor School of Central Florida
1270.description: Arbor School of Central Florida proudly serves students ages 5 -22 with varying disabilities. Currently Arbor School is at physical capacity for both the Winter Springs and Lake Mary Campus. This funding would allow Arbor School to build capacity by opening a 3rd campus in Wekiva Springs. The new campus would initially serve K-5 grade and expand to middle and high school over a 3-5 year period. The funds would help cover the costs related to staffing, rent, and insurance.
1270.purpose: Around 15% of children receive special education under IDEA. ADHD, autism, and dyslexia affect roughly 5–9% of school-aged children, highlighting the need for specialized support. Arbor School meets this need by tailoring individualized learning plans, therapeutic services, multi-sensory instructional methods, small class sizes, and highly trained staff, where students with disabilities can thrive
1270.activities: These funds will be used to open a campus in Wekiva Springs enabling families with special needs children to access a quality education. This campus would serve approximately 170 students, doubling the current capacity.
1270.direct_services: Arbor School provides a quality education that includes small classrooms, a student/teacher ratio of 5/1, speech, language, occupational therapies, STEAM, performing arts, and workforce training for students with disabilities ages 5 - 22.
1270.population: The Arbor School of Central Florida serves students ages 5 -22 with disabilities such as autism, Down syndrome, intellectual disabilities, learning disabilities as well as ADHD and anxiety related conditions. Estimated enrollment at the new campus will be 170 students.
1270.outcome: Arbor School measures success through 40% academic growth, 30% social and behavioral improvement, 20% executive functioning and life skills, and 10% family and student feedback. This balanced approach ensures personalized progress, helping students achieve their goals, gain confidence, and develop essential skills for independence and lifelong success

1576.description: These funds will allow Boys Town to address system gaps for high-need families through prevention and diversion services. The funds will make available Care Coordination Services (CCS), evidence-informed case management, or Common Sense Parenting (CSP), an evidence-based parent education program. CCS will be provided to 100 families, helping more than 200 children. An additional 150 families will be served through CSP.
1576.purpose: Care Coordination Services (CCS) and Common Sense Parenting (CSP) are designed to reduce risk factors associated with juvenile justice and child welfare involvement. The programs also enhance protective factors that support mental and behavioral health, placement stability for post-adoption families, and economic self-sufficiency.
1576.activities: Boys Town Florida will provide prevention and diversion support services including Care Coordination Services (CCS), evidence-informed case management, and Common Sense Parenting® (CSP), evidence-based parent education. CCS assesses needs and connects families with essential resources and support before crises escalate. CSP teaches parents practical strategies to address challenging behaviors, enforce effective discipline, enhance communication skills, establish age-appropriate supervision, and
1576.direct_services: CCS Consultants work closely with families in their homes and communities. Based on assessments and referrals, families are connected to numerous services, such as mental health, educational support, medical care, and housing. Service linkages are tracked to ensure families progress and parents/caregivers learn how to access resources independently prior to case closure. CCS aims to stabilize fami
1576.population: Due to the elevated risk of crisis and system involvement, Boys Town Florida will focus on the following populations at our North, Central, and South Florida sites: families facing mental or behavioral health challenges; those ineligible for Medicaid, and post-adoption families needing continued support. We anticipate serving 100 families through CCS and an additional 150 families through CSP.
1576.outcome: If awarded funding, we anticipate the following outcomes: (1) Participants will demonstrate improved mental health (CCS: Improvement on the depression domain on the pre-and-post Children's Functional Assessment Rating Scale. CSP: Improvement on the pre-and-post Parental Stress Scale). (2) Families participating in prevention and diversion support services with adolescent children will not have contact with the juvenile justice system after the program (CCS: Socio-legal domain of the Children's Functional Assessment Rating Scale completed at discharge and no contact with the juvenile justice system per family reporting. CSP: No contact with the juvenile justice system per family reporting). (

1655.description: This project addresses chronic flooding in the industrial and commercial area bounded by Powerline Road, NW 33rd Court, NW 18th Terrace, and NW 31st Street. The area’s limited drainage and extensive impervious surfaces result in significant ponding during moderate to heavy rainfall. To mitigate these conditions, the City of Pompano Beach Utilities Department proposes to install underground exfiltration trench systems within public rights-of-way and re-grade swale areas to provide additional stormwater storage. These upgrades will improve infiltration, enhance groundwater recharge, mitigate against property damage and promote long-term environmental sustainability. The project aligns with recommendations from the Stormwater Master Plan and supports the City’s resilience and flood-mitigation goals.
1655.purpose: Control and manage runoff by adding infiltration trenches; improve water quality to surface body waters; recharge groundwater system which supplies the Biscayne aquifer. Prevent pollution and mitigate flooding and property damage.
1655.activities: Installation of subsurface drainage infrastructure Re-grading of existing swales Site restoration and roadway resurfacing
1655.direct_services: Alleviate flooding by installing new drainage, enhanced safety for drivers and pedestrians, mitigate property damage.
1655.population: The target population includes all residents and businesses especially industrial businesses and commuters within the corridor and residents downstream affected by runoff from rain events.
1655.outcome: The outcome will be measured by data collected from previous rain events. Other key benefits of this project include flood prevention and the reduction of standing water which will greatly improve the safety of drivers and pedestrians. This will also help eliminate stagnant water that can become a breeding ground for mosquitoes and other pests. It will also help mitigate against property damage / losses.

1734.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1734.description: Acquire, store, transport and distribute healthy and nutritious fruits, vegetables, proteins, dairy and non-perishable food products free of charge to Farm Share's nearly 2,000 statewide partner agencies as well as directly distributing food to hungry families, children, seniors and individuals in food insecure communities. Farm Share also acts as a first responder organization during times of natural disasters and pandemics.
1734.purpose: Florida faces a chronic hunger challenge and is ranked 10th in food insecurity. This is unacceptable, especially in light of the fact that 40% of every crop harvested in Florida is thrown away or plowed under. These are edible, nutritious foods that are thrown away instead of being packaged and sold on grocery store shelves. Farm Share exists to take this produce and other shelf stable food products, dairy and protiens and use it to address the hunger crisis in the State of Florida. We are able
1734.activities: Acquisition and Distribution of healthy and nutrition fruits, vegetables, non-perishable food products and proteins to partner agencies (soup kitchens, food pantries, churches, law enforcement agencies, etc...) throughout the state of Florida. These partners agencies then distribute the food directly to persons in need in the regions and local communities that they serve. We also directly distribute food to families, children, seniors and individuals in need utilizing our fleet of semi-trucks an
1734.direct_services: Farm Share facilitates nearly 20,000 Community Food Distributions each year statewide in conjunction with our nearly 2,000 partner agencies. These food distributions provide food directly to those persons identified below in high poverty communities. Farm Share frequently partners with other social service organizations to provide health screenings, educational opportunities and job training on si
1734.population: Families, children, seniors and individuals who are hungry and living in poverty or affected by a natural or man made disaster. More than 86 million meals are expected to be served to these persons statewide.
1734.outcome: Farm Share tracks a broad range of outcomes on an ongoing basis, including amount of food collected, distributed, and the number of food distribution events held around the states to provide food to underprivileged residents or those affected by a disaster. By the end of this funding period, we anticipate distributing over 100 million pounds of food to people across the State of Florida.

1379.description: Funds requested provide for critically needed renovation and expansion of Miami Beach Community Health Center's 710-720 Alton Road location. Renovation will ensure that MBCHC, a critical safety net provider on Miami Beach, will continue to provide high quality, affordable primary health care and specialty services, chronic disease management, and support services to a largely poor, uninsured, and medically underserved patient population. MBCHC provided 162,901 visits for 51,561 patients in 2024.
1379.purpose: Renovation of 710-720 Alton Road will ensure that a critical safety net provider on Miami Beach will be able to continue providing award-winning, high-quality, affordable health care services to the poor, uninsured, and medically underserved. MBCHC's operations from the 710 side of the building are cramped. Renovating the 720 side of the building will facilitate expansion of operations to serve increasing numbers of patients.
1379.activities: MBCHC engaged a general contractor for design build services to perform the necessary repairs and to add 25 examination rooms to the building at 710-720 Alton Road, Miami Beach. Work to be done to the 720 side of the building includes: removing and replacing the existing floating slab, installing new pin piles, providing clean fill compacted and treated for termites, installing 12" x 18" grade beams following the existing steel column layout, and installing a new 8" concrete slab with rebar mat
1379.direct_services: The project to renovate the 720 section of the building at 710-720 Alton Road will expand MBCHC's capacity to provide primary health care (including oral health and behavioral health) and enabling services, such as outreach and enrollment services, public benefits eligibility assistance, pharmacy and laboratory services, and transportation, to increasing numbers of low-income and uninsured people.
1379.population: Low-income and uninsured individuals are the target population. MBCHC expects to serve 15,000 or more individuals in the year following completion of this project. Over ninety-five percent of MBCHC patients are low-income. Eighty-six percent have incomes below the Federal Poverty Level. More than a third (33.7%) of patients are uninsured.
1379.outcome: The expected benefit from this project is a safer building, suitable for occupancy, from which to deliver high quality, affordable health care services to the community. The outcome will be certified by Miami Beach and Miami-Dade County building inspectors. Through data collected and published by he United Stated HHS and HRSA UDS reports, data on MBCHC services will reflect the high quality of care received by the MBCHC patients.

1145.description: Tech for Good requests state funding to provide hands-on training in AI, Data Science, Generative AI, and Digital Marketing for 200 City of Miami residents from Little Havana, Allapattah, Little Haiti, Little River, and other Opportunity Zones impacted by Hurricane Milton. The program will equip underserved individuals with in-demand technology skills, leading to 80 job placements and $1.7 million in new annual wages. Supported by a 50/50 match from the Venture Miami Scholarship Fund and private partners and implemented with Miami Dade College North as a community partner, this initiative advances equitable recovery and workforce development across Miami.
1145.purpose: The project will train 200 underserved Miami residents impacted by Hurricane Milton in AI, Data Science, Generative AI, and Digital Marketing. It aims to equip participants with in-demand digital skills leading to 80 job placements and $1.7M in new annual wages, thereby supporting workforce recovery and advancing Miami's innovation economy
1145.activities: Instructor-led academies, mentorship, and career coaching focused on AI, Data Science, Generative AI, and Digital Marketing. Activities include student recruitment, technical training, certification preparation, job-readiness workshops, and employer networking to ensure placement success.
1145.direct_services: Participants will receive hands-on technical training, professional mentorship, certification opportunities, and direct job- placement support — all at no cost to them — improving employability and long-term income stability.
1145.population: The target population is underserved adults (ages 18–45) from the City of Miami neighborhoods of Little Havana, Allapattah, Little Haiti, Little River, and nearby Opportunity Zones that were impacted by Hurricane Milton. The project is expected to serve 200 participants. The goals also include 170 program completions and 80 job placements.
1145.outcome: The project will train 200 residents, aiming for 170 completions and 80 job placements, and is expected to generate over $1.7 million in new annual wages while increasing employment and digital skills. Outcomes will be tracked via attendance, completion certificates, and verified job-placement data in the AGS Prime system and reviewed quarterly by the partners.

1927.description: Funds will be used for the construction of a 1,200-ft of 10-inch water main improvements along with new fire hydrants on Cassady Street, including engineering services during construction. These critical upgrades will increase fire protection for residents as well as fire flow, improve distribution system pressure, and ensure a safe, adequate drinking water supply for the city. The project will replace aging infrastructure, enhance system resiliency, and support long-term water service reliability to meet current and future demands.
1927.purpose: The funds will be used to harden the water distribution system, increasing fire flow capacity, water pressure, and overall reliability of Umatilla's potable water system. By replacing critical water mains, abandoning damaged and leaking lines, and installing new water lines, this project will improve fire flow and ensure clean, safe drinking water delivery. 2882.description: The Florida Legacy Homeownership Initiative is a practical plan to help hardworking Floridians—especially our police officers, teachers, healthcare workers, and veterans—buy and keep their homes. It would fund land and construction upfront, then offers grants and savings programs to help families purchase their home. Before buying, families complete a financial literacy and savings course. After purchase, they get support to stay current on bills and protect their property through estate planning. The return on investment is clear: fewer families need public housing or emergency aid, neighborhoods stay stable, and wealth stays in the family. Taxpayer dollars go further by building long-term security, not short-term fixes.

This project will enhance traffic flow on major corridors within the City of Palm Bay, improve public safety by reducing emergency response times and decreasing accidents through the addition of emergency vehicle preemption.

This initiative yields measurable outcomes: fewer incidents, increased attendance, stronger academic performance, and a pipeline of resilient graduates who contribute meaningfully to Florida’s future.

2063.description: The Senior Food and Resource Program reduces food insecurity and improves health for seniors by providing nutritious food and supports in accessible, trusted community locations. Through a network of agency partners, the program delivers multiple access models including on-site congregate meals, mobile distributions, home delivery, and community pantries.

The program ensures that older adults have consistent access to nutritious food and essential resources through trusted, easily reachable locations across the Treasure Coast.

2063.outcome: Our goal is to improve health and reduce food insecurity among seniors by providing consistent access to nutritious food in central, convenient, and accessible community locations. We will measure this by tracking the number of meals, number of seniors served, and number of partners.

2416.description: Design, permitting, and construction of the Williston Public Safety Complex (Complex) that would house Williston Fire Rescue, Williston Police Department, Williston Communications Center and Florida Forestry Service. The Complex will be located adjacent to the Williston Municipal Airport, which is centrally located in Levy County and away from Evacuation Areas. The Complex would allow for all Emergency Responders to be located in an area large enough for safe operation. This will also allow for pre and post disaster planning and operations during an event.
2416.purpose: Funds will be used to fund the design, permitting, and construction of a new Public Safety Headquarters for the City of Williston. This facility will support Emergency Management, Fire Rescue, Emergency Medical Services, and Law Enforcement. The new Complex will provide services for the City of Williston and surrounding areas of Levy County.

The larger training rooms will allow for more public education training to include CPR and Fire Prevention for Households.

2416.outcome: The Public Safety Headquarters would benefit the overall physical, mental, and financial health of the community by having the resources and facilities to support first responders in reacting to emergency situations. Having a new and safe facilities would allow first responders to react more quickly and efficiently to emergencies. The facility's teaching rooms will educate first responders in the newest methods and technologies for emergency response and community engagement.

1537.description: The project will expand access to workforce training across Florida by equipping partner organizations, including state agencies, workforce boards, schools, and community programs, with Transfr's virtual reality training systems. As the statewide grantee, Transfr will oversee distribution, implementation, and reporting, while partner organizations will leverage Transfr's programming to recruit, expose, and prepare Floridians for employment in high-demand industries. This coordinated approach strengthens local capacity and supports Florida's 2030 workforce goals to strengthen the talent pipeline and increase employability statewide.

The goal is to strengthen Florida's talent pipeline and support Florida 2030 workforce targets, ensuring at least 80% of workers demonstrate essential employability skills and 60% earn a high-value credential.
1537.activities: Funds will provide VR training systems (software and hardware) to state and local agencies, workforce boards, and community partners. 1537.direct_services: Participants will access VR-based career simulations and guided training that mirror real workplace environments. These experiences help Floridians identify and explore career interests, gain job-ready skills, and connect with employment pathways in high-demand career fields such as Manufacturing, Healthcare, Construction, Information Technology, and more.

1737.description: A new reclaimed water storage tank, strategically located near a high-demand area like the Oldsmar Sports Complex, directly supports the goals of Florida Senate Bill 64 by increasing the capacity for beneficial reuse and simultaneously reducing nonbeneficial wet weather discharge to the bay. Currently, the WRF has intermittent discharge events to the Bay that could be avoided with additional capacity functioning as a crucial holding reservoir that absorbs sudden, wet- weather surplus.

This makes the supply reliable, ensuring the Complex uses its full allocation and maximizes beneficial reuse. Additionally, by reducing wet-weather discharges, the project reduces even the small, cumulative nutrient loading to the Bay from this facility.

1737.outcome: The project enhances Bay health by reducing nutrient loading. By decreasing the intermittent discharge of wet-weather surplus, the new tank directly reduces the flow of nutrients (Nitrogen and Phosphorus) into the Bay connected to algal blooms and water quality degradation crucial to habitats like seagrass beds, thus protecting the Bay's fish and wildlife. The new storage tank acts as a holding area for the extra reclaimed water produced during rain events. This eliminates the need for the facility to make intermittent discharges of treated water (even low-nutrient water) into the bay, which directly reduces the nutrient loading and achieves the state's environmental goals. 1566.description: The Town of Suwannee, Dixie County was impacted by Hurricane Helene, which made landfall in September of 2024 as a Category 4 storm. The Town's wastewater treatment plant ID# FLA016664-006 experienced a full system failure due to storm surge. This funding will be used to design and permit resiliency and system hardening improvements for the Town's wastewater treatment plant in order to repair and prevent a repeat of the public health crisis and environmental hazards that occurred during hurricane Helene.
1566.purpose: The funds will go towards the design and permitting for the Town of Suwannee's wastewater treatment plant to make essential resiliency and hardening improvements. These improvements will mitigate future risks of wastewater overflow and system failure during natural disasters by sustaining and protecting operations before, during, and after storm surge events.
1566.activities: The funds will be used to design and permit resiliency and hardening improvements to the Town of Suwannee's wastewater treatment plant, which serves a population of approximately 750 people.
1566.direct_services: These improvements will assist in maintaining essential wastewater services, reduce the risk of sewer overflows, enhance infrastructure resilience, and provide energy efficiency before, during, and after extreme weather events.
1566.population: The entire Town of Suwannee will be served by this project. The Town's population is currently approximately 750 people.
1566.outcome: The wastewater treatment plant improvements to be designed and permitted will ensure the plant's future resiliency before, during, and after natural disasters. This will also ensure that the plant can maintain operations, efficiency, and safety to prevent full system failures. The benefits will improve wastewater management systems, storm water management systems, and improve the quality of drinking water, surface water, and ground water. An additional benefit will be the protection of the surrounding environment and community from harmful wastewater. The method of measurement will be a reduction in the level of water pollutants and contaminants in wastewater as demonstrated through sampling

1559.description: This project previously received $300,000 in funding to expand the spray field during the 2023-2024 budget cycle. With rising water levels and increasingly intense storms, this area offers a rare contiguous open landscape through which retention, infiltration, and buffering can be integrated to mitigate peak runoff and filter pollutants before they reach the C-8 system.
1420.purpose: Increasing the site’s capacity to capture, store, and slowly release runoff, reducing the risk of flooding in surrounding neighborhoods. Retention and detention ponds will be regraded and expanded to hold larger storm events, while conveyance channels and drainage infrastructure will direct water efficiently toward treatment areas and the C-8 canal.
1420.activities: Creating natural treatment systems help remove nutrients, sediments, and pollutants, which in turn protects aquatic habitats in the Biscayne Bay Aquifer. Enhancing stormwater storage and slowing runoff reduces erosion and sedimentation, preserving the integrity of surrounding waterways and providing more stable habitats for fish and wildlife.
1420.direct_services: The redesign willl help slow stormwater infiltration, allowing natural processes to remove pollutants before water percolates into the groundwater. As runoff passes through vegetated areas and soil layers, contaminants such as nutrients, sediments, and heavy metals are filtered and broken down by microbial activity, reducing the risk of groundwater contamination.
1420.population: The properties that surround the area near and abutting the C-8 canal as well as the properties on SR915 to the west.
1420.outcome: Reducing the risk of flooding in surrounding neighborhoods; reducing the risk of groundwater contamination; and natural filtration of pollutants from stormwater before it reaches the C-8 canal, all measured by water quality tests.

1399.description: The funds requested will contribute to the construction of a critical public safety facility for North Bay Village and surrounding areas. This project will have a total cost of over $50,000,000. The Village is currently in the construction bidding phase, so a final cost estimate is unavailable at the time of writing. The Village is covering the vast majority of the funds required, with $37,000,000 in hand as of today. The project establishes a public safety complex with fire and police stations that provide critical emergency response capabilities. The facility will improve service delivery and emergency response times along the critical SR-934 evacuation route.
1399.purpose: The primary goal is to construct the North Bay Village Hall & Public Safety Complex, which will substantially enhance emergency emergency response capabilities and strengthen public safety infrastructure in North Bay Village, Miami, Miami Beach, and surrounding areas, while improving critical evacuation route coverage along SR-934. North Bay Village does not currently have a fire station, and its police department leases space in a private facility.
1399.activities: The project encompasses construction of an emergency response facility, including installation of modern public safety equipment, dedicated spaces for first responders and support staff, emergency communications infrastructure, and a coordinated disaster response center. Specifically, the funds will be directed to the construction of a fire station and police station.
1399.direct_services: This facility will provide improved emergency response times, enhanced disaster preparedness capabilities, better- coordinated public safety services, increased capacity for emergency medical services, and strengthened evacuation support along SR-934. North Bay Village is an island community, separated from mainland Miami and Miami Beach by two bascule bridges. It does not currently have a fire st
1399.population: The target population served by this project is the entire population of North Bay Village, as well as surrounding areas. About 15,000 individuals are expected to be served.
1399.outcome: The project will provide measurable improvements in emergency response times, enhanced emergency response capabilities, more efficient evacuation coordination during disasters, and expanded service coverage throughout the area. These outcomes will be monitored through comprehensive data collection and regular performance assessments.

1400.description: The funding will be allocated to the construction of a major sanitary sewer replacement project along Camden Drive. The project includes replacing aging sewer mains, laterals, and manholes to ensure reliable wastewater service, reduce the risk of system failures, and support safe roadway reconstruction. These improvements will protect public health, modernize essential underground infrastructure, and enhance the overall resilience of the community.
1400.purpose: The funds will be used to replace aging sanitary sewer mains, laterals, and manholes along Camden Drive and restore the roadway above them. This work will ensure reliable wastewater service, reduce the risk of system failures and public health hazards, and provide safe, improved roadway conditions for residents and the community.
1400.activities: Activities and services will include replacement of sewer mains, laterals, and manholes; roadway restoration including sub-base work, curb and gutter replacement, milling and paving; and construction administration and inspection services to ensure compliance and quality control.
1400.direct_services: The funding will provide Bal Harbour residents with reliable sanitary sewer service by replacing failing underground infrastructure that currently poses risks of system backups and service interruptions.
1400.population: General (The majority of funds will benefit no specific group) >800
1400.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is the modernization of critical sanitary sewer infrastructure along Camden Drive, ensuring reliable wastewater service, protecting public health, and preventing costly system failures or environmental impacts. In addition, the project will restore roadway conditions through improved sub-base work, curb and gutter replacement, and resurfacing, providing safer and more durable transportation access for residents and visitors. The outcome will be measured through reduced emergency maintenance calls and sewer overflows, and compliance with utility and environmental regulations.

1672.description: The requested funds will be used for the construction of drainage infrastructure to address critical flood control issues in the Lakes of Emerald Hills community. This includes the installation of drainage structures, an outfall pipe connecting Leaping Cat Lake to the C10 Canal Spur, culverts, pavement restoration, and lake maintenance, including muck removal. Improvements will alleviate flooding, restore water quality, and establish sustainable stormwater management for the surrounding area.
1672.purpose: The requested funds will be used for the construction of drainage infrastructure to address critical flood control issues in the Lakes of Emerald Hills community. This includes the installation of drainage structures, an outfall pipe connecting Leaping Cat Lake to the C10 Canal Spur, culverts, pavement restoration, and lake maintenance, including muck removal. Improvements will alleviate flooding, restore water quality, and establish sustainable stormwater management for the surrounding area.
1672.activities: The City of Hollywood has issued a contract for the design phase of the project. The City will secure permits and initiate the bidding process for construction services, targeted to begin by August 2026.
1672.direct_services: The project will improve drainage efficiency and mitigate the risk of flooding and water damage to surrounding homes.
1672.population: The target population is over 1,000 residents in the Lakes of Emerald Hills community. This includes the Lakes of Emerald Hills HOA (201 homes), the Townhouses HOA, 15 unaffiliated properties, and a City of Hollywood park, all of which rely on Leaping Cat Lake as a drainage basin.
1672.outcome: The construction of the flood control drain will enhance stormwater management by mitigating flooding and improving drainage efficiency in the Lakes of Emerald Hills community. This infrastructure will also improve surface water quality by reducing pollutant levels, removing accumulated muck, and preventing further contamination caused by stormwater runoff. Outcomes will be measured through reductions in flood events and monitoring flow rates. Improvements in surface water quality will be assessed through regular water quality inspections.

1845.description: Requested funding will implement Phase III of South Daytona’s Sewer System Rehabilitation Pipelining project. In FY 2023-24 and 2024-25, the state appropriated $750,000 million (fully matched by local funding). The initiative reduced sewer costs by nearly 20% in FY 2024-25, avoiding $500,000 in capacity costs. Over the life of the project, more than $24 million in treatment charges will be saved. The rehabilitation will also conserve energy, lower chemical usage, and protect regional water resources by reducing stormwater infiltration. Phase III is matched by local funds to continue strengthening critical infrastructure and delivering lasting financial and environmental benefits for the community and the State of Florida.
1845.purpose: The requested funds will advance Phase III of South Daytona’s Sewer System Rehabilitation Pipelining project which is strengthening critical infrastructure, reducing inflow and infiltration, lowering treatment costs, and protecting regional water resources.
1845.activities: Funds will support cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) lining, contracted labor and equipment, inspection and testing, and project management to ensure reliable rehabilitation of aging sewer lines.
1845.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from reduced sewer rates, improved sewer reliability, fewer backups and overflows, and enhanced environmental protection through reduced stormwater infiltration.
1845.population: The project will serve all 13,000 residents of the City of South Daytona, as well as businesses and institutions connected to the sewer system. Indirectly, the project benefits the broader region by reducing unnecessary treatment at the Daytona Beach regional facility.
1845.outcome: The project will lower long-term sewer treatment costs (a projected $24 million in lifetime savings), reduce inflow and infiltration, conserve energy and chemicals, and extend the lifespan of the infrastructure. Outcomes will be measured through sewer flow monitoring, annual financial analysis of treatment charges, and system inspection reports.

1581.description: This project addresses canal stabilization along the North Canal in South Miami-Dade County. The work includes repair, restoration & stabilization of the canal bank erosion. There is an immediate need to restore canal bank & erosion control to protect the canal from pollutants that are harmful to water quality & flood control throughout the canal network. The North Canal has also experienced widespread erosion.
1581.purpose: Canal stabilization along the North Canal in South Miami-Dade County. There is an immediate need to restore canal bank & erosion control to protect the canal from pollutants that are harmful to water quality & flood control throughout the canal network. The North Canal has experienced widespread erosion in recent years.
1581.activities: The work includes repair, restoration & stabilization of the North Canal bank erosion.
1581.direct_services: Improved water quality and roadway safety as a result of the project's timely and successful completion.
1581.population: Residents in the Southern part of Miami-Dade County as well as travelers on the road adjacent to North Canal. Thousands of individuals will be served by the project's completion.
1581.outcome: Improved water quality and roadway safety. The level of benefit or outcome will be measured by monitoring water quality parameters, such as turbidity and pollutant levels, before and after the restoration. Additionally, periodic inspections of the canal bank will assess structural stability and erosion control effectiveness.

2603.description: The Mickler Boulevard outfall north treats and conveys stormwater runoff from the city of St. Augustine Beach. Erosion and sedimentation resulting from rainfall events have compromised outfall resiliency and capacity. This funding initiative request is for design, permitting and construction of a durable bulwark to protect existing 1) underground and overhead utilities; 2) traffic evacuation & pedestrian mobility routes and 4) stabilize the outfall west bank to mitigate present and projected surge impact and erosion of adjacent properties. Reduce 1) cost of proactive and 2) frequency of reactive emergency maintenance along this vital outfall segment.
2603.purpose: Provide durable bulwark to protect existing 1) underground and overhead utilities; 2) traffic evacuation & pedestrian mobility routes and 4) stabilize the outfall west bank to mitigate present and projected surge impact and erosion of adjacent properties. Reduce 1) cost of proactive and 2) frequency of reactive emergency maintenance along this vital outfall segment.
2603.direct_services: Increased Level of Service (LOS) by providing durable bulwark to protect existing 1) underground & overhead utilities; 2) traffic evacuation & pedestrian mobility routes & 3) stabilize the outfall west bank to mitigate present and projected surge impact and erosion of adjacent property. Reduce 1) cost of proactive and 2) frequency of reactive emergency maintenance along this vital outfall segment.
2603.population: City of St. Augustine Beach residents and a portion of St. Johns County residents. Approximately 7,000 individuals are served.
2603.outcome: Mitigate stormwater runoff: 1) Roadway inundation by floodwater: City staff observations of road inundation and infrastructure performance, field data collection, resident interviews, and # of Public Works work orders related to roadway/flood damage. 2) Infrastructure damage mitigation: # of threats or safety hazards to the general public and emergency responders, # of related resident comments or complaints and routine vulnerability assessment updates.

1847.description: Replacement of a 40-year-old 911 dispatch consoles with a reliable, ISO-compliant system that ensures continuous service and interoperability. The project also integrates EaseAlert, a station alerting system that reduces responder stress and cardiac risk while improving turnout times, enhancing safety and providing faster, more effective emergency response.
1847.purpose: The purpose is to replace 40-year-old 911 dispatch consoles with a reliable, ISO-compliant system that ensures continuous service and interoperability. The project also integrates EaseAlert, a station alerting system that reduces responder stress and cardiac risk while improving turnout times, enhancing safety and providing faster, more effective emergency response.
1847.activities: The project will provide reliable 911 call-taking, CAD integration, and radio interoperability to coordinate response. It will also implement EaseAlert to deliver vibration and visual alerts directly to responders, minimizing the startle effect, reducing cardiac strain, and ensuring faster, safer emergency turnout.
1847.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from faster, more reliable 911 call processing, improved coordination of fire, EMS, and police response, and reduced risk of communication failures during emergencies. This ensures quicker dispatch of help, stronger disaster response, and greater safety for the community in everyday incidents and large-scale crises.
1847.population: All 911 users who live, work, and visit the City of Titusville, FL.
1847.outcome: Improvements in measurable 911 parameters to include tracking emergency response and turnout times, survival rates for medical calls, and reductions in communication delays. Additional metrics include responder wellness indicators such as reductions in stress-related health incidents, system uptime, number of dispatch failures prevented, and improved coordination during disasters as documented in after-action reports.

1316.description: This Project proposes to construct a new Headworks facility equipped with modern screening, grit removal systems, and odor control to effectively intercept and remove coarse and fine debris from the incoming wastewater before it enters the main treatment process. The Headworks process is vital for removing bulky solids in wastewater treatment. Currently, the Cooper City WWTP lacks a Headworks facility, leading to operational challenges of accumulated solids in the surge tank which carry over into wastewater treatment units and complicate the City’s capability to meet regulatory requirements and contribute significantly to the degradation of existing components of the treatment process. The estimated construction cost is $9.3 million. The City submitted a Resilient Florida Grant and federal appropriation ($1.3M) to assist in funding the construction phase. State funding is requested for c
1316.purpose: The specific goal of the funds requested is to prevent the accumulation of solids in surge tanks, mitigate the risk of sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs), ensure the smooth and efficient operation at subsequent treatment stages, and safeguard community health and the environment. Funds will go towards the construction of a new Headworks facility equipped with modern screening, grit removal systems, and odor control system to effectively intercept and remove debris at WWTP.
1316.activities: Maintaining robust infrastructure, including sewer and wastewater systems, is essential and a priority for the people of Florida. Funds will be used for Contractual Services essential for the Construction Phase. This Project will screen out bulky solids at the front of the treatment facility, manage and handle solids more efficiently, and control contaminants and odors so City operators can maintain operations effectively, thereby safeguarding community health and the environment.
1316.direct_services: Currently, during heavy rainfall, the system becomes overwhelmed, leading to backups at WWTP which creates a chain reaction that results in surcharging at lift stations and sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs). This Project will enhance and optimize WWTP services, preventing the accumulation of solids, mitigating the risk of overflows, ensuring smooth and efficient operations and safeguarding of commun
1316.population: All City residents - 34,400. Direct services to citizens include improved WWTP operations, mitigated environmental harms and odors, and reduced SSOs. The 2024 Water and Wastewater Master Plan Update, presented at a City public workshop on March 13, 2025, identified this Project as a necessity to improve efficiency and reduce odors for citizens. Sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs) release untreated wastewater into streets and public spaces. By removing debris that can cause these overflows, headworks
1316.outcome: Benefits include enhanced operational efficiency, odor control, managed excess flow to prevent flooding, reduced plant hazards, reduced SSOs, and enhanced capacity at the WWTP. During heavy rainfall, a headworks process manages and controls high flows of combined stormwater and sewage. This prevents the WWTP from being overwhelmed, which helps avoid upstream flooding and related public health risks. The methodology by which this outcome will be measured includes monitoring the reduced accumulation of solids, intercepted and removed coarse and fine debris, prevented sewer system blockages and equipment damage, and reduced sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs) and property flooding during severe wea

1850.description: This project strengthens stormwater and irrigation resilience at Bill Keller Park in DeBary, protecting nearly 50 homes in Plantation Estates and Woodbound Lakes. Upgrades include new pumps, electrical systems, wind-rated enclosures, and backup power. A dual-source irrigation station using Lake Charles and groundwater improves drought resilience for 15.2 acres, reduces aquifer use and nutrient runoff, and increases flood protection, efficiency, and system reliability. The project is shovel-ready. DeBary applied for a FDEP Resiliency Grant but was not successful.
1850.purpose: The project improves stormwater network within one of DeBary’s most flood-prone areas, particularly the older, poorest residential neighborhoods built before today’s engineering and environmental standards were adopted. The project addresses vulnerabilities identified in the city’s FDEP sponsored vulnerability assessment. The project is shovel-ready and increases flood protection, water efficiency

1851.description: DeBary will implement critical stormwater infrastructure improvements to reduce flooding, protect homes, and enhance water quality in its oldest and lowest-income neighborhoods, originally developed in the 1940s and 1950s. This project replaces outdated culvert systems with modern, efficient pipes and drainage networks designed to manage stormwater more effectively. Additionally, new stormwater retention and treatment ponds will filter runoff before it flows downhill into the adjacent Gemini Springs, one of Florida’s Outstanding Springs, helping to preserve its ecological integrity. By addressing chronic flooding and erosion, the project will prevent the loss of property, including yards and landscaping, that residents have experienced during storms. These upgrades will improve neighborhood resilience, protect public and private investments, and ensure long-term environmental and communi

Improved drainage prevents mold and contaminants from accumulating around homes. 1540.description: The FSU College of Law Election Law Center provides objective, non-partisan, evidence-based analysis of election- related laws, policies, and constitutional issues. It sponsors conferences, lectures, and courses, and assists policymakers and election officials. The center has also provided scholarships and fellowship opportunities for law students seeking to pursue careers in election law, working with the Department of State, FL Elections Commission, and Supervisors of Election. It prepares research including articles, testimony, and publicly accessible websites to disseminate its research, enhance transparency, and increase public confidence in Florida elections.
1540.purpose: The funding will be used to establish and maintain the nonpartisan FSU College of Law Election Law Center to develop objective, evidence-based analysis of election-related legal, constitutional, regulatory, and policy issues.
1540.activities: The Center will hold conferences, workshops, and lectures for law students, practitioners, and the public, as well as educational presentations for election officials. It will conduct research and generate reports and articles on election law issues for use by scholars, election officials, practitioners, and lawmakers. 1540.direct_services: The Center will hold conferences and lectures open to the public, sponsor and create websites such as the Florida Post-Election Audit which are accessible to the public, and publicly disseminate articles and other research prepared by the Center to promote transparency and bolster public confidence in Florida's electoral system.
1540.population: The Election Law Center will serve students, election officials, legislators, scholars, and voters. Each year, dozens of students at FSU College of Law are likely to participate in its various programs, along with hundreds of attorneys (getting CLE through Center programs) and other members of the public attending conferences, lectures, and other events. Thousands of people visit the Center's webpage and online projects the Center co-sponsors.
1540.outcome: The Election Law Center will track the number of students who take affiliated courses and participate in its programs; the number of articles, reports, and other materials the center generates; attendance at the Center's conferences, lectures, and other events; quotes in the media; and opportunities to make educational presentations to, or otherwise assist, government officials. The Center will also rely on feedback from legislators, election administrators, and other officials.

1536.description: Bond Community Health Center proposes to increase access to cancer screenings to Floridians living in rural counties and sparsely populated areas which will result in early detection and increased cure rates. Utilizing a state-of-the-art combination mobile health unit (primary care/3-D mammography unit) Bond will provide prostate, cervical, and colorectal and breast cancer screening along with preventive health care and health education.
1536.purpose: Provide early detection of cancer to enable increased likelihood of cure. Control chronic conditions such as hypertension and diabetes. Increase access to preventive health care services
1536.activities: Physical examinations, 3-D mammograms, other cancer screenings (prostate, cervical, colorectal, etc), evaluation and treatment of chronic conditions such as hypertension and diabetes, laboratory services.
1536.direct_services: Physical examinations, 3-D mammograms, other cancer screenings (prostate, cervical, colorectal, etc), evaluation and treatment of chronic conditions such as hypertension and diabetes, laboratory services.
1536.population: Adults living in rural and sparsely populated areas of the Big Bend. More than 1,000 individuals will be served annually.
1536.outcome: Early screening of cancer and chronic conditions result in improved outcomes, increased cure rates, and decreased end-organ damage. The project will expand FAMU Health and interdisciplinary programs through research, simulation- based learning, and workforce training. Serving both campus and community, the facility will support licensure preparation and partnerships that advance health innovation and opportunity across North Florida.

1526.direct_services: The facility will provide workforce training, career and health fairs, and community education programs that strengthen public health and economic opportunity. It will serve as a hub for healthcare simulation, professional credentialing, small-business engagement, and community wellness activities.
1526.population: The project will serve FAMU students, faculty, healthcare professionals, community residents, and business partners across North Florida. Once operational, the facility is expected to directly serve more than 800 individuals annually through academic programs, community events, and professional training opportunities.
1526.outcome: The project will expand Florida’s healthcare and service workforce, strengthen industry partnerships, and enhance community engagement. Outcomes will be measured by increased program enrollment, credential completion rates, job placement data, number of community participants served, and the facility’s annual economic impact on the region.

The program helps youth avoid hospitalizations, SIPP placements, and foster or justice involvement. Families work with credentialed Family Support Navigators who provide hands-on crisis support, connect youth to clinical services, and coordinate resources to keep families stable and youth safely at home. Each family is paired with a Family Support Navigator—a credentialed peer with lived caregiving experience—who provides hands-on guidance to connect youth to clinical care, coach caregivers, and coordinate across schools, healthcare, and community systems. By combining evidence-based peer support with practical assistance and targeted financial relief, Breakthrough improves family functioning, reduce
1607.purpose: The Breakthrough program seeks to improve outcomes for youth with significant mental health needs by reducing reliance on high-cost, restrictive systems of care. Program goals include decreasing psychiatric hospitalizations, SIPP placements, and involvement in foster care or juvenile justice. Breakthrough aims to increase access to coordinated therapeutic services, strengthen family functioning, and build caregiver capacity to advocate effectively within education, healthcare, and community syst
1607.activities: The Breakthrough program pairs each participating family with a Family Support Navigator, a credentialed peer with lived caregiving experience, who provides individualized guidance and support over approximately six-months. Navigators assist families with applications for benefits, crisis response, and transp
1607.direct_services: Through Breakthrough, families receive intensive peer-based support designed to stabilize crises and strengthen long- term well-being. Family Support Navigators conduct regular home visits, provide individualized coaching, and connect families to therapeutic and community resources. 3365.description: Completion of a rebuilt urgent care center and community health center. A prior facility was torn down to make room for this new facility, which also includes a more broad access to primary & specialty care along with the urgent care services.
3365.purpose: NCH tracks and reports to the state numerous patient data, including volumes, outcomes, and other uniform reported information. This urgent care facility increases access to non-emergent levels of care as well saving transportation pressures by keeping care accessible in isolated communities. By leveraging the latest technologies and educational methodologies, the project endeavors to enhance the quality of education and research within the nursing field, ultimately contributing to the improvement of healthcare outcomes and the development of highly skilled healthcare professionals.

1354.description: Transitions Life Center is a 501c3 whose mission is to provide a safe, caring, and enriching community for adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities (I/DD). We accomplish our daily mission by promoting teamwork, honor, respect, independence, values, and education. These funds will cover the program fees expected to be accrued by the individual attending the program. The cost for one day of programming is $50-$55, depending on the level of care required. Funds would be utilized as "scholarship" funds to help provide attendance opportunities to adults with an I/DD who cannot afford to attend an adult day program due to financial restrictions.
1354.purpose: The funding will provide opportunities for adults with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities the opportunity to attend our day program. Funding will be allocated into a "scholarship" account, which will be granted to individuals who meet the required criteria for attendance and financial assistance with the daily fee.
1354.activities: The funding will provide opportunities for adults with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities the opportunity to attend our day program. Funding will be allocated into a "scholarship" account, which will be granted to individuals who meet the required criteria for attendance and financial assistance with the daily fee.
1354.direct_services: The services provided to adults with an IDD will day programming services for those who need financial assistance in order to attend a day program.
1354.population: The special needs population; specifically adults over the age of 18 that fit our program requirements and have a need for financial assistance in order to attend our day program which further advances their "abilities."
1354.outcome: The benefit of this project would be to have the ability to offer more services to adults with I/DD who may need day program services, but are unable to financially afford it. By attending a day program, caregivers would also have the ability to take a break from the demands of care giving. We can measure the outcome by determining how many TLC members currently have a scholarship to attend and then re-evaluate after 1 year to report how many more Members TLC has acquired and that utilize the scholarship in order to attend.

2994.description: The purpose of the project is to improve traffic safety and traffic flow along Williams Road, west of US 41. In 2025 there was an estimated 59,184 trips per day along US 41 and 6,324 trip per day along this section of Williams Road. The project will include the installation of a traffic roundabout, which would eliminate dangerous left turns, and also extend the turn lanes at US 41 creating better stacking thereby alleviating traffic congestion.
2994.purpose: The purpose of this project is to improve traffic safety and traffic flow along Williams Road, west of US 41. This area has experienced significant traffic congestion leading to high increases of traffic accidents.
2994.activities: The project includes the construction of a roundabout, raised median, and extended turn lanes to eliminate dangerous left hand turns and increase vehicle stacking along US 41.
2994.direct_services: Citizens will see improved traffic safety through the elimination of dangerous left turns. Currently there is a significant number of accidents occur at this intersection. Citizens will see significant efficiencies in traffic flow and increased safety for drivers and pedestrians due to the roundabout and extended turn lanes.
2994.population: The Citizens that live west of US 41 along Williams Road and any citizens and visitors that frequents any of the commercial facilities along Atlantic Gulf Drive will benefit from the project.
2994.outcome: The benefit from the project will be improved traffic safety and the ability to accommodate higher traffic volumes. This will be measured via reduction of accidents and increases in the flow of traffic through the US 41 intersection.

2953.description: Due to the significant population growth in Northeast Florida, there is an urgent demand for skilled healthcare professionals, including CNAs and EKG technicians. CCDS has answered the call with seven health science programs. Funds for this program would increase the number of CNA/EKG certified graduates by removing critical barriers. Funds will ensure students complete the mandatory 40 clinical hours by covering costs (e.g., background checks, transport) and provide industry-grade equipment that mirrors clinical settings and exam standards. This secures certification eligibility and produces workforce-ready healthcare professionals.
2953.purpose: The goal is to increase the number of CNA and EKG certified graduates by removing critical barriers. Funds will ensure students complete the mandatory 40 clinical hours by covering costs (e.g., background checks, transport) and provide industry-grade equipment that mirrors clinical settings and exam standards. This secures certification eligibility and produces workforce-ready healthcare professionals.
2953.activities: Fourth year health science students at all seven schools will receive transportation to clinical sites twice a week. Additionally, students will receive background checks, TB tests, drug screens, and scrubs needed for clinicals. Health science programs will receive industry-grade equipment, such as EKG machines and exam tables, that simulate clinical settings and exam standards.
2953.direct_services: The funds will support 175 students earning their CNA and EKG certifications. Once they graduate, these skilled, certified professionals can fill vacancies, easing staff shortages in hospitals and care facilities. Citizens benefit from improved patient-to-staff ratios and access to timely, high-quality medical services in a rapidly growing region.
2953.population: This program will directly benefit approximately 175 students in their fourth year of health science, seeking certifications in CNA and EKG.
2953.outcome: More students will graduate from our seven health science programs with dual certifications in EKG and CNA. The school district will track the number of students who graduate high school with two certifications, rather than just one certification.

2349.description: Renovation of existing school high school to allow it to serve as a Vocational Trades High School.
2349.purpose: The funds will expand career pathways and education choice opportunities for 116,400 Polk County students by strengthening partnerships between local employers, schools, and community stakeholders. The goal is to increase access to high-quality career exploration, workforce-aligned programs, and postsecondary readiness supports for all students.
2349.activities: Funds will support development of data tracking dashboard with Exponent Education to deliver measurable outcomes and impact for Polk County schools, Polk RiSE scholarships, virtual field trip experiences that connect students to local industries, implementation of Big Picture Learning Initiative, and career-readiness curriculum are all designed to increase high-quality career pathway
2349.direct_services: Providing Career Readiness Curriculum and Virtual Field Trips, an online program allowing for career exploration with real businesses to all Polk High School students. Provision of a career pathways dashboard that will allow all schools to track student progress towards industry certs and pathways. Curriculum for teacher training and scholarships will directly impact Polk County High Schools.
2349.population: Economically, at risk youth, and high school students. Over 100,000 Polk students are expected to be served.
2349.outcome: The expected outcome is an increase in the number of students (116,400) participating in high-quality career pathways, virtual field trips, career readiness curriculum, and Big Picture Learning programming; growth in students completing industry certifications, internships, and pathway-aligned coursework. Outcomes will be measured through a district-wide dashboard (SchooLinks/Exponent Education), certification records, internship tracking (ImBlaze), pre/post curriculum assessments, graduation and attendance data, program participation logs. 2258.description: The inspHire program supports Florida's strategies to reduce incarceration costs and the prison population for sustainable savings. Its goal is to deliver returns by desistence, reducing recidivism, decreasing crime, and breaking cycles of hopelessness. Through reentry services and employment, inspHire improves social determinants of health for returning citizens, fosters economic development, job creation, and the growth of self-sufficient, productive members of society.
