2266.description: Funds would be utilized for expanding the treatment capacity of the existing Regional Surface Water Treatment Plant and increasing the use of associated surface water supplies to maximize the available yield of surface water supplies to meet the growing demands of the Tampa Bay region.
2266.purpose: This project includes expanding the treatment capacity of the existing Tampa Bay Water Regional Surface Water Treatment Plant and increasing the use of associated surface water supplies to maximize the available yield of surface water supplies to meet the growing demands of the Tampa Bay region. The overall objective of the project is to increase Tampa Bay Water's annual average yield of existing surface water supplies by 10 to 12.5 million gallons per day (MGD).
2266.activities: The service provided by this project is an increase in the current surface water supplies that serve as drinking water for member counties of Tampa Bay Water. The project will not change the services provided but rather increase their availability.
2266.direct_services: Direct services provided are safe, potable drinking water that is provided by Tampa Bay Water through its six member governments to more than 2.6 million people in the Tampa Bay Region.
2266.population: The target population for this project are the residents of the six member governments that make up Tampa Bay Water, they include St. Petersburg, Pinellas, Pasco, Hillsborough counties, New Port Richey, and the city of Tampa.
2266.outcome: An improvement in drinking water quantity and resiliency in the regional water supply system is the expected outcome of the project. More specifically, an Increase Tampa Bay Water's (Agency) annual average yield of existing surface water supplies by 10 to 12.5 million gallons per day (MGD). The benefits can be measured through data that documents an increase in average yield of surface water.

2267.description: Security and facility upgrades for courthouse. The primary use of this portion of the funding will be related to the security enhancements, safety corridors, inmate holding areas, sallyport, and other court specific safety features of the overall project. However, these features are integrated into the overall expansion of the courthouse.
2267.purpose: The funds will be used for much needed safety, and security, enhancements for the Robert D. Sumner Judicial Center in Dade City, Pasco County. These enhancements include safety corridors, inmate holding areas, sallyport, and other court specific safety features of the overall project.
2267.activities: The Robert D. Sumner Judicial Center in Dade City, Florida, houses various court services, including criminal and civil proceedings, family and juvenile law, and probate matters. Services include handling adoptions, child custody and support cases, divorces, felony cases, and guardianship. It also processes paperwork for cases in the county court, such as small claims, and provides facilities for jury service. The Pasco County Clerk handles a large volume of court- related paperwork for these ca
2267.direct_services: The Robert D. Sumner Judicial Center provides direct services to citizens including court services for traffic, civil, small claims, and misdemeanor cases, family and probate court services, protection against abuse through injunctions, and access to a legal resource center. Citizens can also find support through victim and witness services and manage jury service responsibilities at this location
2267.population: The Robert D. Sumner Judicial Center serves the citizens of Pasco County, which is part of the broader Sixth Judicial Circuit that also serves Pinellas County. The center's target population is the entire population of Pasco County. The center processes a high volume of cases, covering both felony and misdemeanor criminal cases, as well as civil, family, and other legal matters.
2267.outcome: Much needed safety, and security, enhancements for the Robert D. Sumner Judicial Center in Dade City, Pasco County. Outcome will be measured from the enhancements which include safety corridors, inmate holding areas, sallyport, and other court specific safety features of the overall project.

2271.description: At Quantum Leap Farm (QLF), our mission is to transform lives by harnessing the healing connection between humans and horses through equine-assisted therapies. We offer a robust set of programs that specialize in serving children and young adults with special needs, such as physical, developmental and behavioral. These include: Therapeutic Riding, Hippotherapy, and Special Needs Family Fun Days. Funding to support our programs that serve our youth and young adults with special needs as well as a support Hippotherapy Staff member ($128,700) • (768) Therapeutic Riding sessions • (360) Hippotherapy sessions • (300) Special needs children and families through Family Fun Days • Part-Time Hippotherapy clinician(s) (Occupational Therapist, Physical Therapist or Speech Pathologist) to assist with the facilitation of the Hippotherapy sessions.
2271.purpose: At Quantum Leap Farm (QLF), our mission is to transform lives by harnessing the healing connection between humans and horses through equine-assisted therapies. We offer a robust set of programs that specialize in serving our special needs children for their various needs. These include: Therapeutic Riding, Hippotherapy, and Special Needs Family Fun Days. This funding request will help fill the gap in funding for our programs in the upcoming year.
2271.activities: Quantum Leap Farm will provide Equine-Assisted Therapy Programs and activities especially designed to support the physical, social and emotional well-being of special needs children and their families. All Equine-Assisted Therapy Programs at Quantum Leap Farm are facilitated by qualified therapeutic riding instructors, or licensed and specially certified occupational therapists, speech pathologists or physical therapists.
2271.direct_services: Quantum Leap Farm’s programs for special needs children include an array of equine-assisted therapies including Therapeutic Horseback Riding, Hippotherapy, and Family Fun Days. (Please see attached program descriptions)
2271.population: Quantum Leap Farm’s programs for special needs children and family members serves individuals and families navigating various diagnosis, such as physical, developmental and behavioral challenges. After funding is awarded, we expect to serve over 1,400 individuals a year. Specific data collected will vary from program to program.
2271.outcome: Participants in all programs will self-report via questionnaires. Depending on which program they participate in, they will report on physical and emotional changes, as well as coping skills and on their overall quality of life. Participants in Hippotherapy also follow a goal setting plan to measure progress weekly.

1741.description: This project will replace aging galvanized drinking water mains in the historical area of Tarpon Springs northeast of downtown. This project will be a find-and-fix project to replace up to 5,300 feet (approximately one mile) of aging water lines in historic neighborhoods (some over 100 years old) that are causing water quality and leakage issues. The total project cost is $1,200,000 with the City requesting $600,000 (50%) in State Appropriation Funding.
1741.purpose: This project will replace aging galvanized drinking water mains in the historical area of Tarpon Springs northeast of downtown. The project will be a find-and-fix project to replace up to 5,3000 feet (approximately 1 mile) of aging water lines in historic neighborhoods (some over 100 years old) that are causing water quality and leakage issues.
1741.activities: The residents within this area will be provided with better water quality and decreased leakage issues.
1741.direct_services: These homes will benefit from replacing aging galvanized drinking water mains that affects water quality and leakage.
1741.population: Approximately 220 homes will benefit from this project.
1741.outcome: It is expected that this project will benefit those residents who are affected by poor water quality and leakage issues by replacing aging galvanized drinking water mains.

2652.description: Edward Waters University (EWU) proposes the development of a transformative Living Learning Community Conference Center in Jacksonville's historic New Town community. The all-in-one facility will house 425 additional residential students and serve as a regional hub for academic conferences, community events, and expanded health and senior services. This center aligns with EWU's mission driven commitment to academic excellence, student success, and neighborhood revitalization.
2652.purpose: Construction of a new EWU Living Learning Community Conference Center (LLCC) and EWU Community Walking Path/Track. This project is an investment in Jacksonville's urban core in the heart of the New Town Community. This new facility is designed to serve students, community, workforce and economic development goals. The EWU LLCC will add 425 new residential beds to campus, provide new convention space for institutional, community, and external events, and expand direct services to the local commun
2652.activities: New and Expanded Operational Capacity and Community Access to: Community Health and Wellness Services in the JAX New Town Community. 3047.description: The City of Labelle is scheduled to replace their wastewater treatment facility in the next two years. The City currently utilizes a sprayfield for wastewater effluent disposal located on SR80 near the Caloosahatchee River. As part of the project, the City is requesting funding support to incorporate solids dewatering equipment to the wastewater treatment facility which would assist the City in meeting compliance with higher class biosolids production, and lower disposal costs.
3047.purpose: Pre-construction costs of solids dewatering equipment to the wastewater treatment facility which would assist the City meet compliance with higher class biosolids production, and lower disposal costs.
3047.activities: Funds will be used for pre-construction costs of solids dewatering equipment to the wastewater treatment facility.
3047.direct_services: No direct services to citizens will be paid for by this appropriation.
3047.population: The target population of this project is the entire City of LaBelle - population of 5,222.
3047.outcome: By installing dewatering equipment to the wastewater treatment facility it will allow the City meet compliance with higher class biosolids production, and lower disposal costs. Methodology to measure would be a reduction in disposal costs and permitting requirements.

3368.description: The Fort Myers Salvation Army Co-Occurring Residential Treatment Program delivers comprehensive, integrated mental health and substance use treatment to justice-involved individuals on felony probation. The program will serve individuals under the Florida Department of Corrections. This evidence-based, trauma-informed program is designed to stabilize, rehabilitate, and reintegrate individuals with co-occurring disorders. Upon admission, each resident receives a psychiatric evaluation, diagnosis, and individualized medication management plan, with monthly follow-ups or more frequent sessions as clinically indicated. Direct mental health services are delivered by Qualified Clinicians, including:Weekly one-on-one counseling,weekly mental health-specific group therapy, medication education and monitoring
3368.purpose: The goal of this funding is to increase immediate access to residential mental health and substance abuse treatment for justice-involved individuals, reducing wait times to see community mental health from 6–8 weeks to within 5 days of admission. All while supporting successful community reintegration, family reunification, and decreased reliance on incarceration resulting in improved public safety and cost savings to the Florida prison system.
3368.activities: Participants will receive comprehensive, evidence-based treatment in a structured residential setting that addresses both mental health and substance use disorders. Services include weekly individual counseling, weekly mental health therapy groups, substance abuse education groups, and targeted educational classes focused on employment readiness, budgeting, stress management, and anger management. In addition, all individuals will have bi-weekly appointments with a licensed psychiatrist for ongo
3368.direct_services: Mental health counseling,Substance abuse treatment ,Psychiatric services, Case management,Life skills classes,Health screenings or medication support, Transportation assistance,Family reunification or support services,Job/vocational training all in a residential setting.
3368.population: Felony adult offenders on state supervision with the Florida Department of Corrections who have a mental health and substance abuse diagnosis. The projected amount of people served would be approximately 24 people in a year.
3368.outcome: The Mental Health program is expected to produce measurable improvements in individual and community well-being by stabilizing participants through timely access to psychiatric care, clinical counseling, and substance use treatment. Outcomes include reduced recidivism, improved treatment compliance, enhanced daily functioning, and increased readiness for employment or education. Participants will experience greater emotional regulation, stronger family connections, and reduced reliance on crisis services, while the broader community benefits from safer streets, reduced incarceration costs, and restored productivity from justice-involved individuals who successfully reenter society. This collaboration will allow Champions to utilize portions of under-enrolled schools to extend the reach of Champions’ community-based programs. The project also includes replacing aging buildings at the main campus with one purpose-built facility to house three cornerstone programs; early childhood development, lactation support to build strong parent/child attachment, a 1st through 5th grade in-school programs serving over 15k children per year, and dedicated space for child abuse training for the community, nonprofits, and teachers. Combining strategic use of available school district facilities with a revitalized central campus,
2280.purpose: Champions for Children will use the requested funds to expand and strengthen its community-based programs that prevent child abuse by teaching parents the skills they need to strengthen their families and create safe spaces for thriving children. For the main campus efforts, activities will include demolition of existing buildings, site preparation and foundation work and a construction phase.

Accreditation confirms that our operations, governance, and programs reflect national best practices. By embedding quality, accountability, and improvement into our organizational DNA, Champions ensures that families receive the highest-quality support fostering positive parenting, child safety, and lifelong resilience. 2298.description: The Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office (HCSO) will establish a training center for HCSO's training needs including the HCSO Academy, as well as space for regional training for other agencies. This project will support basic, advanced, and specialized law enforcement and leadership training. This state-of-the-art facility will be a regional training facility for traditional classroom, physical fitness, and scenario-based training to provide the highest quality law enforcement training for both new recruits and experienced personnel.
2298.purpose: HCSO will establish a training center for HCSO's training needs including the HCSO Academy, as well as space for regional training for other agencies. This project will support basic, advanced, and specialized law enforcement and leadership training. This state-of-the-art facility will be a regional training facility for traditional classroom, physical fitness, and scenario-based training to provide the highest quality law enforcement training for both new recruits and experienced personnel.
2298.activities: HCSO will begin renovations to complete a regional training center with spaces for traditional classrooms, defensive tactics, and scenario-based training for HCSO personnel (including the HCSO Academy) and other agencies in the region. An existing building has been identified that will be remodeled and updated to provide the ideal spaces for different types of training for HCSO and other agencies.
2298.direct_services: The proposed regional training center will provide traditional classroom, physical fitness, defensive tactics, and scenario-based training for law enforcement personnel of all experience levels; from new recruits to veteran deputies and officers. This facility will allow law enforcement officers to learn the latest skills in the best environment to provide their communities with the best service.
2298.population: The population served by this project is HCSO’s service population, which is the citizens of and visitors to Hillsborough County, with a population of approximately 1.57 million people.
2298.outcome: The regional training center will allow more training days; both for HCSO personnel and other agencies in the region. The facility will be established to support a full range of training activities, including specialized facilities. This can lead to quicker adoption of new techniques, more offerings of helpful courses, and the possibility to cross-train with other agencies. Logs of the use of the regional training center can be provided, including the number of courses as well as the different agencies using the facility.

2300.description: Construction of a building to house exhibits and programming space for children and adults visiting the St. Augustine Lighthouse & Maritime Museum. The space will be used by the Museum's Education division to provide a full range of educational programs and exhibits highlighting the impact of World War II on Florida and the local community. From protective measures enacted across the state such as blackout orders to the stories of the military experiences of men and women from Florida who traveled the world, these programs will give visitors a better understanding of this watershed moment in the history of our nation and our state. This building will feature engaging exhibits that include artifacts from the Museum's collection alongside stories of those who lived the war first-hand through oral histories and photographs. Our goal is to give the 230,000+ visitors including 5,000 school ch
2300.purpose: Our purpose is to provide a learning space where visitors, including school-aged students, can learn about the experience of World War II in Florida, including the details of how and why it was fought, how Florida contributed to the cause and ultimately its victory, why the war remains a seminal period in Florida history, and inspire a better appreciation of the costs of protecting our freedom across generations through its exhibits and first-hand stories.
2300.activities: Immersive exhibits will include artifacts, photographs, and oral histories about Florida's role in the war. Staff will offer visitors guided tours and programs, space for activities to promote learning for all ages and abilities, sharing first-hand experiences and stories that reinforce a better understanding of the war's impact locally as well on the state and country.
2300.direct_services: The Museum will offer exhibits, programs and tours focused on educating visitors about the contributions of Florida's citizens and leaders throughout the war toward victory over Imperial Japan and Nazi Germany. The Museum's collection contains so many artifacts including letters, photographs, oral histories, uniforms and other items donated by service men and women. Staff will focus on providing p
2300.population: The Museum welcomes over 240,000 visitors per year with roughly 47% of them coming from within the state of Florida. School-sponsored tours of the Museum bring over 5,000 school-aged children to the site as part of the fourth- grade curriculum with other elementary, middle and high school-aged children represented as well. Senior groups also participate in group tours through programs such as Road Scholars through Eckerd College. These visitors desire more in-depth information than traditional v
2300.outcome: The outcome of this project is to provide an educational space to learn about the significant events, stories and impact of World War II, allowing visitors to understand the "why" and "how" of the war. The project will also honor the generation who witnessed the war either by fighting or by making sacrifices to support the war effort. By sharing the personal stories and experiences that the exhibits will provide, visitors will ultimately better understand why this conflict changed the world, our country and our state.

1750.description: VolunteerCleanup.org is an event-management platform that connects volunteers with litter cleanups and provides organizers with the tools and training to run effective hands-on experiences that build awareness of plastic pollution and inspire long-term solutions. In South Florida, over 150 organizers have led 5,000+ cleanups with 125,000+ volunteers, removing more than 1 million pounds of trash from neighborhoods, shorelines, and waterways. This project will 1) expand our platform into 5 additional counties, 2) develop new organizers through micro-grants, training, and supplies, and 3) support existing Miami cleanup organizations.
1750.purpose: VolunteerCleanup.org is an online platform that helps organizers recruit volunteers and manage effective cleanup events. Funding will allow us to engage and educate thousands of Floridians about marine debris through hands-on shoreline, waterway, and neighborhood cleanups. This project will: (1) expand our service area into five additional coastal counties; (2) develop new organizers through micro-grants, training, supplies, and educational materials; and (3) support existing Miami-Dade organize
1750.activities: We will support and expand volunteer cleanups that remove litter and provide firsthand, eye-opening experiences about plastic pollution. These events educate residents, inspire action to reduce waste at the source, and foster neighborhood pride. We will (1) expand programming in Miami-Dade to create more volunteer cleanup opportunities, and (2) expand into five additional coastal counties by providing outreach, micro-grants, training, supplies, and educational materials to help new groups launch
1750.direct_services: Funds will provide citizens with volunteer cleanup opportunities and hands-on training about marine debris. Micro- grants, supplies, and support for organizers will expand access to local shoreline, waterway, and neighborhood cleanups, directly engaging residents in improving and protecting their communities.
1750.population: The target population includes residents across Florida (adults, youth, schools, & civic groups) who benefit from clean neighborhoods and waterways. We expect to serve over 20,000 new citizens statewide through accessible, educational events that also provide student and court-ordered service hours. In Miami, we have supported 150 organizers who engaged over 125,000 volunteers. As we expand into 5 new coastal communities, we will mentor and support 5 groups in each area, each leading 5 cleanups
1750.outcome: This project will improve environmental quality, increase civic engagement, and expand community stewardship. Outcomes will be measured through: (1) cleanup metrics—pounds of debris, number of cleanups, and types of materials collected; and (2) post-cleanup surveys measuring knowledge gains and intentions to reduce single-use plastics. Our most recent surveys show that 66% increased their knowledge of marine debris, 96% want to do more to protect the environment, and 73% committed to using fewer single-use plastics.

2078.description: The City will undertake construction to harden and implement resiliency measures at the Verna Wellfield. Upgrades will protect the drinking water system’s resilience, safeguarding it against weather events and cyber threats ensuring safe drinking water. Planned improvements include replacing underground vaults with above-ground switchgear, installing instrumentation and control systems to relay data to operations centers, and implementing new grounding measures to protect against power surges.
2078.purpose: The Verna Wellfields are a water source owned by the City of Sarasota. It draws water from the Florida aquifer and is pumped to the City’s 12th street treatment plant which supplies drinking water to approximately 57,000 City residents.The wellfield has been in operation since 1966 and is need of various resiliency upgrades. This will prevent power loss and equipment damage that could occur during heavy rain, flooding, hurricanes. Install instrumentation and control systems to relay data to operations center. 2078.direct_services: The direct service to citizens will be the assurance of clean, safe drinking water, even during an extreme weather event.
2078.population: The general public of approximately 57,000 City of Sarasota residents would be the target population.
2078.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome will be to improve drinking water quality. The City of Sarasota Utilities Department is dedicated to enhancing the quality of life for all residents by delivering safe, reliable drinking water. This project will ensure the long-term security of the City’s water supply by implementing improvements that add redundancies and create a more robust, resilient system for continued service. The City will conduct comprehensive vulnerability reporting and risk assessments to measure reductions achieved through this project. Following construction, ongoing reporting will track any outages or equipment downtime to ensure continued reliability and resilience of the system.

1677.description: The project aims to improve stormwater management across flood-prone areas in Hallandale Beach, addressing both localized and broader flood risks. The key locations include: (1) Foster Rd.(Regionally Significant Major Roadway) – 60- inch trunk line; (2) N.W. 7th Ave. – 48-inch trunk line; (3) N.W. 3rd St. – 48-inch trunk line; (4) N. Atlantic Shores Blvd.(Regionally Significant Major Roadway) – 96-inch trunk line; and (5) S.W. 11th Ave.– 48-inch trunk line. These efforts aim to mitigate flooding, and safeguard vital assets, including residential properties, roadways, and evacuation routes.
1677.purpose: This initiative encompasses five critical stormwater capital improvement projects planned for Fiscal Years 2024 - 2026, aligned with the City's Stormwater Management Master Plan. These projects are vital for effectively managing stormwater runoff, mitigating environmental and social impacts, and enhancing community resilience. The focus is on modernizing stormwater infrastructure, reducing flood risks, and safeguarding key assets, including residential properties, roadways, and evacuation routes
1677.activities: The funded activities will focus on stormwater management to reduce flood risks and protect critical assets, including residential structures, roads, and evacuation routes, from potential flood damage. Services include implementing infrastructure improvements, enhancing runoff management, and modernizing systems to ensure resilience and sustainability.
1677.direct_services: The appropriation project will eliminate 26 residential structures from the list of those at risk during a 100-year, 24-hour storm event. The initiative enhances stormwater management services for residents by reducing flood risks, upgrading infrastructure for runoff control, and bolstering protection of homes, roadways, and evacuation routes against potential flood-related impacts.
1677.population: The target population for this project is the general community of Hallandale Beach. The initiative is expected to serve all residents and visitors, benefiting the entire population rather than any specific group.
1677.outcome: Completing this project will eliminate flood risk from 26 homes and improve about 4,164 feet of roadway, including 249 feet of evacuation route. Peak water levels will drop by up to 0.41 ft (100-year storm) and 0.17 ft (25-year storm) in the northeast quadrant, and by as much as 0.81 ft and 1.45 ft near Foster Road and NW 7th Terrace for the respective storms. Flooding in those areas will decrease from indefinite duration to 15.5 hours (Hallandale Beach Stormwater Master Plan).

2618.description: The funding requrest will construct a 16” reclaimed water main across the Halifax River. This new crossing will create a looped system, improve service reliability, and allow for future expansion to the remaining 600 properties on the South Peninsula. It also supports the goals of Senate Bill 64 mandating the elimination of treated wastewater effluent discharges to water bodies within the next decade.
2618.purpose: The funding request improve service reliability, and allow for future expansion to the remaining 600 properties on the South Peninsula. It also supports the goals of Senate Bill 64 mandating the elimination of treated wastewater effluent discharges to water bodies within the next decade.
2618.activities: A firm will be hired to construct the system.

2618.outcome: The proposed 16" reclaimed water will become the primary main connecting utility customers. The City will continue to maintain the current mains as secondary mains to provide redundancy. The City will install and monitor flow meters and pressure gages that will ensure service is optimized to customers on the City's Peninsula. It will also ensure the pipes operate without failure in crossing the Halifax River.

1751.description: The funds for this project would allow for reconstruction of roads, drainage improvements, curb and gutter enhancements, new landscaping, sidewalk improvements and ADA ramps on SW 15th Road from SW 3rd Avenue to SW 11th Street.
1751.purpose: These improvements will increase safety, reduce flooding, improve accessibility, and enhance the overall quality and functionality of the surrounding community.

These include engineering and design work, permitting, roadway reconstruction, drainage upgrades, installation of new curbs and gutters, construction of sidewalks and ADA-compliant ramps, landscaping enhancements, and all required inspections and project management.
1751.direct_services: The project will provide several direct benefits to citizens, including safer and smoother roadways, improved drainage that reduces street flooding, enhanced pedestrian pathways through new sidewalks, better accessibility with ADA- compliant ramps, and upgraded neighborhood landscaping. These improvements will create a safer, more accessible, and more reliable transportation environment for all re
1751.population: The target population for this project includes all residents, businesses, and visitors who travel through or live within the project area. This includes motorists, pedestrians, seniors, individuals with disabilities, and families who rely on safe and accessible infrastructure. Based on local traffic volumes and neighborhood population density, the project is expected to directly benefit several thousand individuals each year by improving roadway conditions, accessibility, and overall public saf
1751.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is improved public safety, enhanced accessibility, and reduced flooding through the reconstruction of roadways, upgraded drainage systems, new curbs and gutters, improved sidewalks, and ADA- compliant ramps. Additional benefits include smoother traffic flow, better mobility for pedestrians and individuals with disabilities, and overall enhancement of neighborhood appearance and infrastructure reliability.

1416.description: The purpose of a welcome center is to provide information and assistance to visitors, whether they are tourists (national and international), new residents, students, researchers, or members of nearby communities. The Deering Estate Welcome Center will serve as a central hub for information, act as a first point of contact to make visitors feel welcome, and will be used to promote programs, exhibits, events, and educational opportunities.
1416.purpose: The Deering Estate Welcome Center will serve as a guest's first exposure to the estate and will set the tone for all visitors. The center will facilitate engagement, generate revenue, promote exhibits, programs, tours, and educational opportunities, and provide opportunities for membership and to sign up for Estate activities. It will also be a platform to highlight community partnerships.

Annually, the Deering Estate offers 23 local artists the opportunity to become an Artist in Residence, 23 cultural programs, and ten art and historical exhibits. Each year, the Deering Estate reaches over 37,000 children with onsite and mobile field study programming. The Estate monitors and protects Diamondback Terrapins, is becoming a bird banding station, and is developing an area of the estate for native plant study and pollinator propegation. The Deering Estate offer Conservation Work

2959.description: This project will dredge and expand the pond and channel areas to increase stormwater capacity, reduce nutrient loading and increase water treatment. Three government entities contribute to the stormwater collection at Shaw Pond: FDOT, Clay County, and the Town of Orange Park.
2959.purpose: The goals achieved will be increased stormwater capacity for 3 entities, FDOT, Clay County and the Town of Orange Park. Additional water quality treatment and improvements will be achieved, as well as nutrient removal and nutrient loading will be reduced.
2959.activities: Water quality improvements, nutrient removal, and stormwater treatment capacity will increase.
2959.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from a reduction in hazardous algal blooms and harmful bacteria in the community.
2959.population: The target population served is roughly 10,000. Expected individuals served are expected to be 2,000.
2959.outcome: The expected benefit is overall health and safety of the citizens. The Town will quantify the amount of organic material removed and monitor nutrient loads before and after the project to measure the outcome.

1763.description: The goal of the project is to continue the City's efforts to reduce the amount of groundwater infiltration entering the city's gravity sewer collection system by installing liners to prevent groundwater from entering the sewer mains. The reduction of groundwater infiltration will also reduce peak wet weather flows to the City WWTP, by minimizing the potential for plant bypasses and reduce nutrient loads to the plant thereby improving the water quality discharged to the Manatee River. Since 2017, the City has invested greater than $10M to line pipes. The Manatee River is a tourism and economic driver for the City and the County; improved water quality to the river improves fishability, eco-toursim, boating, swimming, and development in the region.
1763.purpose: The goal of the project is continue the City's efforts to reduce the amount of groundwater infiltration into the city's gravity sewer collection system by installing liners to prevent groundwater from entering the sewer mains. The reduced flow to the plant will reduce the nutrient load to the plant (nitrogen, phosphorus and suspended solids), improving the quality of the effluent that discharges to the Manatee River. The river is of regional significance and a driver for the economy, development
1763.activities: Various contractors under contract with the city will be utilized to complete cured-in-place pipe lining of leaking vitrified clay gravity sewers throughout the city that are prioritized for lining to eliminate/reduce infiltration and inflow.
1763.direct_services: The citizens in the county will benefit from impacts of improved water quality; fishing, eco-tourism, boating, swimming, development, and the economy by the improvements to the Manatee River.
1763.population: City of Bradenton and Manatee County residents, business owners, and tourists are all better served by a cleaner ecosystem.
1763.outcome: Reduction of groundwater infiltration into the collection system, a reduction flows to wastewater plant, and improved water quality discharges to the Manatee River. The improvements to water quality will have positive impacts on the environment and the economy for the City and the County. Direct measurement at the plant will quantify reduced flows to the plant and discharge testing for nitrogen, phosphorus and suspended solids at the discharge point will serve as the measure of improved water quality.

1764.description: The City of Bradenton is undertaking a feasibility study to evaluate potential improvements to the Bill Evers Reservoir Dam. In recent years, the dam has experienced three separate incidents of brackish river water breaching and backflowing into the reservoir during extreme weather events. The study will assess structural and environmental conditions to identify measures that can enhance the dam’s performance, prevent saltwater intrusion, and improve the resilience of the City’s potable water supply.
1764.purpose: The Bill Evers Reservoir is a vital source of freshwater for the City of Bradenton, providing all of its potable water needs. However, it’s proximity to a brackish tidal river exposes it to storm surge and backflow risk during extreme weather. These events have led to the intrusion of saltwater into the reservoir, compromising water quality. A feasibility study will provide the technical foundation to understand these vulnerabilities and determine practical, cost-effective strategies to strength
1764.activities: Consulting services will be contracted in conjunction with ACOE on the feasibility of repairing, rehabilitating or replacing the dam structure that protects the potable water supply for the City. The plant is currently permitted for up to 12 MGD. Additional supply is NOT being sought, just protection of the existing.
1764.direct_services: The Bill Evers Reservoir is a vital source of freshwater for the City of Bradenton, providing all of its potable water needs. However, it’s proximity to a brackish tidal river exposes it to storm surge and backflow risk during extreme weather. These events have led to the intrusion of saltwater into the reservoir, compromising water quality. A feasibility study will provide the technical foundatio
1764.population: The City of Bradenton +60,000 residents and businesses.
1764.outcome: This initiative supports broader state goals of improving water system resilience and environmental sustainability. By proactively evaluating the dam’s condition and potential improvement options, the City aims to secure a reliable water supply under changing climate conditions. The study will help guide future infrastructure planning and investment decisions that safeguard public health and maintain long-term water resource stability.

1765.description: Parrish Fire District (District) seeks a $3 million appropriation to bridge construction costs for its Station #3 estimated to have a total cost of $7 million, with future development fees anticipated to complete the project. The District serves a historically rural area now experiencing rapid suburban growth. This transformation has outpaced the District’s limited capital resources and station infrastructure. Following the recent construction of Fire Station #2, impact fee reserves are otherwise limited. The new fire station will provide more efficient fire rescue and medical services and maximize response time. It also will lower insurance premiums for homeowners within the District due to the residents proximity to the station and other fire suppression equipment. Additionally, this funding would allow the District to provide immediate aid rather than delayed or non-efficient mutual a
1765.purpose: Local construction funding of the District Station #3 driven by growth and National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 1710 standards, which will: 1) reduce insurance premiums for residents and businesses; 2) provide more efficient Fire Rescue/Medical Services; 3) place a fire station within five-mile response area, maximizing response times and lowering insurance premiums for homeowners; and 4) provide automatic aid rather than delayed or non-efficient mutual aid response to bordering governmen
1765.activities: Quicker response times for fire protection, rapid rescue and medical response to the community. Also, the District will be able to provide more non-emergency functions such as fire prevention to schools & citizens, pre-fire service inspections, and CPR and AED training.
1765.direct_services: Emergency types of responses to fires, hazardous materials, high angle & confined space rescues and all types of medical emergencies for this fast growing community. Additionally, the District will also provide fire prevention education to schools citizens, pre-fire service inspections and CPR/AED training, and other first aid training.
1765.population: All residents and visitors to the area will be serviced along with residents/visitors where the District provides mutual aid. In addition, travelers along I-75, US 301, and State Roads 62 and 64 will be able to receive faster emergency response following an accident. This also helps alleviate congestion on major roads since the District will be able to respond and clear accidents faster.
1765.outcome: Improve quality of education through Fire Prevention education for the youth and adults in Parrish through increased events within the community and protect the general public from harm. Fire Station #3 will assist in providing faster response times thus reducing the exposure of the general public from harm. Following NFPA 1710 Standards and NIST Technical Note 1661 Report on Residential Fireground Experiments will ensure we are maximizing and achieving industry standards for protection of people/property and emergency response care for people.

1645.organization: Harmony and Mental Health Foundation, Inc.
1645.description: The requested funds will support an initiative providing rental supplementation for low-income elderly individuals with chronic mental illness in Miami-Dade County. The goal is to stabilize housing, improve treatment adherence, reduce psychiatric crises, and promote aging in place by integrating mental health services with financial assistance for housing.
1645.purpose: The requested funds will support an initiative providing rental supplementation for low-income elderly individuals with chronic mental illness in Miami-Dade County. The goal is to stabilize housing, improve treatment adherence, reduce psychiatric crises, and promote aging in place by integrating mental health services with financial assistance for housing.
1645.activities: Individual and group therapy, psychiatric evaluations, medication management, and case management will be provided to low-income elderly individuals with mental illness. Funds will support rental supplementation and administrative operations to stabilize housing, improve mental health and prevent institutionalization.
1645.direct_services: The funding will provide housing assistance for low-income elderly with mental illness, while Floridian Health Centers delivers direct services including psychiatric care, therapy (individual and group), and case management to stabilize housing, improve mental health and reduce emergency interventions.
1645.population: The target population served by this project are low income elderly persons who suffer with poor mental health. We expect to serve approximately 101-200 individuals.
1645.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is improved mental health stability among 140 low-income elderly participants measured by a 25% average reduction in depression and anxiety symptoms over six months. The methodology by which this outcome will be measured are standardized clinical tools PHQ-9 (for depression) and GAD-7 (for anxiety) administered at intake, midpoint, and program completion to track changes. Progress will also be documented through case manager reports and client self-assessments.

1756.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1756.description: A comprehensive approach to overpopulation at Miami-Dade Animal Shelter, including (i) boarding long-stay dogs in homes, giving them real-world experiences for a better temporary quality of life, (ii) increasing foster care placements for neonatal cats, (iii) and increasing spay and neuter services.
1756.purpose: The funds requested will reduce shelter overpopulation by improving the quality of life for long-stay dogs through boarding initiatives, expanding foster care placements for neonatal kittens, and increasing accessibility in spay/neuter services across Miami-Dade County.
1756.activities: The project will establish a pet boarding program for long-stay dogs that allows them to gain socialization and behavioral enrichment in real-life setting, provide additional resources to assist caregivers with their duties that include round-the-clock bottle-feeding, constant temperature monitoring, and provision of proper socialization for neonatal cats, and expand the accessibility of free and low-cost spay and neuter services in the county.
1756.direct_services: Miami-Dade County citizens will have access to free and low-cost spay and neuter services; and staff, volunteers, and foster volunteers will benefit from the resources for neonatal cats.
1756.population: The project will serve Miami-Dade County with an estimated population of 2.8 million residents, more specifically, pet owners seeking affordable veterinary care, individuals interested in fostering animals, and Animal Services' staff and volunteers.
1756.outcome: The project is expected to decrease shelter intake and overcrowding and improve animal well-being. Outcomes will be measured through metrics such as reductions in average animal shelter stays, number of neonatal kittens in foster, and the number of spay/neuter surgeries performed.

Should there be an interest in fulfilling this requirement, Twin Oaks possesses 25 years of experience in managing juvenile populations that require residential competency training, prioritizing the safety of both the youth and their respective counties.
1746.purpose: To help alleviate the growing waiting lists for adult forensic beds, Twin Oaks Juvenile Development is prepared to construct an additional cottage dedicated exclusively to direct file youth. 1746.activities: In addition to competency restoration services youth will receive educational, mental health, medical, vocational, and when the need requires will receive transitional services to ensure a smooth return to their home community.

2699.description: The Nassau County Mobility Plan, North Florida Transportation Planning Organization, and the State of Florida approved East Nassau Community Planning Area Sector Plan identify a new Interchange to be located on Interstate 95 between the SR00/A1A Interchange and the US Hwy 17 Interchange. 1585.description: The Age Well Program provides nursing, therapy, social work and physician home visits for low to moderate income seniors who are not eligible for LTC. 1585.purpose: The Age Well Program provides nursing, therapy, social work and physician home visits for low to moderate income seniors who are not eligible for LTC. 3003.description: Erect perimeter fencing at a city owned sports/recreation facility. This fencing will support security and organization during official sporting events to include Babe Ruth baseball, football, softball, soccer and pickle ball.
