Due to the nature of the project and coupled with the FDOT regulatory requirements, turn lanes and partial reconstruction of the existing driveway at the Keystone Heights Airport will be required. The requested funding will ensure the FDOT safety standards are met and transportation engineering design and analysis are compliant.
3007.activities: Traffic study, job growth, economic gains, enriched local opportunities for skilled trade workers and increased infrastructure improvements to the existing community network of economic development.
3007.direct_services: Measured and sustained economic opportunities within a REDI community. The added value to the existing project will create a safe transportation system as an entry point for job growth. The fundamental attributes of the DEO grant will be enhanced to serve the local community and foster economic development within Bradford County and have radius of affect in the surrounding community.
3007.population: Skilled labor force, technical labor, professional services, commercial & general aviation industry, military training operations (FNG), 500-1000 people
3007.outcome: Improved safety and access into the airport thereby reducing vehicular accidents on State Road 100. FDOT Traffic Impact Analysis

3794.description: The City of Lake City is seeking $1 Million in funds to repair the facade of its 114-year-old City Hall building. The facade of the City Hall building has deteriorated to the point that the city has installed a safety net around the exposed bricks as a safety measure against the potential falling debris. Local budgetary resources are insufficient to absorb the project cost. Dept of State, Division of Historical Resource's Special Category Grant, entire grant program was not funded in the FY26 state budget process, leaving the city without the financial resources that were expected due to being ranked on the list.
3794.purpose: The purpose of this project will be to safeguard the City Hall facility and protect public safety by correcting structural deficiencies in the City Hall façade, where deteriorated masonry poses a hazard of falling bricks and compromised façade integrity.
3794.activities: Professional contractors will reset and secure exterior brickwork, harden windows, replace deteriorated mortar joints, and anchor loose sections of masonry, as necessary. A qualified engineering firm will perform engineering services. They will prepare plans, direct work, and inspect the results. They will monitor the progress of work and bring attention to any unforeseen issues.
3794.direct_services: The threat of falling bricks on the adjacent sidewalk will be abated, improving safety for citizens.
3794.population: The project will serve the residents, businesses, and visitors of Lake City, particularly those in the historic commercial district and surrounding areas. The Lake City council meetings take place at City Hall; this project will improve safety for all attendees of meetings. Lake City is home to approximately 12,239 residents.
3794.outcome: The benefits of this project will be additional safety for citizens and reduced liability for the city. The repairs proposed in this project could mitigate a future catastrophic failure of the facade. The methodology used to measure the benefits of mitigating such a failure would be the value of building or the cost of repairs, if such an event occurred.

3017.description: This funding request will be used to construct a 10,000 sq. ft. warehouse that is built up to hurricane standards to store shelter supplies and other items that are used in shelters that is used during declared states of emergency. The past three hurricane seasons have and the influx of evacuees have put more evacuees in on our shelters which requires more supplies. The warehouse can also be used in coordination with DEM and FEMA.
3017.purpose: This funding request will be used to construct a 10,000 sq. ft. warehouse that is built up to hurricane standards to store shelter supplies and other items that are used in shelters that is used during declared states of emergencies. The past three hurricane seasons have impacted Columbia County, and the influx of evacuees have created the need for more supplies in on our shelters. The warehouse can also be used in coordination with DEM and FEMA.
3017.activities: The funds will construct a warehouse for supplies to be stored for emergency shelters during declared state of emergencies.
3017.direct_services: The warehouse will allow for a more efficient emergency response before and after hurricanes.
3017.outcome: Columbia county can mobilize resources faster before after a hurricane or other emergency. Having the warehouse will also support coordination with state and federal partners.

2703.description: This program will establish an effective innovation pipeline in North Florida to accelerate startup formation, technology transfer, and commercialization in areas such as In-Space Biomanufacturing and advanced materials. The FAMU-FSU College of Engineering will partner with the Mayo Clinic Berg Innovation Exchange and Cecil Spaceport to provide structured innovation and entrepreneurship training, mentoring, and prototype development support.
2703.purpose: An effective innovation pipeline will be established in North Florida to accelerate startup formation, technology transfer and commercialization, ultimately strengthening regional innovation and advancing high-impact technologies.
2703.activities: The FAMU-FSU College of Engineering will partner with the Mayo Clinic Berg Innovation Exchange and Cecil Spaceport to provide structured innovation and entrepreneurship training, mentoring, and prototype development support.
2703.direct_services: Prospective and existing entrepreneurs will be provided services and mentorship related to startup formation, technology transfer, and commercialization.
2703.outcome: Increased economic activity as measured by new startups, technology transfer (inventions and patents) and commercialization in North Florida, in particular in areas such as In-Space Biomanufacturing and advanced materials.

1579.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
1579.description: Programming to increase public awareness and education on the issue sex trafficking and exploitation, provide anti-sex trafficking education to youth/students and adults to prevent the commercial sexual exploitation of children, expand outreach and services to victims on the streets and in jails, increase/enhance victim restoration services available to sex trafficking survivors in the Sarasota and Tampa Bay areas.
1579.purpose: End sex trafficking in Florida. Increase public awareness to the issue sex trafficking and exploitation, educating the public regarding services available for sex trafficking victims, conduct anti-sex trafficking education to prevent the commercial sexual exploitation of children and youth, increase outreach and services to sex trafficking victims on the streets and in jails, and increase and enhance victim treatment and restoration services available to survivors of sex trafficking both locally
1579.activities: Anti-human trafficking programming to raise public awareness, prevention education to end commercial sexual exploitation of children/youth, increased street based victim outreach & support, court diversion program for victims, specialized assessment and trauma resolution therapy provided by licensed professionals to victims in safehouse treatment programs, trauma informed advocacy, support and case management to victims "on the streets" as identified and referred by law enforcement, enhanced coo
1579.direct_services: Public awareness, education, prevention curriculum to school-age students, adults, street outreach, victim advocacy,community & jail-based victim support groups, trauma informed case management, court diversion program, linkage to community resources. Residential clinical & victim restoration services, intensive training to other anti-sex trafficking nonprofits increase statewide capacity.
1579.population: Victims of sex trafficking and sexual exploitation, at-risk youth, elementary, high school students, university/college students, persons with poor mental health, persons who are jobless, economically disadvantaged, homeless, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, and the general public, community groups, churches, other agencies. >400 victims are expected to be served. In addition, >1,400 youth ages 5-17 at risk of being sex trafficked are anticipated to be educated with prevention curricu
1579.outcome: Project targets root causes of criminal behavior in sex trafficking victims including but not limited to prostitution, drug related offenses and gang-affiliated charges. Upon graduation of our program, 87% of our clients do not return to their previous life in the streets. Improve the physical health of sex-trafficking survivors with access to dental and medical care. Trauma therapy to improve the mental health of clients related but not limited to: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, Depression and Anxiety, Bi-Polar Disorder, and Cognitive Dysfunction. Reduce substance abuse with services including clinical counseling, weekly Narcotics/Alcoholic Anonymous meetings, and group therapy sessions. I

2708.description: Rapid In-space biomanufacturing of Cancer organoid models will be used for high throughput drug screening based on tumor growth, structure, and gene expression. Cancer organoid experiments, including those for Glioblastoma Multiforme, will link Mayo oncologists modeling tumor evolution with engineers creating miniaturized, sensor-equipped organoid culture modules compatible with Intuitive Machines’ Zephyr platform, enabling quantification of tumor growth, structure, and gene expression in both ground based systems and in true microgravity, and immediate recovery at Cecil Spaceport and analysis at Mayo.
2708.purpose: Rapid In-space biomanufacturing of Cancer organoid models will be used for high throughput drug screening based on tumor growth, structure, and gene expression.
2708.activities: Cancer organoid experiments will link Mayo oncologists modeling tumor evolution with engineers creating miniaturized, sensor-equipped organoid culture modules compatible with Intuitive Machines’ Zephyr platform, enabling quantification of tumor growth, structure, and gene expression in both ground based systems and in true microgravity, and immediate recovery at Cecil Spaceport and Mayo analysis.
2708.direct_services: This project will benefit Florida citizens by advancing novel tumor treatments.
2708.population: This project has the potential of benefiting all Florida citizens who require tumor treatment.
2708.outcome: This project will advance tumor detection, quantification of tumor growth and treatment. The research will be conducted, at the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering and the Jacksonville Mayo Clinic, with the application of state-of- the-art medical technologies and standards.

2147.description: This project involves the purchase and installation of an intelligent Emergency Vehicle Preemption (EVP) system at 16 intersections along the highly congested Indiantown Rd corridor, a critical state roadway. By providing a "green light" to responding fire rescue units, the technology clears traffic to significantly reduce emergency response times and prevent dangerous intersection collisions. This life-saving initiative enhances the safety of first responders and the public, improves overall traffic management, and leverages ongoing state investments to create a safer, more efficient roadway.
2147.purpose: To enhance public safety and improve traffic flow on the congested Indiantown Road corridor by installing an intelligent traffic signal preemption system. This project will reduce emergency response times, decrease the risk of intersection collisions, and protect first responders, directly aligning with Florida's goal of modernizing traffic management technology. By reducing emergency response times, this project will improve patient outcomes for time- sensitive emergencies (stroke, heart attack
2147.activities: Funds will be used for the procurement and installation of Emergency Vehicle Preemption hardware and software at 16 signalized intersections on Indiantown Road. This includes equipping emergency response vehicles with corresponding in-vehicle communication units. The project will provide a direct, tangible improvement to public safety services.
2147.direct_services: The project provides direct public safety benefits with faster and more reliable emergency medical and fire response. The system also enhances protection for first responders, enabling them to reach residents in need more quickly and without undue risk, thereby strengthening emergency services for the entire community.
2147.population: The target population for this project is approximately 78,000 people which includes all residents of the Town of Jupiter, daily commuters traveling through the Town, and visitors who rely on safe and efficient emergency response while in the community. Overall, the project is expected to serve more than 4,000 individuals per year through improved emergency response and safer transport of patients.
2147.outcome: This project will decrease intersection clearance time for emergency vehicles; improve emergency response times, improve patient outcomes for time-sensitive emergencies (stroke, heart attack, cardiac arrest, serious trauma), reduce property damage from fire, and improve traffic signal recovery time post-preemption event. Outcomes will be measured by system analytics and fire rescue report data analytics that compare future outcomes against baseline data to demonstrate improved overall response times, safety, and patient outcomes.

2099.description: The Town of Jupiter and Palm Beach County have partnered on a joint initiative to improve traffic safety, reduce congestion, and enhance mobility at a critical intersection serving both jurisdictions. Through this collaboration, the partners seek funding to support the design, permitting, and construction of a new traffic signal and corresponding intersection improvements that will enhance roadway efficiency and promote safer travel for motorists, cyclists, and pedestrians.
2099.purpose: The funds requested will specifically be used to construct a new traffic signalized intersection improvements of the Central Boulevard and Toney Penna Drive intersection. This will achieve the goal of improving motorist and pedestrian safety by reducing the risk of crashes, enhancing traffic flow, and providing safe, accessible crossings. Ultimately, the project aims to reduce congestion, prevent accidents—including serious injuries and fatalities—and improve overall mobility and quality of life
2099.activities: Procurement & Contracting - Conducting bidding processes and contracting qualified construction firms to perform the work. Construction - Installing traffic signal infrastructure including poles, signal heads, detection systems, turn lane modifications, pedestrian crosswalks, and ADA-compliant ramps. Project Management & Coordination.
2099.direct_services: The project will improve traffic safety, enhance traffic flow, and efficiency for emergency response.
2099.population: The traffic volume is approximately 32,000 vehicles per day and 200 pedestrians/bicyclists per day.
2099.outcome: The project is expected to significantly improve safety and mobility at the intersection of Central Boulevard and Toney Penna Drive by: Reducing the number and severity of traffic crashes including preventing fatalities and serious injuries; Enhancing pedestrian safety with signalized crossings and ADA-compliant infrastructure; Decreasing vehicle delays and congestion, improving overall traffic flow; Supporting emergency vehicle access through better traffic control.

1660.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1660.description: The construction of this facility will replace the aging agriculture facilities built in 1950. The facility would be constructed to serve as a natural disaster staging facility for local governments and post-storm recovery efforts by FPL. It will also be used for educational promotion of the agricultural fair for youth. The facility would also be used year-round to support community events, increase tourism, as well as speed recovery from natural disaster.
1660.purpose: The facility will be constructed to serve as a natural disaster staging facility for local governments and post-storm recovery efforts. The facility will also be used by the community and for the promotion of the agricultural fair. The facility would replace an aging facility that was piecemealed together over 75 years and damaged by Hurricane Milton.
1660.activities: During states of natural disaster, the facility (and grounds) will be used by FPL for restoring services to the community. It will allow for housing on-site workers thereby speeding restoration services. The facility is also central to the display and exhibition of youth projects for the annual Sarasota County Fair as well as other events, businesses, and groups that use the facility.
1660.direct_services: The facility will be available for citizens use for activities aligning with the mission of the association per state statute. The use by FPL will speed restoration of services to all Sarasota County citizens as well as in Manatee and Charlotte counties. It can also be used to support regional statewide natural disasters by staging appropriate emergency services and utilities.
1660.population: The target population is the community at large. It will serve over 500,000 people annually through the fair, activities, and storm related services.
1660.outcome: The benefit of the project is to have a facility that will withstand a natural disaster, serve the community in the response as well as privide a centerpiece for the Sarasota County Fair. The methodology by which this outcome will be measured will be by the increased utilization and economic impact in Sarasota.

3071.description: The extended fixed pier, wave attenuator and floating dock increases and protects boat access and access for anglers. Associated amenities available for recreational boat users are shore-side accommodations for visiting boaters include picnic areas, manatee viewing area as allowed per Manatee Protection Plan , City accommodations and significant historical and natural destination points. The project will complete construction of the Pier Extension and provide additional facilities for boaters.
3071.purpose: The fully constructed pier and boat access will facilitate an increased number of cruises per year which will contribute to the enrichment of Green Cove Springs economic development making it a highly anticipated destination of Northeast Florida. Additional access for anglers and recreational boaters will also be provided. The new floating dock will facilitate additional recreational vessels. The new fixed pier provides additional opportunities for anglers.
3071.activities: This appropriation will assist with the construction of the remainder of the project which will double the recreational boat access capacity, add access to anglers and greatly improve and protect the facilities from further damage. Many other boaters from Clay and neighboring counties use the pier and floating docks regularly throughout the year with many boaters being turned away during special events and periods of high demand.
3071.direct_services: This appropriation will assist with the construction of the remainder of the project which will double the recreational boat access capacity, add access to anglers and greatly improve and protect the facilities from further damage. Many other boaters from Clay and neighboring counties use the pier and floating docks regularly throughout the year with many boaters being turned away during special e
3071.population: 20,000 plus Target population is all ages who are looking for opportunities to boat and fish.
3071.outcome: The extended fixed pier, wave attenuator and floating dock increases and protects boat access and access for anglers. Associated amenities available for recreational boat users are shore-side accommodations for visiting boaters include picnic areas, manatee viewing area as allowed per Manatee Protection Plan , City accommodations and significant historical and natural destination points. The project will complete construction of the Pier Extension and provide additional facilities for boaters.

3298.description: Statewide initiative to give every traditional Florida high school student access to immersive 360 virtual tours of all 42 Florida colleges and universities. Using patented technology, we will create high-quality virtual campus experiences and distribute one VR headset to each of Florida’s ~550 traditional public high schools. Students will be able to borrow headsets through their guidance counselors to explore every Florida college/university—solving the problem of travel costs that prevent many from seeing their options in person. Each headset will also include free educational VR content in anatomy, chemistry, math, and more, bringing modern technology into every school. Districts can choose to expand their VR offerings locally by purchasing additional headsets.
3298.purpose: Give every Florida high school student access to immersive 360 virtual tours of all 42 Florida colleges and universities. Using patented technology, we will create high-quality virtual campus experiences and distribute one VR headset to each of Florida’s ~550 traditional public high schools. Students will be able to borrow headsets through their guidance counselors to explore every Florida college/university—solving the problem of travel costs that prevent many from seeing their options in perso
3298.activities: Filming 360 degree virtual tours of all 42 Florida colleges and universities. Tech support and customer service, distribution of headsets statewide.
3298.direct_services: Allowing for the opportunity of every high school students to take a virtual campus tour of Florida's number one ranked higher education system.
3298.population: Any and all Florida high school students interested in attending one of Florida's colleges or universities. 500,000 plus.
3298.outcome: This project will allow students to make an informed decision of what college or university they wish to attend in Florida. It is providing an opportunity for high school students who cannot afford or do not have the time to make site visits to all our higher education institutions. It puts the opportunity right in their hands to make an informed decision on what is best for their future. We will collect data and report back to the state how many campus visits are utilized per high school.

2660.description: This request would allow for a plans update and all necessary pre-construction activities, along with right-of-way acquisition, that will accelerate the future widening of State Road 501 from Michigan to Industry Rd. This critical regionally significant corridor infrastructure improvement will enhance traffic flow, improve safety, and support regional economic growth. This project will bring significant benefits by improving public safety through congestion relief and serious injury and fatality crash reduction, while enhancing regional mobility.
2660.purpose: The appropriations request would allow FDOT to advance pre-construction activities in an effort to accelerate the delivery of SR501 to widen from Michigan to Industry Road, which will enhance traffic flow, improve safety, and support regional economic growth as a new multimodal hub is developed. This project will bring significant benefits by improving public safety through congestion relief and serious injury and fatality crash reduction, while enhancing regional mobility.
2660.activities: All necessary planning, plans update, including right of way acquisition.
2660.direct_services: The SR 501 Curve expansion project will directly benefit residents by reducing daily traffic congestion, improving commute times, and enhancing roadway safety through wider lanes and upgraded intersections. It will also provide new sidewalks and bike paths, giving residents safer options for walking and biking within their community and increase accessibility to Cocoa's new multimodal hub.
2660.population: The general public to include residents and business owners along the corridor and tourists commuting to Port Canaveral and other nearby hubs.
2660.outcome: This project will improve transportation by reducing traffic, it will increase economic activity, increase tourism, and create immediate job opportunities. These benefits can be measured through traffic counts, economic activity, visitor counts, and job data.

1864.description: The City of Palmetto continues its efforts to maintain compliance with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) and other regulatory agencies. The primary objective of these is implementing lining program of the existing aging sanitary sewer piping network City-wide and to eliminate inflow and infiltration (I&I) thus reducing the potential for Sanitary Sewer Overflows (SSO’s). This will improve overall water quality by reducing potential discharges into nearby estuaries, wetlands and bays including the Manatee River, Terra Ceia Bay and ultimately the Gulf of America.
1864.purpose: The City will hire a contractor who specializes in Sanitary Sewer pipe lining. Specific activities will include lining existing sanitary sewer pipes which are damaged to ensure future overflows are minimized or completely eliminated. The end result of the lining process will create new infrastructure and increase the overall longevity of the sewer system.
1864.activities: This will improve overall water quality by reducing potential discharges into nearby estuaries, wetlands and bays including the Manatee River, Terra Ceia Bay and ultimately the Gulf of America. Also reduce the possibility of unwanted sanitary sewer overflows.
1864.direct_services: The sanitary sewer lining process will improve overall water management through elimination or reduction of Sanitary Sewer Overflows (SSO's)
1864.population: The entire population of the City which is over 13,000 residents.
1864.outcome: The sanitary sewer lining process will improve overall water management through elimination or reduction of Sanitary Sewer Overflows (SSO's). Improved water quality for nearby water bodies. Metrics include: Number of SSO's that are reported on an annual basis and especially during wet weather events. Water quality testing.

3335.description: Approximately 180 parcels within the City of Miami Gardens have no sewer service but are located in areas which abut available sewer infrastructure. These properties are currently served by septic tanks. The purpose of this project will be to connect these properties to the existing sewer infrastructure which are in close proximity to the properties. The project will involve a pubic sewer lateral installation phase and a private plumbing and septic abandonment phase.
3335.purpose: The purpose of this project will be to connect these 180 properties to the existing sewer infrastructure which are in close proximity to the properties. Currently these properties are being served by septic tanks. The project will involve a public sewer lateral installation phase and a private plumbing and septic abandonment phase.
3335.activities: The activities and services that will be provided with these funds is to convert 180 properties from septic tanks to existing infrastructure.
3335.direct_services: The direct services provided to citizens is to remove them from septic tanks.
3335.population: The target population are those residents within the city of Miami Gardens that are on Septic tanks. The individuals expected to be served are the 180 on septic tanks.
3335.outcome: Protect the general public by eliminating septic system backups which are inconvient, unsanitary, and hazardous to the health of the public. This will be measured by the number of septic tanks removed and sampling of groundwater and surface water. Improving wastewter management allowing for safe transport of wastewater for proper treatment. This will be measured by the number of new parcels connected to sewer systems. Improving surface water quality by eliminating the occurrence of septic tank leaks which contaminate groundwater.

2385.organization: Voices for Children of Broward County
2385.description: The Tri-County Child Welfare Collaborative serves as a safety net for children in foster care across Broward, Palm Beach, and Miami-Dade counties. Navigators provide case management, advocacy, and resource linkage in shelter and problem-solving court hearings and through community partners. Working alongside the 17th Circuit Court Judges, ChildNet, and local service providers, the Collaborative ensures that children’s essential needs are met without delay, strengthens placement stability, and prevents crises. This coordinated approach reduces deeper involvement in the child welfare and juvenile delinquency systems while improving long-term safety, stability, and well-being for vulnerable children.
2385.purpose: The Collaborative serves as a safety net for children in foster care across Broward, Palm Beach, and Miami-Dade. Navigators provide case management and resource linkage in shelter and problem-solving court hearings and through community partners to meet urgent needs, strengthen stability, prevent placement disruptions, and reduce deeper system involvement.
2385.activities: Navigators provide case management, advocacy, and resource support for children in foster care and caregivers across Broward, Palm Beach, and Miami-Dade. Services include support in shelter and problem-solving court hearings and through community partners to meet urgent needs, strengthen stability, and prevent placement disruptions.
2385.direct_services: Children in foster care and caregivers will receive direct case management, advocacy, and resource linkage to meet essential and normalcy needs. Navigators will assist with housing, transportation, education, and enrichment supports, ensuring stability, safety, and access to opportunities across Broward, Palm Beach, and Miami-Dade.
2385.population: Children currently in care, at risk of entering care, and those who have aged out across Broward, Palm Beach, and Miami-Dade counties who are involved in or at risk of involvement in the dependency and/or juvenile delinquency systems.
2385.outcome: The goal of the project is to strengthen stability, safety, and well-being for children in foster care across Broward, Palm Beach, and Miami-Dade. Outcomes will be measured through Navigator case records, court and CBC data, and partner feedback showing reduced crises, stronger placements, and improved access to essential supports.

2557.description: The Sarasota Manatee Jewish Housing Council is a high-risk Jewish senior facility that cares for a vulnerable population. To provide a safe and secure campus for residents, staff families and visitors, we must harden the entrances to two buildings with hurricane resistant glass and bollards. To efficiently monitor the 27-acre campus we will add security cameras and exterior lighting in the parking areas and on the sidewalks that surround the resident buildings.
2557.purpose: The goal would be to secure the two buildings on this high-risk Campus with lights, security cameras, addong bollards at main building entrance, reinforcing the sliding glass entry doors and upgrading the first floor access doors on each building. The buildings have multiple entrances. The Kretzmer Center, inside Kobernick House, would be a target of antisemitic hate crimes as it serves as the central location for Jewish religious services and cultural gatherings.
2557.activities: We will construct install exterior security cameras and additional lights in the parking areas outside each wing of Kobernick House, install bollards at the circle drive of each building to deter vehicular assault, install reinforced hurricane glass on each building entrance to provide an additional barrier for attack or hurricanes, and upgrade the multiple entry doors in each wing with security doors to prevent intrusion.
2557.direct_services: Provide rehabilitation therapy, skilled nursing services, memory/dementia care, assisted living and independent living services all within a safe and secure environment. By securing the buildings, the cultural activities and programs will increase their service to the community, inviting the community to participate without fear of threat or attack. We welcome over 5000 people annually on campus.
2557.population: Residents, Administrative staff, Nursing staff, aides, families, and community members who visit the campus to attend Jewish holiday events and celebrations. Over 5,000 visitors who come to the campus annually.
2557.outcome: By providing additional hardening of the buildings on campus, cameras and other safety features, our campus will be a more secure site for the many people that live, work and visit. Therefore, leading to higher job satisfaction, preventing harm to residents, families, staff and guests, and allowing us to stop intruders and those looking to carry out hate crimes.

1800.description: The Florida Council on Economic Education (FCEE) was founded in 1975 by the Florida Council of 100 to improve economics and financial literacy education across the state. The FCEE, which collaborated with the Florida Department of Education to write current state standards in personal finance and assisted in the adoption of the course textbooks, works with a vast network of Florida educators and university-based Centers for Economic and Financial Education. State funding will allow FCEE to distribute 50,000 financial literacy workbooks to Florida teachers and students, increase the capacity of FCEE's Learning Management System platform with impactful and relevant content including a cross section of materials to address differentiated learning techniques, and enhance the portal’s ability to provide materials accessible to teachers, parents and students across the state based on Florida l
1800.purpose: Since 2022, financial literacy has been required for Florida high school graduation, helping students make informed decisions and build financial security. State funding will enable FCEE to expand online access for students, teachers, and parents to lesson plans, supplemental materials, and resources that meet state standards for personal financial literacy and distribute 50,000 workbooks—supporting over 200,000 students expected to complete the required coursework in 2026–27.
1800.activities: The FCEE will print 50,000 financial literacy workbooks to be distributed to Florida teachers and students. These funds will also be used for an expansion of the FCEE online portal of best-practices and classroom resources including video production, pre and post testing, interactive modules, career and technical programming with an emphasis on career readiness, one-on-one teacher coaching by university professors and master teachers, and forums for sharing best practices thus affording more acc
1800.direct_services: Through this funding, the FCEE will expand access for Florida's educators to lesson plans, supplemental materials, and online resources in order to fulfill the state mandate for the personal financial literacy coursework. Educators will also have access to on demand professional development workshops and one-on-one coaching sessions teaching them to develop robust courses and learn how to tailor t
1800.population: Target population includes teachers and students of all learning levels and ages, parents seeking information for their families, and community groups focused on personal finance education. Over 50,000 people are anticipated to be served.
1800.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is a measurable increase in teachers’ financial literacy competencies and access to high-quality instructional resources statewide. Through the expansion of our Financial Freedom resource distribution and the enhancement of our online resource platform, we anticipate reaching over 80% of Florida’s school districts. By leveraging our existing educator network and university-based Centers for Economic and Financial Education, the project will provide teachers with standards-aligned materials, digital professional development modules, and student- centered tools that promote applied financial learning.

1781.description: Reef Relief is seeking funds to expand and enhance our Coral Reef Conservation Program (CRCP). Funds will be used to broaden the reach of our educational programs. The Discover Coral Reefs School Program, spring and summer programs will raise awareness and educate consumers, providing educational messaging to students, adults, and tourism in Florida.
1781.purpose: We are requesting funding to support our Coral Reef Youth Education Program. This program places a special focus on youth education as an important, initial step in saving endangered marine ecosystems through two main components, our Discover Coral Reefs School Program (DCRSP) and our Coral Camp for Kids program.
1781.activities: Our Discover Coral Reefs School Program offers over a dozen marine science topics taught in interactive classroom presentations supplemented with question-and-answer sessions and related activities. Reef Relief also offers a unique educational opportunity through our Coral Camp for Kids and Reef Explorer Coral Camp Programs.
1781.direct_services: Students Pre-Kindergarten through graduate level will be empowered to make informed decisions. They will gain experiences and snorkel skills from visiting the coral reef. As well as life skills regarding decision making, critical thinking, and resource partitioning. Residents will experience better quality of life from decreased pollution. Tourism will have higher quality experience elevating the
1781.population: The Discover Coral Reefs School Program, spring and summer programs, target students aged Pre-Kindergarten through graduate level. While we will target approximately 12,000 students worldwide through in person and virtual learning, there will be a special emphasis on students, adults, and tourists, specifically those located in Florida counties directly impacted by the Florida Barrier Reef.
1781.outcome: Participants in the Discover Coral Reefs Middle School Program and spring and summer programs are pre and post tested. Every year, we aim to stay in line with or increase the retention rates for both programs. This is a way to not only gauge the success of our programs, but to determine the effectiveness of our teachings. We are also starting to see program alumni and students graduate and go on to pursue marine conservation fields.

1840.description: Requested funds will replace and upgrade approx. 2.25 miles of undersized water mains to 8in and 12in diameter, ensuring improved water quality for customers. Leak detection will identify aging mains for replacement, completing the replacement of the most urgent segments in Council District 3. These upgrades will enhance water conservation, reduce water loss, improve fire flow and protection, ensure compliance with Florida's Lead & Copper Rule Revision, and provide efficient water flow.
1840.purpose: Requested funds will replace and upgrade approx. 2.25 miles of undersized water mains to 8in and 12in diameter, ensuring improved water quality for customers. Leak detection will identify aging mains for replacement, completing the replacement of the most urgent segments in Council District 3. These upgrades will enhance water conservation, reduce water loss, improve fire flow and protection, and ensure compliance with Florida's Lead & Copper Rule Revision, and provide efficient water flow.
1840.activities: Requested funds would be used for the design and replacement of undersized/aged water mains (currently 6-inch) to 8-inch to 12-inch water mains along a 2.25-mile stretch within the City of Homestead.
1840.direct_services: Thousands of residents will enjoy improved water quality.
1840.population: The general public will be served by this project and will serve thousands of residents.
1840.outcome: The project will improve drinking water quality by enhancing system capacity, reducing pipe corrosion, and ensuring the consistent delivery of clean, safe water to customers. The benefit will be measured by performing regular water quality tests, tracking reductions in contaminant levels, monitoring improvements in water pressure and flow, and analyzing customer feedback on water quality.

1960.description: Forgotten Coast K9 is committed to ending veteran and first responder suicide through the use of service dogs. This funding will be used to complete construction of the area's first service dog training facility for veterans and first responders. This will allow us to train dogs and provide mental health care in a safe and comfortable environment.
1960.purpose: Forgotten Coast K9 is committed to ending veteran and first responder suicide through the use of service dogs. This funding will be used to complete construction of the area's first service dog training facility for veterans and first responders. This will allow us to train dogs and provide mental health care in a safe and comfortable environment.
1960.activities: Funds will be used for the construction of our training facility, offices, and student housing. The funds will also provide for all permitting, engineering and design, construction oversight.
1960.direct_services: Our program is a 26-30 week program. We provide the dog and all training and equipment needed to make a successful partnership between student and dog. There will also be a mental health consultant available to the students while on campus.
1960.population: Veterans and first responders suffering from PTSD and other ailments due to their service. We hope to serve in excess of 800 persons during our tenure at this location.
1960.outcome: We expect to reduce suicidal ideation among our students, along with reduced substance abuse.

1834.description: This project enhances the security and reliability of Miami-Dade County’s critical water and wastewater infrastructure. Funding will support improved access-control systems, expanded CCTV coverage, and strengthened perimeter security at treatment facilities, wellfields, and pump stations to prevent unauthorized access and system disruptions. These upgrades protect against service interruptions and environmental risks, ensuring continuous delivery of safe drinking water and reliable wastewater services for the community.
1834.purpose: Funds will improve water and wastewater management by enhancing the security and reliability of critical infrastructure systems. Security upgrades—such as access controls, CCTV, and perimeter security—will prevent unauthorized access and damage to treatment facilities, wellfields, and pump stations, reducing the risk of service interruptions or environmental contamination. Ensuring the protection of our facilities is critical to maintaining the uninterrupted delivery of services.
1834.activities: Activities and services will focus on enhancing security infrastructure and technology to safeguard the continuity of essential water and wastewater services. This includes strengthening facility access controls, expanding surveillance capabilities,and perimeter security.
1834.direct_services: The requested funds will provide Miami-Dade County WASD with the necessary tools to protect and prevent its infrastructure from threats, support first responders, and ensure the continuity of vital water and wastewater services. This project aligns with statewide priorities of public safety, infrastructure protection, and emergency preparedness.
1834.population: Residents of Miami-Dade County, benefiting more than 2.8 million people, including the local community within the project area.
1834.outcome: Outcome: Reduced incidents of unauthorized access, theft, vandalism, and unplanned operational shutdowns at water and wastewater facilities—ensuring uninterrupted service delivery, public safety, and environmental protection. Measurement: Year-over-year decreases in security breaches and service disruptions, along with reductions in unplanned shutdowns and emergency repair costs—tracked through operational, maintenance, financial, and compliance metrics.

1959.description: Super resolution microscopy is a cutting-edge technology to visualize intricate details within cells gaining a deeper understanding of cellular mechanisms, identify therapeutic targets and develop effective treatments. Combined with high throughput imaging it enables to screen thousands of compounds, assess effects on cellular processes, and identify promising candidates for further development.
1959.purpose: Acquiring super-resolution microscopy and high-throughput imaging equipment will equip researchers with advanced tools to conduct discovery-based research at its fullest potential. These technologies will be utilized by investigators studying inflammation across various diseases, with a particular focus on conditions relevant to Florida’s aging population, including infectious diseases, and viruses that are linked to diseases such as Cancer and Alzheimer's disease.
1959.activities: Purchase of a super-resolution upgrade to a confocal microscope and a high throughput imaging system to enhance research capabilities in the Florida region. This equipment will be available to neighboring academic institutions to enhance the overall Biomedical research efforts in Florida.
1959.direct_services: Super-resolution microscopy and high throughput imaging are transforming the landscape of therapeutic development. By combining these technologies, we can gain unprecedented insights into cellular biology, identify novel drug targets, and streamline the drug discovery pipeline. This integrated approach holds great promise for developing innovative therapies that can address unmet medical needs.
1959.population: General, but significantly people with disease, aging population and those who are immunocompromised
1959.outcome: There are several expected benefits and outcomes to this project. This equipment will help researchers gain new insights into how cells in the body work, find new drug targets, and speed up the drug discovery process. This could lead to more effective treatments and better results for patients. In addition, FRIC is dedicated to training the next generation of researchers. FRIC partners with FIU and FAU and will train graduate students or other researchers from FAU who will have an opportunity to use and train on this equipment.

3072.description: The Lake Brooklyn Water Safety Complex at Camp Immokalee will improve child safety and prevent drownings by expanding access to swim instruction for youth and families in rural Clay, Bradford, Union, and Putnam Counties. The project will build a multipurpose pavilion and accessible trail connections at the existing pool site, providing a safe facility for hundreds of children each year and improving access for more than 30,000 who live in the surrounding area.
3072.purpose: The Lake Brooklyn Water Safety Complex at Camp Immokalee will improve child safety and prevent drownings by expanding access to swim instruction for youth and families in rural Clay, Bradford, Union, and Putnam Counties. The project will build a multipurpose pavilion and accessible trail connections at the existing pool site, providing a safe facility for participants.
3072.activities: Drowning-prevention and water-safety education, swim instruction, outdoor learning experiences, family wellness programs, and senior and youth health and wellness activities
3072.direct_services: Project will provide direct services to more than 2,500 children and families annually through drowning-prevention and water-safety programs, swim instruction, and community wellness activities. The facility will create safe, year-round access for residents and be sustained through strong local family and partner support.
3072.population: Target population for the Lake Brooklyn Water Safety Complex at Camp Immokalee are youth and families in rural Clay, Bradford, Union, and Putnam Counties. 2,500 individuals expected to be served.
3072.outcome: Children and Families receive certified water-safety instruction aligned with Florida's physical-education and drowning- prevention goals. The YMCA will Maintain records of curriculum completion, instructor certifications, and participant learning outcomes.

1952.organization: Boys & Girls Clubs of Central Florida
1952.description: The funds will support the construction of a gym for the new Boys & Girls Clubs of Central Florida location in Winter Garden (opening 2026), which will serve over 200 youth ages 6–18.
1952.purpose: The funds will support the land development and construction of the new Boys & Girls Clubs of Central Florida location in Winter Garden’s full-size gym. With the gym, the location will serve over 200 youth ages 6–18.
1952.activities: The gym will promote physical fitness, teamwork, and healthy lifestyles as part of comprehensive youth development programming. The new 20,000-square-foot facility—including dedicated Youth and Teen Centers—will serve up to 220 children and teens daily, compared to just 40 currently served in a shared county recreation center.
1952.direct_services: Club activities center on health and life skills, character and leadership development, the arts, sports, fitness, and recreation, education and career development, and mental health. These activities range from tutoring, specialized programming, workshops with professionals throughout the community, mentorship, and much more. The gym specifically will provide a place for health and fitness activi
1952.population: BGCCF serves youth ages 6-18 and, by extension, supports their families, frequently in low-income neighborhoods. This Club will serve up to 220 youth and teens daily.
1952.outcome: There are numerous benefits of the project including: Improved physical health (measured through fitness testing and surveying of exercise habits) Improved mental health (measured through student access to programming and mental/emotional health surveys) Increased economic activity (measured through graduation rates and college, vo-tech, and military enrollment) Reduced substance abuse (measured through surveys)

3131.description: The Town of Grand Ridge received Hazard Mitigation Grant Funds for a new fire station in FY 2022-23. Since then the fire station project has begun but unable to complete due to the increasing cost of construction. The requested funds will allow the Town of Grand Ridge to complete the project thereby giving the fire department a new, safer location out of which to operate.
3131.purpose: The Town of Grand Ridge received Hazard Mitigation Grant Funds for a new fire station in FY 2022-23. Since then the fire station project has begun but unable to complete due to the increasing cost of construction. The requested funds will allow the Town of Grand Ridge to complete the project thereby giving the fire department a new, safer location out of which to operate.
3131.activities: The funds will be used to complete the construction project for a new fire station in Grand Ridge.
3131.direct_services: The funds will be used to complete the construction project for a new fire station in Grand Ridge. This new fire station will serve the citizens of Grand Ridge and parts of unincorporated Jackson County.
3131.population: The citizens of the Town of Grand Ridge along with parts of unincorporated Jackson County.
3131.outcome: A new, safer home for the Grand Ridge Fire Department.

3091.description: The Town of Brooker has a goal to construct a full-time career paid fire station. The Town of Brooker is one of the most rural portions of Bradford County with fire and EMS response taking a minimum of 15 minutes from the closest station. Funding this request will result in shorter response times, greatly expanding and improving the Fire and EMS service to the community. This is Phase II of the station construction project.
3091.purpose: The Town of Brooker has a goal to construct a full-time career paid fire station. The Town of Brooker is one of the most rural portions of Bradford County with fire and EMS response taking a minimum of 15 minutes from the closest station. Funding this request will result in shorter response times, greatly expanding and improving the Fire and EMS service to the community.
3091.activities: This new fire station will be incredibly beneficial to all citizens and visitors of Bradford County. The new station will provide immediate access to emergency service delivery for the population across the region.
3091.direct_services: The new fire station will be staffed with full-time career firefighters, expanding and improving the community's access to fire and EMS services. This station will serve as a community hub for the residents of this unserviced, rural area. This will be a significant expansion of fire and EMS services to the Southwest area of Bradford County.
3091.population: This project will serve the entire population of Bradford County. Approximately 29,000.
3091.outcome: Much quicker response times to patients in need of life-saving medical treatment. Measured by system response time data.

3152.description: Request funding to support continued operations of a mental health diversion program designed to redirect certain populations away from incarceration in local jails. Participants will be placed into the program typically as a condition of their bond and Pretrial Release Supervision. Services included in the program include needs assessment, service referrals, case management, substance use disorder treatment, psychosocial rehabilitation, self-help, advocacy, recovery planning, health and wellness, and relapse prevention. This innovative program has served 220 incarcerated persons referred by the Okaloosa County Pre-Trial Program since opening in January 2020. During 2024, 65% of participants achieved successful program completion. Additionally, of clients who completed the program in 2024 only 7 clients experienced rearrest during 2024 which continues to be below the average recidivism r
3152.purpose: Provide post-booking diversion for appropriate people with misdemeanor and low level felony charges from the criminal justice system as well as post-release wraparound services to those who are released from custody to prevent recidivism. Due to the success of this program the Office of State Attorney First Judicial Circuit has expanded the range of offenses eligible for consideration for referral to this program has expanded from the original misdemeanor only to now include low-level non-violen
3152.activities: Services included in the program include needs assessment, service referrals, case management, psychosocial rehabilitation, substance use disorder treatment, self-help and advocacy, recovery planning, health and wellness classes, relapse prevention and education factors that have contributed to their judicial involvement. Active monitoring of participants will be provided by Pretrial Services in coordination with BCI staff.
3152.direct_services: Direct services included in the program include needs assessment, service referrals, case management, psychosocial rehabilitation, substance use disorder treatment, self-help and advocacy, recovery planning, health and wellness classes, relapse prevention and education factors that have contributed to their judicial involvement.
3152.population: Persons with poor mental health, economically disadvantaged persons, homeless, drug users, currently or formerly incarcerated persons and the general population of Okaloosa County, which has a population of over 200,000.
3152.outcome: Recovery and rehabilitation of patients and reduced recidivism. Test whether costs of incarceration, length of incarceration, recidivism, can be lowered, safety increased and liberty protected in a cost-effective way in counties with a paucity of mental health and substance abuse treatment resources.

2502.organization: Florida Alcohol and Drug Abuse Association
2502.description: The federal Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) strongly advocate for the use of medication-assisted treatment as a best practice approach to serve individuals with alcohol and opioid use disorders. Program funds community treatment providers for provision of substance abuse screening, medical assessments/lab work and extended-release naltrexone medication injections for individuals with alcohol and/or opioid abuse or dependence throughout the state that are uninsured or under-insured. Services are delivered through a statewide network of 45 providers from Pensacola to Key West.
2502.purpose: In response to the opioid epidemic and the ongoing problem of alcohol abuse/dependence among Florida's citizens, the program facilitates recovery from substance abuse, lowers rates of opioid overdose, and reduces costs to society for employment issues, high-cost healthcare utilization, and criminal justice/court involvement related to opioid and alcohol use disorders.
2502.activities: The program funds substance abuse screening/evaluation, medical assessment, and extended-release medication injections to help uninsured or under-insured individuals with alcohol and/or opioid dependence recover. The program enhances retention/completion rates for outpatient, residential, and other forms of psychosocial treatment.
2502.direct_services: Clinical screening to diagnose alcohol and/or opioid use disorders; medical assessments/lab work to determine fitness of patients to receive medication and continue with maintenance protocols; and, medication administration for dosing extended-release injectable naltrexone every 3 to 4 weeks until cessation of the medical protocol as determined by the physician.
2502.population: The non-recurring funds enable the program to serve 403 patients who are uninsured or under-insured and present with alcohol and/or opioid abuse and dependence problems through the provision of clinical screening, medical assessment/lab work, and extended-release injectable naltrexone medication.
2502.outcome: The program's outcome performance measurement is that at least 60% of individuals receiving extended-release injectable naltrexone services will successfully complete or remain actively engaged in psychosocial treatment for alcohol and/or opioid use disorders at time of discharge from services. Performance is calculated by dividing the numerator, which is all individuals successfully completing or still actively engaged in psychosocial treatment at time of discharge from medication-assisted treatment (MAT) services by the denominator, which is all individuals discharged from MAT services.

2898.description: The requested funds will support the next phase of planning a permanent home for The Florida Orchestra (TFO), the state’s largest orchestra serving 155,000 guests annually in Tampa Bay region. Funding will cover expert consultants, such as a theater/concert hall planning and design, acoustics, market analysis, fundraising, cost estimator, architect, and engineering to ensure feasibility studies and designs meet the community's and state’s needs for this regional cultural asset.
2898.purpose: The funds will be used to determine the viability, suitability, and strategic direction for TFO's CMEI. The research performed will offer data-driven decisions, plans, and recommendations to help guide the organization as it prepares for the next phase of the project which includes investment and implementation.
2898.activities: Consulting studies will establish a comprehensive market analysis, feasibility study, financial planning, donor capacity, architectural designs, structural assessments, space lists, adjacency diagrams, room data sheets, cost estimates, SWOT analysis, scenario planning, theatric acoustical assessments, interviews, strategic alignment with community partners, and final reports.
2898.direct_services: TFO's CMEI will serve the community by providing economic impact through increased groups of visitors and tourists; enhanced arts & cultural experiences to attract diverse audiences, increasing community and corporate partnerships, developing education and innovation opportunities, and serve as a resource for evacuation needs.
2898.population: The Tampa Bay community is the target population served by this project. Music is for all, and TFO's mission is to inspire, educate, and unite to build community through the power of music. TFO's Center for Music Education & Innovation will be an economic driver and a cultural asset serving more than the 150,000 guests currently being served annually.
2898.outcome: The project's benefit is enhancing community vitality, economic growth, and cultural engagement. Outcomes include increased tourism dollars, job creation, growing arts participation, property value boosts, and community cohesion. Success will be measured through metrics like visitor numbers, economic impact (e.g., spending, employment), community surveys, and project-specific indicators such as attendance, partnership engagement, and long-term sustainability.

2504.description: Founded in 1971, EC-SAR is the only student-staffed maritime search and rescue team at an undergraduate college in the US, responding to more than 400 maritime distress calls per year. This highly trained group of student volunteers works closely with the U.S. Coast Guard, 911 and other agencies, providing free 24-hour maritime assistance to the boaters of Tampa Bay and adjacent waterways. Leveraging the program's five decades of experience (including serving as the first rescue units to respond to the Sunshine Skyway Bridge collapse in 1980), EC-SAR has become one of the most respected search and rescue organizations on the west coast of Florida. In 2012, EC-SAR developed a search pattern for locating people in the waters surrounding the Skyway Bridge, recognized by the Tampa Bay Search and Rescue Council, Pinellas County Emergency Response Services and the U.S. Coast Guard. In 2019, EC
2504.purpose: Funds will be used for operating support and infrastructure improvements, facilitating the team's ability to continue rescues, patrols, and training. In addition to needed infrastructure upgrades (including boat docks, lifts and pilings), funds will support operating costs such as fuel, navigation electronics, uniforms, and capital replacement expenses (e.g., new engines). While EC-SAR currently receives annual funding from Pinellas County for Maritime BLS First Responder Services, this represen
2504.activities: EC-SAR team members coordinate the utilization of four rescue boats and an operations/communications center to save lives and property on a daily basis. Students serve a 24-hour-duty rotation every 3 days, participate in weekly patrols, and monitor VHF radios and phones for incoming calls for assistance. EC-SAR students train rigorously in a nine-month program focused on basic and advanced skills including: boating safety, seamanship, line work, basic life support, in-water rescue, emergency res
2504.direct_services: EC-SAR serves a 500-square nautical-mile area of response, adding to the maritime safety of Pinellas, Hillsborough and Manatee counties - including 26 municipalities with resident populations totaling nearly 2.9 million. In partnership with the U.S. Coast Guard, 911 Emergency Response and other state and local agencies, EC-SAR fulfills a critical need by ensuring the safety of the Tampa Bay region
2504.population: The target population is the boating community in EC-SAR's 500-square nautical-mile area of response. Beyond the 500+ boaters annually served by EC-SAR on average, this funding will directly benefit the team members by improving their training and rescue resources. EC-SAR is a highly motivated group of volunteer students who are dedicated to serving the community. Although students do not receive pay or academic credit for their participation, the opportunity to learn and practice unique skills
2504.outcome: EC-SAR will continue to protect the boating community of Tampa Bay and adjacent waterways, by responding to an average of 400 distress calls per year. The team will compile annual statistics on the number of calls received, cases performed, boat hours logged, and number of people assisted.

2178.organization: Dixie County Board of County Commissioners
2178.description: The Phase 3 funds requested will be used for the construction of the Dixie County Sheriff’s Office Multipurpose Evidence Building on County-owned land. The new building will be an accredited agency for housing any local, state, or federal evidence. The building will also service as a training site to host in-house and regional training sessions. A dedicated building for evidence storage and training will ensure public safety is enhanced.
2178.purpose: The Phase 3 funds requested will be used for the construction of the Dixie County Sheriff’s Office Multipurpose Evidence Building on County-owned land. The new building will be an accredited agency for housing any local, state, or federal evidence. The building will also serve as a training site to host in-house and regional training sessions. A dedicated building for evidence storage and training will ensure public safety is enhanced.
2178.activities: The multipurpose evidence building will support public safety by ensuring valuable evidence is not damaged, and will provide a regional location for local, state, and federal evidence to be stored safely. The facility will also feature interview rooms, which will assist law enforcement in their mission to promote law and order within the County and surrounding areas.
2178.direct_services: The Phase 3 funds requested will be used for the construction of the Dixie County Sheriff’s Office Multipurpose Evidence Building on County-owned land. The new building will be an accredited agency for housing any local, state, or federal evidence. The building will also serve as a training site to host in-house training sessions. With evidence being stored in a secure location and training provid
2178.population: The general public of Dixie County will be served by this project. Thousands of residents will be served.
2178.outcome: The new building will be an accredited facility and a training site for our local, state, and federal law enforcement. Through a series of surveys and questionnaires, the benefit of this project can be measured. Data such as the prevalence of illegal drug use, drug trafficking, violence, and additional criminal behaviors can be tracked. As this data is collected it can be analyzed to determine the effectiveness of the new facility.

3193.description: "Around the Mound" is a proposed project to reconfigure State Road 30 and State Road 85. The purpose of the project would be address existing and future vehicle capacity on SR 30 /U.S. 98 as well as the high volumes of regional and commuter traffic traveling through downtown Fort Walton Beach.
3193.purpose: The specific purpose of the request is to fully fund the design & engineering of "Around the Mound". The City of Fort Walton Beach and Okaloosa County have partnered to cover the original estimate of $2,700,000 however estimates are now $4,750,000.
3193.activities: The purpose of this project is to address existing and future vehicular capacity and safety issues on SR 30/US 98 as well as the high volumes of regional and commuter traffic traveling through Downtown Fort Walton Beach.
3193.direct_services: The project is needed to increase the capacity of U.S. 98 to accommodate current and future traffic and to reduce regional and commuter traffic through downtown Fort Walton Beach. Request of these funds will allow design to proceed.
3193.population: All daily commuters and visitors to Okaloosa County.
3193.outcome: Improve transportation conditions, increase economic activity, increase tourism. Method for measurement would be FDOT LOS evaluation, and reduction in travel times.

2400.description: FDEP designated Lake Weir as impaired for nutrients. Project will reduce nutrient loading, improve water quality, reduce frequent algal blooms, improve habitat for fish/wildlife, and enhance clarity for recreational use/property value enhancement for the surrounding 2,000+ homes. Project will implement innovative technologies around the lake to trap/uptake nutrients before they enter the lake, dredge nutrient dense hot spots, and restore wetlands that act as nutrient sinks.
