Project will reduce nutrient loading, improve water quality, reduce frequent algal blooms, improve habitat for fish/wildlife, and enhance clarity for recreational use/property value enhancement for the surrounding 2,000+ homes. Project will implement innovative technologies around the lake to trap/uptake nutrients before they enter the lake, dredge nutrient dense hot spots, and restore wetlands that act as nutrient sinks.
2400.activities: Project will implement innovative technologies around the lake to trap/uptake nutrients before they enter the lake, dredge nutrient dense hot spots, and restore wetlands that act as nutrient sinks.
2400.direct_services: Services will be provided to lake residents and visitors to enhance water quality, reduce algal blooms, uptake nutrients from community runoff, improve recreational use, and enhance fishing opportunities.
2400.population: Marion County resident and visitors, as well as the 2000+ residents of Weirsdale who surround the lake
2400.outcome: Project will help improve water quality, enhance habitat for fish and wildlife, improve clarity of lake, reduce toxic algal blooms, and enhance recreational opportunities.

2000.description: This funding is for the retention of personnel to provide the needed clinical services at no cost to Florida's veterans, military personnel and first responders who suffer from PTSD, many of whom do not have the financial means to pay for treatment, even if it was only the co-pay. If insurance were to be billed for these services or the individual had to pay out of pocket, the cost would exceed $1 million. Thus, providing these services at no cost is a great benefit to the citizens of Florida.
2000.purpose: Retention of personnel to provide the needed clinical services at no cost to Florida's veterans, military personnel and first responders who suffer from PTSD, many of whom do not have the financial means to pay for treatment, even if it was only the co-pay. If insurance were to be billed for these services or the individual had to pay out of pocket, the cost would exceed $1 million. Thus, providing these services at no cost is a great benefit to the citizens of Florida.
2000.activities: UCF RESTORES provides PTSD treatment and resiliency services at no cost to Florida’s veterans, active duty personnel, and first responders. Many of the veterans we serve cannot access treatment at the VA.
2000.direct_services: Our innovative two-week intensive outpatient treatment program, where personnel are treated five days per week, is the only program of its kind in the country. The program includes the use of virtual reality (sights, sounds, and smells) to enhance the effects of the therapy and we have seen remarkable success. Since 2016, we have treated 800 veterans/active duty and 1200 first responders.
2000.population: Citizens of Florida who have experienced a traumatic event - approximately 300-400.
2000.outcome: A key outcome of RESTORES’ work is to allow the state to retain its critical group of first responders by allowing them to recover from their trauma-related injuries and return to the workplace. Not only does this improve the quality of life for these heroes, it has a substantial economic impact in terms of savings from the recruitment and training of replacement personnel. Research studies have shown that 76% of first responders and 66% of veterans/active duty personnel no longer meet the diagnostic criteria for PTSD following our treatment program, an unmatched success rate that points to the effectiveness of this unique approach.

2406.description: The current Police and Emergency Operations Center is housed in a 1960's re-purposed building in a topographically challenging area, which experienced its most catastrophic flooding event to date from the impacts of Hurricane Milton and took 10 months to mitigate and reconstruct to the existing standard. The city has previously contracted architectural schematics and design for a new hurricane-hardened Public Safety Complex to be built on another property that the city owns meeting todays stormwater standards. This funding request will help bring architectural schematics and design from 30% to 100%.
2406.purpose: Funding a new, storm-hardened police facility to serve as the city's centralized emergency operations base will ensure public safety operations are protected and remain viable in situations of hazardous weather and disaster events, and allow emergency staff to properly respond to the community needs before, during, and after hurricanes and other disaster related events that impact the citizens and local area.
2406.activities: The Public Safety/EOC facility will house the city's disaster operations, as well as patrol, investigations, community improvement, police administration, code enforcement, animal control, records, evidence, police cadets and volunteers. The funding will facilitate the architectural schematics and design drawings being completed from 30% design to 100% design.
2406.direct_services: Ensure the emergency operations division has a secure and functional facility from which to administer disaster and emergency public services to over 14,000 citizens of Orange City.
2406.population: All estimated 14,882 permanent residents of the city, as well as transient medical and commercial visitors of around 35,000 per day who come to Orange City every day to utilize our medical services, retail shopping, and restaurant outlets.
2406.outcome: The most critical benefit will be to provide a hurricane-hardened facility that will ensure the safety of emergency personnel so they can effectively respond to weather and emergency related events and disasters in addition to daily emergency calls for service.

2414.description: This is a critical lift station built in the late 1970s that serves over 400 properties including an elementary school. Due to its age and older pump components, it no longer operates effectively in an area experiencing increased flood events. The project will raise the wet well and electrical systems above the floodplain and replace and upsize the force main to improve reliability and capacity.
2414.purpose: This is a critical lift station built in the late 1970s that serves over 400 properties including an elementary school. Due to its age and older pump components, it no longer operates effectively in an area experiencing increased flood events. The project will raise the wet well and electrical systems above the floodplain and replace and upsize the force main to improve reliability and capacity.
2414.activities: Construction activities necessary to construct the proposed improvements. Engineering & Inspection services to ensure the work is constructed per the approved design documents.
2414.direct_services: By completing the lift station project, the City is able to provide continuous and reliable collection and transmission of wastewater.
2414.population: The target population is over 400 residences and businesses.
2414.outcome: The City expects to be able to continue to provide continuous and reliable collection and transmission of wastewater with the completion of this project. Staff will continue to track the number of times the lift station is down and for how long and compare that information with previous data.

2171.description: Colonial High School’s Flight Academy is a premier Dual Enrollment program that partners with Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University to prepare students for high-demand careers in aviation. Through rigorous coursework in both manned and unmanned flight, our students gain industry-recognized skills that position them for success immediately after graduation. Our vision statement: To become a strong team of professional aviation instructors and students breaking barriers and creating opportunities by creating a pathway for youth to become skilled aviators, leaders, and innovators, transforming their lives while enriching the future of the aerospace industry.
2171.purpose: Our mission is to provide high-quality aviation education that empowers students to pursue meaningful careers in aviation. By removing financial barriers, offering expert instruction, and fostering supportive learning environment, we aim to build a pipeline of skilled pilots and aviation professionals who will strengthen and transform the future aviation workforce.
2171.activities: With direct, on-site instruction from our highly skilled CFII-certified flight instructor, students gain hands-on, professional training that gives them a powerful head start in their aviation careers.
2171.direct_services: Students will receive direct, on-site instruction from our CFII-certified flight instructor, providing them with advanced, industry-level training that better prepares them for future aviation careers.
2171.population: This project is designed to serve the current and future students of the Colonial High School Flight Academy Program, ensuring that all participating learners—present and incoming—benefit from enhanced instructional resources, advanced training opportunities, and expanded pathways into aviation careers.
2171.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is to equip students with the knowledge, training, and credentials needed to pursue their chosen aviation careers. By preparing more students for industry-ready roles, the program also supports the broader goal of addressing the workforce shortages currently faced within the aviation industry.

2413.description: The project is located in an older area that saw extensive flooding in Hurricanes Ian & Milton. It includes the construction of a new stormwater pond, pump station, and force main pipes to move water from homes & neighborhoods to the new pond and then pump to the Halifax River. This will help relieve flooding for about 250 homes in the area built mostly in the 1980s or earlier and before modern stormwater requirements.
2413.purpose: The project is located in an older area that saw extensive flooding in Hurricanes Ian & Milton. It includes the construction of a new stormwater pond, pump station, and force main pipes to move water from homes & neighborhoods to the new pond and then pump to the Halifax River. This will help relieve flooding for about 250 homes in the area built mostly in the 1980s or earlier and before modern stormwater requirements.
2413.activities: This funding includes the construction of a new stormwater pond, pump station, and force main pipes to take water to the Halifax River to reduce flooding to approx. 250 homes flooded in the northeast area of Port Orange during Hurricanes Ian and Milton.
2413.direct_services: Adding stormwater storage via a new pond and pumping the stormwater through a new force main directly to the Halifax River will help reduce flooding of structures in an area built in the 1980s before modern stromwater requirements.
2413.population: The target population is approximately 250 residences that flooded during Hurricanes Ian and Milton.
2413.outcome: Protection of the general public from the environmental hazards associated with flooding by reducing the flooding of structures. A comparison of the number of flooded structures before the project and after the project during similar storm events will be the method of measuring the success of the project.

2006.description: This program provides Florida’s K-12 students with an immersive, inspirational experience in the American Space Program, by integrating space missions into the STEM curriculum both virtually and in person at the Kennedy Space Center to enhance learning and engagement. Tailored to grade level, it fosters a deep interest in space exploration while equipping students with in-site into the critical STEM skills needed. By exposing students to real-world applications and career opportunities in the aerospace industry, the initiative inspires them to pursue studies in science, technology, engineering, and math, expanding their awareness of the vast possibilities within space exploration.
2006.purpose: Support for this program will provide 25,500 Florida K-12 students firsthand experience of the American Space Program. Technology upgrades and added resources will expand the program's reach by over 50% from last year, and allow for on-demand and streaming educational content to be available to all students and teachers statewide. The goal is to cultivate students’ passion for space exploration and guide them toward future opportunities in the space workforce through customized programs and STEM
2006.activities: This free program will engage students in hands-on lessons tailored to grade-level and introduce them to NASA missions and associated STEM content earning centered around current and future missions from educators, subject matter experts, or even an Astronaut. Students will also explore the KSC Visitor Center to learn about space exploration during their visit.
2006.direct_services: Over 25,500 Florida K-12 students (up from 17,000) will take part in hands-on lessons that deepen their understanding of space exploration, aerospace missions, and the skills vital to the American space program. Tailored by grade level, these STEM-focused lessons help students connect their experiences at KSC with classroom learning, ensuring they can apply their knowledge beyond their visit.
2006.population: The initiative expects to reach over 25,500 K-12 students from school districts across Florida, as well as students from schools of choice and a growing home-school population. This will be accomplished by providing immersive, inspiring experiences at the Kennedy Space Center and virtually.
2006.outcome: The primary expected benefits of this project are to significantly expand access to high-quality space and STEM education by inspiring students and educators with the knowledge necessary to increase awareness in space exploration and related STEM fields. Therefore, enhancing Florida’s role as a national leader in space education and exploration. The success of this project will be measured through the number of students engaged in the program as well as pre and post visit surveys to students that participate. Gains in STEM knowledge, as well as potential increases related to their interest in pursuing a career in space or a STEM related fields will also be tracked

2533.description: The funding would be used for design, land acquisition, and/or construction of at least two lanes of a future four-lane roadway extension of 51st Street West from 53rd Avenue West to El Conquistador Parkway. The project will include two general purpose lanes, street lighting, and bicycle/pedestrian facilities.
2533.purpose: To construct a key transportation corridor that supports economic development and revitalization in the Southwest District of Manatee County.

2533.population: General public Commuters Local businesses Pedestrians and cyclists
2533.outcome: Improved mobility, economic growth, and safety. Methodology: Construction milestones, traffic flow analysis, and economic development tracking.

The existing facility, constructed decades ago, lacks fire sprinklers, does not meet ADA accessibility requirements, and is constrained by outdated space configurations. The design will include plans for a second gymnasium, multipurpose rooms for classes and rental groups, and additional office space to support operations. The project will also address safety and accessibility deficiencies, ensuring compliance with modern codes. The design phase will produce bid-ready construction documents that position the Village to proceed with a facility that improves public safety, expands recreational opportunities, and better serves the needs of residents of all ages.
2662.purpose: The requested funds will enable the completion of architectural and engineering design plans for the renovation and expansion of the North Palm Beach Community Center. This includes ensuring compliance with modern building codes, ADA accessibility standards, and fire safety regulations. The outcome will be a comprehensive set of construction-ready documents that will facilitate the subsequent phases of the project, ensuring the facility meets current and future community needs.
2662.activities: Funds will be used to contract professional architectural and engineering services to develop comprehensive design and construction documents for the renovation and expansion of the North Palm Beach Community Center. Activities will include site and facility assessments, code compliance reviews, ADA accessibility planning, fire safety system design, space planning for additional gymnasium and multipurpose rooms, development of office layouts, cost estimating, and preparation of bid-ready plans a
2662.direct_services: The funding will support the creation of detailed design and engineering plans that will enable the renovation and expansion of the North Palm Beach Community Center. These plans will ensure the facility meets modern building codes, ADA accessibility standards, and fire safety requirements. Upon completion of construction, residents will benefit from expanded recreational opportunities, enhanced s
2662.population: The targeted population served by this project are the residents of North Palm Beach (approximately 13,500 people) as well as surrounding communities who frequent the Community Center for sports and programming.
2662.outcome: Funds will support the design and engineering phase for the renovation and expansion of the North Palm Beach Community Center, producing construction-ready documents that ensure ADA accessibility, fire safety compliance, and expanded multipurpose space to better serve the community’s recreational and programmatic needs. Progress will be tracked through project milestone reports from contracted design firms, official reviews and approvals by governing agencies, ADA compliance certifications, and internal project management documentation.

2359.description: The YMCA of the Palm Beaches is replacing it's 40 yr. old aged community center with a new state-of-the-art 55,000 sf community center, with a total est. cost of $29,500,000. The Y is a needed resource in this densely populated, economically challenged, central area of Palm Beach County. This project will triple the size, serve four times the number of members/citizens (estimated at 18,000), and be located along one of the busiest thoroughfares in the County, with approximately 60,000 car passes daily. The YMCA has partnered on this project with Palm Beach County, which has given the Y a 50-year ground lease and is building its new aquatic center adjacent to the community center, for the Y to manage. The first floor of the project will house a Youth Engagement and Resource Center, which will attract thousands of vulnerable teens, provide them with mentoring services and usher them into p

This will triple the size, serve four times the number of members/citizens (approx. 18,000), and be located along one of the busiest thoroughfares in Palm Beach County. The YMCA has partnered with Palm Beach County to secure a 50-year ground lease for the project. Space dedicated entirely to mentoring will attract thousands of vulnerable t
2359.activities: A full service YMCA will be constructed, at an approximate cost of $29,500,000 to provide traditional health and wellness programs for all ages, in addition to innovative programming for young people (12-22) in need of mentoring through the Youth engagement and Resource Center. Services will include, assigned mentors, job skills training and placement, postsecondary education placement and tuition assistance services.
2359.direct_services: Diabetes Prevention programs, swim lessons, youth sports, Teen Leadership programs, summer day camp, preschool, before and after school programming, mentoring, senior wellness programs, community volunteer initiatives, programs that work to prevent childhood drowning, post-secondary education placement, job skills training and placement, group exercise classes, water aerobics, health education cla
2359.population: Elderly persons * Persons with poor mental health * Persons with poor physical health * Jobless persons * Economically disadvantaged persons * At-risk youth * Homeless * Developmentally disabled * Physically disabled * Drug users (in health services) * Preschool students * Grade school students * High school students * University/College students * Teens in need of mentoring services. 2076.description: The roofs of several City-owned facilities are at the end of their useful life. State funds will assist the City in expediting needed replacements of roofs at at Gerber Park Bathroom Building and Sabal Pines Park Dugouts (8) and Gerber Park Dugouts (2), which are used by families and youth throughout the City as well as neighboring municipalities.
2076.purpose: Expedited replacement of end-of-life roofing at various recreational facilities used by families and youth This will provide for replacements at Gerber Park Bathroom Building and Sabal Pines Park Dugouts (8) and Gerber Park Dugouts (2).
2076.activities: Needed replacement of roofing at identified facilities
2076.direct_services: Continuity of operations and services, safety, and resilience of recreational facilities that are used by families and youth.
2076.population: Thousands. The City of Coconut Creek has a population of 58,000. Sabal Pines Park is the City's largest park and hosts major annual events attended by thousands. Both parks are used by youth athletics which include youth from surrounding municipalities.
2076.outcome: Maintains safe environments for student athletics, outdoor education programs, events and other enjoyment of the facilities. Measured by: building inspections; number of youth participants; facility usage hours and uptime tracking.

2057.description: State Road 50 is a significant east west highway that splits Clermont north and south. Numerous concerns from residents and guests have been expressed regarding the safety of pedestrians crossing SR 50. The City of Clermont is requesting funding to study and create concept plans of which locations would be the safest to cross and what facilities can be built to provide for the safe crossing.
2057.purpose: To create a safe pathway for pedestrians and bicyclists to cross State Road 50 either north or south.
2057.activities: Study the creation of a safe route.
2057.outcome: Reduce accidents and conflicts between vehicles and pedestrians/cyclists.

2106.description: The Continuum of Care program offers enhanced offender rehabilitation to include cognitive-based therapy (individual and group) integrated with enhanced transition case management and community based post-release services.
2106.purpose: The primary goal of the Continuum of Care program is to reduce recidivism. Since implementation of the Continuum of Care at GEO facilities, we have realized a reduction in recidivism year over year for those engaged in the program versus those that are not engaged. Other program goals are ensuring a successful reentry for participants through engagement with their local communities, which in turn will enhance public safety.
2106.activities: Core correctional practices training for facilities staff; evidence based in-prison rehabilitative programming for individuals who will be transitioning back into their community; post release support services for successful reintegration. All Continuum of Care Services are provided, pursuant to a contract with DOC, on a cost reimbursement basis with no profit or administrative fee.
2106.direct_services: Cognitive behavioral treatment programs; education and vocational training; substance abuse counseling and treatment; one-on-one transition support including individual cognitive behavioral therapy, and dedicated case management including a 24x7 call center and funded individual service packages for basic welfare and support via community resource referrals for up to one year.
2106.population: The Continuum of Care program serves individuals while in-custody and post-release into the community. Currently, the program serves over 4,000 individuals in three facilities. Services are provided on a cost reimbursement basis with no profit or administrative fee.
2106.outcome: Since the primary goal of the program is to reduce recidivism, this is measured by reviewing recidivism data at 1 and 3-year intervals. However, there are many ways to measure the various components of the program. For those in- custody, the Continuum of Care creates more positive environment and reduces safety risks. this is measured by reviewing discipline reports, SIRs/criminal thinking scales, formal grievances filed and staff complaint as a comparison over time. The Education/Vocation component can be measured by determining the total number of hours completed in each program and certifications granted for participants. Post-release participants education and employment status are measu

2511.description: The Florida Holocaust Museum, one of only three Holocaust museums nationally accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, is a recognized leader in Holocaust education in Florida, the U.S., and abroad. Through exhibitions, virtual tours, survivor conversations, and multimedia platforms, the Museum reaches over 1,300 teachers, 380,000 students, 24,000 participants, and 2,000 law-enforcement officers annually, and delivers evidence-based Holocaust instruction directly into Florida schools. The Museum safeguards nearly 25,000 artifacts and 400 testimonies and recently added two major assets—the Danish rescue boat Thor and the Elie Wiesel Collection—to ensure students and the public encounter the Holocaust as an urgent civic lesson with contemporary relevance. Funding would convert these new assets into lasting education through research, curriculum, virtual engagement, public programs, a
2511.purpose: The requested funding would allow the Museum to develop integrated Holocaust education materials for students, educators, and partners; build a more interactive virtual tour; add new public events; advance research on the new Elie Wiesel, Thor, and core Holocaust exhibits; and curate additional artifacts. This will ensure these new assets become lasting tools for Holocaust learning as we enter a period when first-hand witnesses are no longer present to tell their stories.
2511.activities: Funds will support development of integrated Holocaust education materials; creation of an interactive virtual tour; expansion of public programs and events; research on the new Wiesel, Thor, and core exhibits; and ongoing curation of artifacts to embed new collections into permanent educational use.
2511.direct_services: Funding will deliver Holocaust education to Florida students, teachers, families, and law-enforcement through exhibits, curriculum, virtual tours, public programs, and access to authentic survivor history. They will be made accessible at no cost throughout Florida for Holocaust education and to combat antisemitism.
2511.population: The Museum uses state-of-the-art technologies to reach more than 1,300 teachers, 380,000 students, and 24,000 individuals annually who are impacted through virtual educational programs, survivor talks, and commemorations each year. We expect these numbers to increase significantly because of the addition of Thor and The Wiesel Collection.
2511.outcome: The Florida Holocaust Museum, one of only three nationally accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, is a leading provider of Holocaust education, with a global reach through partnerships with organizations worldwide. With the global rise of antisemitism, the Wiesel Collection will be both a permanent and traveling exhibition, accessible to Holocaust and genocide researchers across the country. The Museum will deploy a post-visit survey to visitors and students to quantitatively ascertain key learnings or take-aways of those who experienced both Thor and the Wiesel exhibit, sentiments that changed as a result of experiencing the exhibits, and critical questions that may remain in the m

2109.description: The County is seeking funding for the futher consolidation of their Sheriff’s Office and its functions. The County has recently purchased a building centrally located in Madison to allow for the consolidation of six offices around the County. This property will serve as a single consolidated location for employees to be co-located to offer residents critical services during emergency events.

2109.activities: This property will serve as a single consolidated location for employees to be co-located to offer residents critical services during emergency events.

2654.description: The Five STAR Veterans Center helps homeless or displaced veterans who are suffering with Post Traumatic Stress or other behavioral health issues. The current footprint of Five Star is too small to serve the growing need of veterans in our State. Funding will go towards Renovations and expansion of the center to serve more at-risk veterans.
2654.purpose: The Five STAR Veterans Center helps homeless or displaced veterans who are suffering with Post Traumatic Stress or other behavioral health issues. Five Star Veterans Center provides shelter and programming to re-integrate veterans into civilian life. This expansion project will allow for more at-risk veterans to be served.

It will enhance situational awareness, improve interoperability among agencies, and support decision-making in dynamic environments. The unit will be deployed countywide for all major incidents, including hurricanes, mass casualty events, and large-scale or soft- target gatherings. The MCU will serve as a forward-deployed operations hub, enabling real-time decision-making, multi-agency coordination, and inter- operable communications during emergencies. Citizens will benefit from more organized evacuations, quicker access to emergency medical services, and

This includes international and domestic travelers, many of whom attend high-profile events that require enhanced public safety coordination. The Mobile Command Unit (MCU) will provide on- site command and control capabilities, enabling real-time decision-making, inter-operable communications, and multi- agency coordination. This will result in more efficient incident management, reduced response times, and better outcomes for affected communities. The methodology for measuring these outcomes will include tracking key performance indicators such as response time improvements, number of successful deployments, inter-agency coordination metrics, and afte

2368.description: The requested funds will support the construction phase of the new Law Enforcement Training Center, including the firearms range and essential training infrastructure. This phase will transform completed designs into a functional, state- of-the-art facility that enhances officer skills, safety, and readiness. The project will provide a modern, sustainable training environment that meets evolving public safety standards and supports long-term departmental and regional training needs.
2368.purpose: Requested funds will support the construction phase of the new Police Training Center, including the firearms range and essential training infrastructure. This phase will transform completed designs into a functional, state-of-the-art facility that enhances officer skills, safety, and readiness. The project will provide a modern, sustainable training environment that meets evolving public safety standards and supports long-term departmental and regional training needs.
2368.activities: Funding will support construction of the new training center, including a firearms range and training infrastructure. The facility will meet operational needs, improve officer safety and readiness, and provide modern, secure, and sustainable space to enhance community safety and policing effectiveness.

Indirectly, it will serve at-risk youth, victims of crime, and economically disadvantaged persons through improved public safety and community engagement. The facility will ensure consistent, high-quality training in firearms, de-escalation, and crisis management. Success will be measured through training completion rates, performance evaluations, reduced travel costs, fewer use-of-force incidents, and continued accreditation compliance.

2816.description: The Center investigates the underlying causes of chronic neuromusculoskeletal conditions, especially neck / low back pain and movement disorders. Its mission is to develop and implement high-impact translational and clinical research that fosters collaboration, innovation, discovery, education, and clinical implementation. The vision is to become the leader in transformational and innovative neuromusculoskeletal research within the State of Florida.
2816.purpose: CNMSR will provide advanced research, education, and clinical services focused on neuromusculoskeletal health. Activities include conducting cutting-edge studies, offering patient care, and training healthcare professionals to improve treatment and prevention of musculoskeletal disorders, enhancing the well-being of Floridians through evidence-based practices and innovations.
2816.activities: The funding will support research into specialized care for pediatric and elderly populations, veterans, and active military. Services will include musculoskeletal assessments, rehabilitation, pain management, and tailored treatments, improving mobility, quality of life, and overall health.
2816.direct_services: The funding will support direct services including specialized care for pediatric and elderly populations, veterans, and active military. Services will include musculoskeletal assessments, rehabilitation, pain management, and tailored treatments, improving mobility, quality of life, and overall health for these diverse groups across Florida.
2816.population: Pediatric and elderly populations, veterans, and active military.
2816.outcome: There is an expected benefit of improvement in physical function scores and reduction in pain levels as well as an increase in employment rate, income levels, and job stability and a decrease in repeat visits/readmissions, reduced treatment recurrence. This will be measured by tracking healthcare cost savings, productivity improvements, external grants applied for and funded, and job retention in individuals who receive care, through employer and patient surveys and economic impact assessments.

2443.description: The City of Groveland, in collaboration with Lake County and project partners, is committed to preserving Wilson Island, a vital environmental asset in the Palatlakaha River. This initiative aims to preserve the last remaining opportunity in Groveland for public access to the Palatlakaha River. Wilson Island has the potential to become one of Lake County's most treasured natural resources, enhancing public access to the Palatlakaha Blueway and supporting a wide array of recreational opportunities.
2443.purpose: The conservation of Wilson Island within the Palatlakaha Conservation Corridor advances the State’s priorities of protecting water quality, wildlife habitat, and corridor linkages put forward by the Florida Wildlife Corridor Act (Senate Bill 976). The protection of Wilson Island contributes to the movement of plants and animals through the wider mosaic of connectivity across the state due to its proximity to the Green Swamp Area of Critical State Concern and Withlacoochee State Forest.
2443.activities: The acquisition of Wilson Island protects rare and unique upland habitat within the Palatlakaha Conservation Corridor from high-density development that would significantly alter the character of this pristine area. Ladd Development has an approved Preliminary Plat to develop Wilson Island. They have submitted a Site Development Plan for 181 residential units and over 85,500 square feet of commercial/mixed-use space. If the land cannot be purchased for conservation in a reasonable timeframe, the
2443.direct_services: The acquisition of Wilson Island would preserve the last remaining opportunity in Groveland for public access to the Palatlakaha River. In addition, Wilson Island provides plentiful restoration and enhancement opportunities, as well as a vision for public resource-based passive recreation. The park would encourage various recreational activities, including birdwatching, reading, walking, picnickin
2443.population: If Wilson Island is preserved as a conservation park, it would be the heart of the Palatlakaha regional Blueway. Not only would Wilson Island expand public access to the Palatlakaha River for Groveland residents, but it also has the potential to become a regional attraction for outdoor recreation eco-tourists, such as paddleboarders, kayakers, and canoers. Providing breathtaking views of both natural wetlands and stunning agrarian landscapes, the Palatlakaha Run emerging from Lake Louisa is the
2443.outcome: The protection of Wilson Island will conserve rare upland habitat in the Palatlakaha Conservation Corridor for wildlife and create recreational opportunities for residents and visitors to experience the real Florida. By securing this property for passive recreation and nature-based activities, the project will enhance quality of life while also stimulating economic development by attracting more paddlers, hikers, and ecotourists to the Palatlakaha Blueway and Lake County's local businesses. These benefits can be measured by visitor counts, levels of program p

2704.description: Sherman Creek is a major drainageway for the City of Atlantic Beach serving the Town Center business district, several neighborhoods, Atlantic Beach Elementary School, City Hall and the Public Safety Building. Over the years, Sherman Creek has become silted in and does not provide for adequate flood protection.
2704.purpose: Restore drainage capabilities of Sherman Creek to protect upstream homes, businesses and critical infrastructure from flood damage, and to help assure evacuation routes remain passable.
2704.activities: - Dredging of accumulated muck and debris from Sherman Creek - Littoral planting to help stabilize the creek banks and provide for water quality treatment - Beneficial reuse of dredged material
2704.direct_services: - Flood protection for residences, businesses and critical infrastructure during severe rainfall events - Increased property value - Improved water quality - Improved fish habitat
2704.population: The population of Atlantic Beach will be served by the project through area streets remaining passable during severe storm events. An estimated 4,000 residents live in structures that will help to be protected from flooding by this project.
2704.outcome: Improved hydraulic capacity of Sherman Creek resulting in a decrease in duration and depth of flooding. This outcome will be measured via stormwater modeling and the recording of water levels during severe storm events.

3033.description: The appropriation will enable Hillsborough College to acquire the equipment and infrastructure to offer the Unmanned Vehicle Systems AS degree program. The program's advanced training in unmanned aerial, ground, and maritime systems will meet the workforce needs of employers within the military, public safety, agriculture, utilities, and logistics fields. The program will also complement Plant City campus's relationship with the University of Florida's IFAS operations.
3033.purpose: The appropriation will enable Hillsborough College to acquire the equipment and infrastructure to offer the Unmanned Vehicle Systems AS degree program. 2327.direct_services: Kayaking, canoing, paddle boarding and other water sports. Walking and running trails, fishing areas, family-friendly areas, event space for use and rentals, special events, wildlife watching, and other educational outreach programs.
2327.population: The target population is youth to seniors. Recreation programming is versatile and can offer something for everyone regardless of age, socioeconomic status, and access to resources. Existing facilities can serve around 15,000-20,000 citizens per year.
2327.outcome: Expected benefits would be improved physical and mental health, social cohesion, increase access to educational opportunities, economic growth and local business support, promotion of cultural diversity and inclusion, and safety and crime reduction. The methodology for measurement will be tracking attendance at events and programs, participant surveys, participant feedback, business participation records and impact, employment data, police reports, crime statistics, and constant data collection

2429.description: Many FGCU students often remain on campus, as they either do not live on campus or their residence does not make it feasible to leave and return for classes throughout a given day. Research consistently demonstrates that students' academic achievements are positively impacted by the on-campus support and services they receive. FGCU goal is to reconstruct and design communal spaces where students can access specialized support services, collaboratively work and gain valuable time for studies.
2429.purpose: In addition to student programming the Cohen Student Union, offers an opportunity to grow our Eagle Culture on campus, build school spirit, and expand our resiliency practices on campus. Strengthens academic and student engagement with specialized student support services through the reconfiguration of E&G space in a highly accessible location for a transformative not transactional atmosphere. Fosters collaborative learning opportunities that provides student study rooms and offices for students
2429.activities: Incorporate specialized student support services through the reconfiguration of E&G space in a highly accessible location to cultivate a transformative not transactional atmosphere. Student study rooms, offices for student support services, and space for students to access the university networks and other services.
2429.direct_services: By creating a space to foster innovation and collaboration, as well as, providing fundamental resources, FGCU will provide space for traditional, non-traditional and commuter student research and class activities, build skills for an ever- changing workforce, access to specialized support experience interactive learning in a highly accessible location on campus.
2429.population: University students with over 16.500 students served and university guests.
2429.outcome: Integrate students' holistic wellness with their educational goals to enhance their progression and provide an enriched learning and university experience. Metrics: Scores on National Survey of Student Engagement and Ruffalo Noel- Levitz Student Satisfaction Inventory. Ensure every student engages in academically integrated, high-impact practices including experiential learning to connect meaningful, real-world experience to their study and create personalized pathways of coursework that align with academic goals thereby improving retention and graduation rates. Metric: Percentage of students with two high impact practices by graduation. SUS performance-based metrics.

2776.description: LBJ Behavioral Services provides case management and counseling through a trauma-informed, ethical, culturally responsive program to support the mental well-being of underserved individuals and families.
2776.purpose: LBJ Behavioral Services provides case management and counseling through a trauma-informed, ethical, culturally responsive program to support the mental wellbeing of underserved individuals and families.
2776.activities: LBJ Behavioral Services provides case management and counseling through a trauma-informed, ethical, culturally responsive program to support the mental wellbeing of underserved individuals and families.
2776.direct_services: Through individualized case management, life skills development, and group psycho-education, we empower participants to build emotional resilience, access critical resources, and achieve greater self-sufficiency. Services integrate evidence-based practices, including Mental Health First Aid and Motivational Interviewing, and are delivered in English, Spanish, and Haitian Creole.
2776.population: The target population is underserved individuals and families across Central Florida. We estimate serving 300-500 individuals.
2776.outcome: Outcome measurement will include tracking participants' improvements in emotional wellbeing, service linkages, and progress toward individualized goals. Regular satisfaction surveys will also help ensure program quality and responsiveness.

The planning for the Roller Hockey Rink facility is a direct response to a community desire for a Roller Hockey Rink facility with a new roof to protect users from the elements. The Roller Hockey Rink facility will serve as a year-round premier facility open to the public for youth/adult use.

The planning for the Roller Hockey Rink facility is a direct response to a community desire for a Roller Hockey Rink facility with a new roof. Improve quality of education, measured by number of program registrants. Enhance or improve environmental conditions for wildlife and flora/fauna, measured through heat index, tree canopy calculations, assessments of population increases of wildlife and flora/fauna. Protect the general public from harm, measured by the amount of remediated soil and increased outdoor recreational space. Increase or improve economic activity, me

2786.description: Replace facility and habitat maintenance equipment, specifically, one (1) John Deere Gator TX, and two (2) gas powered pressure washers w/100 ft. hoses, 26 waterproof, long-range 2-way radios. These items are critical to our ability to efficiently carry out the maintenance of our facility, grounds and animal habitats and necessary to the functioning of our facility, programs and our manatee rescue team.
2786.purpose: To replace facility and habitat maintenance equipment, specifically, one (1) John Deere Gator TX, two (2) gas powered pressure washers w/100 ft. hoses, 26 waterproof long-range 2-way radios. These items are critical to the maintenance and functioning of our facility, grounds and animal habitats as well as the functioning of our Manatee Rescue Team.
2786.activities: Our facility and natural marine habitat are unique and vital assets for our dolphin and sea lion family, our programs, our community and the state. Maintaining these assets requires that we replace essential equipment as it deteriorates and becomes unusable. This funding will enable DRC to continue to maintain and improve our facility and animal habitats for the benefit of our animals, visitors and students as well as manatees in distress who will be rescued by our Manatee Rescue Team.
2786.direct_services: This funding will enable us to continue to maintain our facility and animal habitats, ensuring our ability to provide memorable, life-changing programs for individuals, families and students from Monroe County, all of Florida, the country, and around the world. It benefits our nation's wounded military veterans and their families who come to DRC to participate in our Wounded Warrior programs. In a
2786.population: Dolphin Research Center is a Florida Keys destination with over 70,000 visitors annually, including individuals, families, veterans and students from all walks of life and all areas of the Keys, the state of Florida, the country and the world.
2786.outcome: Replacing these critical equipment items will ensure our continued ability to: Provide the best possible home for our dolphin and sea lion family; Continue groundbreaking cognitive and behavioral research with dolphins; Aid manatees in distress through our Manatee Rescue Program; Enhance the lives of children with Special Needs and Make-a-Wish participants through our Dolphin Pathways program; Support Wounded Warrior Soldier visits to Dolphin Research Center to benefit our nation’s military men and women and bring much-needed joy into the lives of wounded soldiers and their families. Measured by comments and reviews, and increased number of visitors.

2745.description: This program serves 200–400 at-risk youth from economically disadvantaged neighborhoods by offering structured athletic, academic, and mentorship programs. Activities include sports leagues, tutoring, leadership development, and workforce readiness training, designed to reduce juvenile crime and strengthen police–community relations. The initiative aims to improve school attendance, academic performance, and behavioral outcomes while fostering trust and resilience among youth.
2745.purpose: Enhance its Police Athletic League (PAL) and Youth Empowerment Initiative, which provides positive outlets, mentorship, and structured athletic and leadership programs for at-risk youth within the city’s most economically disadvantaged neighborhoods. Funding will expand youth participation in sports, mentoring, academic enrichment, and workforce readiness programs operated in partnership with the Lauderhill Police Department and local nonprofits.
2745.activities: • Reducing juvenile crime through structured after-school and weekend programming. • Promoting physical fitness and teamwork through sports such as basketball, soccer, and flag football. • Enhancing academic achievement and workforce readiness through tutoring, leadership workshops, and vocational mentorship. • Fostering positive police-youth relationships that build trust and community resilience
2745.direct_services: The funding requested will directly support the Police Athletic League which provides accessible, structured and inclusive athletic programs for local residents-particularly undeserved youth and families. The initiative focuses on improving physical health, mental health well-being and cultural enrichment through organized sports such as soccer, basketball, cricket, soccer and flag football.
2745.population: Economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, grade school students, and high school students. Between 201- 400 of the target population expected to be served.
2745.outcome: Improve physical health through regular physical activities, participants will improve cardiovascular fitness, strength, and overall health, helping combat sedentary lifestyles and reduce the risk of chronic diseases. Measured by: enrolling and serve at least 1000 youth annually, maintain 90% participants satisfaction through annual surveys; 90 of participants attendance rate indicating consistent physical activity engagement, 80% of participants report increased energy and motivation for active lifestyle. Improve mental health: organized sports builds mental well-being by reducing stress, boosting self-esteem and fostering teamwork, discipline and goal-setting skills. Measured by: consisten

2749.description: To become a State of Florida approved Recruit Fire Training Facility, FL Statute 69A-37.060 requires a liquefied petroleum gas (LP) gas firefighting field with props for specialized training in LP gas floating fuel pit fire training, LP Fueled Automobile fire training, and a 500- gallon LP fuel tank with a shut-off valve for hose line approach and valve closure. This training field will enable North Lauderdale firefighter recruits and personnel to mitigate liquid petroleum gas fire incidents in the area. Funding for Live Fire Training with LP gas props per NFPA 1402 will enhance safety and operational readiness, reducing firefighter and civilian injuries.
2749.purpose: The goal is to provide a training facility that meets Florida statute 69A-37.060 Certification as an Approved Firefighter Recruit Training Facility and as a certified training facility as outlined by the Insurance Services organization (ISO). This allows North Lauderdale and surrounding jurisdictions to provide Live Fire gas field training that improves and/or maintains current ISO rating schedules for Fire Suppression & Public Protection for North Lauderdale Fire personnel and each surrounding
2749.activities: Training all area first responders for fire/rescue operations, consistent with National Standards. This central location will enable surrounding emergency response agencies within Central Broward to train and work together. Funding will provide training for all propane LP gas emergencies within the city and surrounding jurisdictions. By complying with FL State Statute 69A-37.060, the facility will train Fire Explorer youths to certify as State of Florida Level 1 and 2 firefighters.
2749.direct_services: Fire Rescue Personnel will be highly trained to mitigate any liquid petroleum gas fire incident that occurs within the city as well as the surrounding cities. In addition, the surrounding fire rescue agencies will receive this training as well.
2749.population: A better trained fire/rescue department will benefit not only all of the 47,000 residents of North Lauderdale, but also the local businesses, parks and other establishments through a better trained fire rescue agency. Additionally, neighboring Fire Departments will be able to train at this facility and that will benefit their communities as well.
2749.outcome: Better-trained first responders and a potential better insurance ISO rating. Progress will be measured by comparing the amount of training sessions per employee year and at the next ISO rating. North Lauderdale will also provide a career track for youths that reside in the city and desire to establish a career as a firefighter through state appropriations funding. The addition of the liquefied petroleum gas field will secure the approval for a state of Florida fire recruit training facility. This will be a great accomplishment and benefit for the community and surrounding communities.

2804.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2804.description: The current facility is deteriorating due to over 50 years of use for housing critical assets such as rotary aircraft and pesticides. Construction of a new, hardened facility will ensure continued services for routine operations and critical post-storm event response. Vector operations begin immediately after a storm event to protect residents from the increase in mosquito borne illnesses. Specialty equipment and materials must be protected from wind and flooding in a hardened facility.

3484.description: The Child Abuse Prevention Project will reduce foster care placements in Broward County by stabilizing 300+ at-risk families. Stabilizing these families will ensure their long term viability as a family unit and their ability to address healthcare challenges head on in the future.-Data tracked throughout the service and post-service periods. Improve mental health, The target population served by this project includes low-income, at-risk mothers and caregivers in Broward County who are facing crises such as poverty, housing instability, or lack of mental and physical healthcare

Funding will support the purchase of high-demand workforce training equipment, enhancement of clinical and simulation labs, and increased certification capacity for students preparing for immediate entry into medical and health-science fields. 2791.description: Enrollment at the Hialeah Campus has grown by over 50% in three years, from 7,500 students in fall 2021 to over 12,000 this term, driven by a population boom in Hialeah and nearby areas. Operating at full capacity, the campus faces challenges in meeting rising demand. Expanding the campus would enable more programs for career development and workforce training, addressing community needs and supporting regional economic growth. This investment is essential to maintaining accessible, high-quality education.
2791.purpose: Miami Dade College's Hialeah Campus serves a rapidly growing student population, and expanded facilities are essential to meet increasing demand. Additional funding will allow the campus to enhance educational spaces, provide access to state-of-the-art resources, and support workforce development programs, ensuring students have the tools they need to succeed in their academic and career goals.
2791.activities: Services and activities will include the development of expanded educational spaces, access to modern technology and state-of-the-art resources, and the enhancement of workforce development programs. These efforts will provide students with hands-on learning opportunities, updated facilities, and career-focused training to support their academic success and career readiness in high-demand fields.
2791.direct_services: The project will provide enhanced educational facilities, modern technology access, and workforce programs to equip students with skills for academic and career success.
2791.population: There are roughly 20,000 students that attend Miami Dade College Hialeah Campus annually.
2791.outcome: The project is expected to improve educational access, enhance student success, and address workforce needs. Outcomes will be measured through enrollment and graduation rates, student retention data, and job placement tracking in high-demand fields.

3213.description: This shovel-ready infrastructure project will construct a new potable well in North Okaloosa to support growth, economic development, and the existing customer base demands. It will provide additional drinking water and fire protection to the Shoal River Industrial Park and surrounding areas. The well adds resiliency and redundancy for North Okaloosa and enables transmission to South Okaloosa via the existing 30” water main, reducing coastal aquifer pumping in the Water Resource Caution Area. The project complements the Shoal River Ranch Water Reclamation Facility (SRRWRF) and supports long-term sustainability by reducing the cone of depression in southern Okaloosa, Walton, and Santa Rosa counties. The well is included in the County’s Individual Water Use Permit and has been designed in coordination with NWFWMD and FDEP.
3213.purpose: To ensure a reliable and sustainable water supply for current and future community needs, the requested funds will support the construction of a new potable water well. This project will: - Support population growth and residential development - Promote economic expansion and job creation - Enhance environmental protection through responsible water resource management - Improve public health by ensuring high-quality drinking water and adequate supply for sanitation and emergency needs
3213.activities: Activities include site preparation, well drilling, casing, pump installation, and integration with existing infrastructure. Services provided will include increased drinking water capacity, enhanced fire protection, and improved system resiliency.
3213.direct_services: This project will provide citizens with increased access to safe, high-quality drinking water and enhanced fire protection services. It will improve water system reliability and pressure, especially during emergencies or peak demand. Residents and businesses in North Okaloosa and surrounding areas will benefit from a more resilient water supply, supporting public health, safety, and future growth.
3213.population: The target population includes residents, businesses, and industrial users in North Okaloosa County, particularly those near the Shoal River Ranch Industrial Park and surrounding development areas. The new well will directly serve approximately 4,000 existing customers in North Okaloosa and support future growth. Additionally, the well enhances resiliency for the permitted Main system, which serves approximately 26,400 active connections across the County.
3213.outcome: The project will increase public water supply capacity, improve drinking water quality, and enhance system resiliency for North Okaloosa County. It will reduce reliance on stressed coastal aquifers, support economic development at the Shoal River Ranch Industrial Park site, and provide long-term sustainability for regional water needs. Outcomes will be measured through: - Hydrologic data analysis (e.g., rise in potentiometric surface of the Floridan Aquifer) - Water quality sampling and compliance with drinking water standards - System performance metrics including pressure stability and supply redundancy - Economic indicators such as job creation, business development, and utility demand gr

3269.description: The Family Initiative Autism Community Center will offer evidenced-based therapy services such as Applied Behavior Analysis, Occupational Therapy and Speech Therapy to individuals with autism from birth through adulthood. The Center will also host community-based programs to support early intervention services, social skills settings for adolescents and adults, and workforce readiness programs to teach independence of the individuals served at this location. The center will be built to ICC 500 standards and will serve as the only special needs shelter in the region during a storm.
3269.purpose: Building a community center which provides evidenced-based therapy services such as Applied Behavior Analysis, Occupational Therapy and Speech Therapy. The center will also host community-based programs to support early intervention services, social skills settings for adolescents and adults, and workforce readiness programs to individuals. The center will serve as the only special needs shelter in the region and will be built to ICC 500 standards to withstand hurricanes.
3269.activities: The services will include evidenced-based therapy services such as Applied Behavior Analysis, Occupational Therapy and Speech Therapy for families. It will also host community-based programs, such as social skills play groups, teen and young adult groups, arts and sports programs as well as sibling and parent groups. The center will also provide early intervention services, diagnostic evaluations for parents with infants and will offer workforce training, vocational opportunities, and internship
3269.direct_services: In addition to the activities and services described above, in the aftermath of Hurricane Ian, Family Initiative collaborated with local municipalities and stakeholders to determine how to help recovery efforts and resiliency activities for the special needs community. The need for a special needs family support and shelter facility is great.
3269.population: Individuals with autism and their families will be the primary population served. Over 800 individuals are expected to be served.
3269.outcome: Individuals with autism will be able to access programs uniquely designed to support their needs and their caregivers will be able to access support services. Children with autism will receive medically necessary services to help them achieve greater independent functioning. Young adults with autism will participate in workforce training, internships, and job placements. Families with special needs children will have a safe place to ride out a natural disaster. The success will be measured by tracking the number of individuals and families served and individual measures of success depending on their need/goal.

2933.description: The Hope Line for First Responders was initially funded by DCF for the Suncoast Region and the OAG starting 2024- 2025 for statewide expansion. This program provides immediate intervention through 1-866-4FL-HERO, managed by the Crisis Center of Tampa Bay. Initially, the project provided follow-up Care Coordination for First Responders within the Suncoast region (11 counties). Funding provided by the OAG in 2024-2025 allowed the expansion for the line and Care Coordination to serve First Responders statewide with immediate needs as well as follow up Care Coordination with a peer First Responder. We request funding to continue to help our efforts of supporting First Responders throughout Florida.
2933.purpose: Expand response to First Responders and their families, statewide.
2933.activities: Expanded call answering, resource cultivation, First Responder peer Care Coordination, and help line awareness for First Responders throughout the state of Florida.
2933.direct_services: The Crisis Center's approach to engage and coordinate First Responder Peers to assist first responders and their families in identifying services and supports in their community by providing trauma sensitive intervention that includes safety planning, information and referral. Some contacts will be provided with connection to peer First Responder Care Coordinators for additional support and connec
2933.population: First Responders and their families located in the state of Florida. The Crisis Center handled over 1,600 calls between October 1, 2024 and September 30, 2025. It is noted that the majority of callers identifying as first responders are law enforcement officers and the top three identified needs are 1) individual, family and community support 2) mental health and/or substance use disorders, 3) housing.
2933.outcome: The Crisis Center will continue to engage with first responders to assist with decreasing the stigma around asking for help (increase call volume) and continue to be an available resource for first responders experiencing mental health/substance use concerns, housing needs, financial assistance and any additional need identified (resources provided).

The proposed station will be located along Atlanta Ave. and US 19 just south of Weeki Wachee High School. This funding will allow the County to build a fully equipped facility to enhance fire and emergency medical services in a rapidly growing area.

3526.description: The goal of this project is to continue to lead the state and nation in research and development of regenerative orthopedic therapies and educate the citizens of Florida on the prevention and treatment of orthopedic injuries. A second goal is to leave a global footprint by developing innovative rehabilitation techniques that expedite the healing process and reduce the need for opioid usage and disseminating those techniques to clinical professionals. A third goal is to develop and retain a regenerative therapy workforce that increases access to qualified research and clinical staff as well as treatment options for more Florida citizens.
3526.purpose: The Andrews Research & Education Foundation will complete clinical research investigations to address unmet clinical needs of the Florida people to investigate the efficacy and safety of orthopedic interventions, to investigate alternative treatment methods, and to educate the people of Florida on additional options for treatment.
3526.activities: Successful research & development will result in cutting edge therapies and joint regeneration as well as improve the quality of life of orthopedic patients. Community educational events will aid in the prevention of orthopedic health related ailments.
3526.direct_services: The project will offer Floridians access to cutting-edge therapies, innovative devices, joint regeneration treatments, diagnostic services, personalized treatment plans, rehabilitation programs, and educational events, ensuring they benefit from the latest advancements in orthopedic care.
3526.population: This project targets a diverse group of patients, up to 400 individuals expected to benefit from alternative care treatments. Additionally, research publications will help other medical professionals adopt new techniques for improved care and outcomes. Primarily, the general public benefits by having access to the best orthopedic care available.
3526.outcome: The project aims to provide Floridians with innovative orthopedic interventions that alleviate conditions, reduce opioid usage, and enhance quality of life. Clinical trials will measure the safety and efficacy of these treatments. Research findings will be shared with the public to ensure access to the latest knowledge and interventions for optimal health. Developing additional regenerative workforce will allow more Floridians to access innovative treatment options.

The redesign will include modern amenities such as a welcoming lobby, a renovated auditorium, a historical gallery, classrooms, meeting rooms, and spaces for staff, making Moore Academic Recruiting Center a multifunctional facility. The center will primarily cater to individuals seeking to learn more about FSU’s academic and cultural offerings, with a focus on prospective students considering enrollment. By combining financial coaching, business development training, and structured workforce exposure, the program provides the practical tools needed for lifelong success.

By combining financial coaching, business development training, and structured workforce exposure, the program provides the practical tools needed for lifelong success

2903.direct_services: Direct services include paid apprenticeship hours for youth, wages for journeymen/mentors who supervise training, individualized mentoring, financial-literacy instruction, OSHA-10 certification, career-readiness coaching, and hands-on construction experience designed to prepare high school students and at-risk youth for employment.

Anchored within the Dennis Wilfong Center for Success at Wilton Simpson Technical College (WSTC), the Space Hub represents a powerful public-private partnership between the Hernando County School District, Hernando County Government, and a growing coalition of industry and community partners, including local Manufacturers Association, industry-related businesses, Brooksville–Tampa Bay Regional Airport, Space Florida, CareerSource Pasco-Hernando, and the Greater Hernando County Chamber of Commerce.
3278.purpose: The incubation center, known as The Space Hub, will create a collaborative ecosystem where existing businesses looking to expand their opportunities, entrepreneurs, researchers, and students can explore, innovate, and commercialize space technologies. Industry and education will meet to create emerging products and technologies in current fields such as, HVAC/R, welding, cybersecurity, semiconductor, and advanced manufacturing, all industries designated as high-growth and high-paying fields of w
3278.activities: Funds will support the creation of the Hernando County Space Hub at Wilton Simpson Technical College, an industry incubation center focused advanced manufacturing and space-related workforce clusters identified as in-demand by local CareerSource Pasco-Hernando Space Florida. Activities will include facility buildout, workforce training, and business incubation services. The Hub will provide technical education, entrepreneurship support, and hands-on lab experiences aligned with high-demand indus
3278.direct_services: The Hernando County Space Hub will provide citizens with direct access to workforce training, career placement, and business incubation services in high-demand industries such as aerospace, advanced manufacturing, and technology. Participants will benefit from hands-on technical education, certification preparation, and entrepreneurial support.
3278.population: This incubator can stimulate economic growth with Florida’s 12th District and will further and positively impact Florida’s footprint as a leader in space innovation. This will create a collaborative space, where every school within our District of more than 24,000 students, and surrounding areas, will have an opportunity to work hands-on with businesses who are willing to mentor the next generation of workforce. It will spur innovation, attract investments and generate new business opportunities
3278.outcome: The program has a clear economic development benefit for a community or region, such as workforce training centers. The project will benefit not only the School District, but the County as a whole. Key indicators will include completion and certification rates, job placement and retention, and levels of employer engagement through partnerships, internships, and new business activity

3244.description: Working on the priority list based on the hydraulic model on replacing the remaining Asbestos Concrete and Cast Iron water mains throughout the City of Lynn Haven's Water DIstribution System.
3244.purpose: Deisgn and costruction of approximately 6,665 LF of asebestos concrete and cast iron water mains.
3244.activities: Construction of new water mians that replaces asebestos concrete and cast iron water mains which have poor water quality and low pressure.
3244.direct_services: Water distribution improvements increasing water quality and fire protection.
3244.population: City of Lynn Haven residents and all water users. Approximately 21,000 residents plus businesses.
3244.outcome: Improved water quality. Water sampling and testing.

3030.description: This project enhances law enforcement's digital evidence capabilities, improving investigations and prosecution rates and accelerating timelines. Cellebrite technology will assist with securely sharing digital evidence across the state to make case critical connections, enhancing the ability to combat crime across the state.
3030.purpose: Digital evidence is now a feature in 90% of criminal cases (Wires Forensics, 2023). Thus, it is imperative to equip agencies across the state with secure technology allowing investigators and attorneys to safely share digital evidence with minimal delay. Cellebrite empowers agencies with state-of-the-art technology and role appropriate training to review and securely share evidence across jurisdictions, making case-critical connections to ensure justice is accelerated across the state.
3030.activities: This project enhances law enforcement's digital evidence capabilities, improving investigations and prosecution rates and accelerating timelines. Cellebrite technology will assist with securely sharing digital evidence across the state to make case critical connections, enhancing the ability to combat crime across the state.
3030.direct_services: Requested funds will not be used directly for services to citizens
