3030.outcome: Protect the general public from harm (environmental, criminal, etc.) and reduce substance abuse.

2849.description: This project would provide job placement services and/or additional independent living services to youth who are committed to the Department of Juvenile Justice custody and who have obtained a high school diploma or equivalent and are not currently enrolled in post-secondary education. Staff funded by the project would assist youth in developing resumes, searching job ads, preparing for interviews, and provide transportation to/from the job site. Staff would also network in the community to develop partnerships with local businesses that would be interested in providing job placement opportunities to eligible youth. Staff would also provide the youth with independent living skills group which would cover budgeting, necessary house work and house upkeep, obtaining loans and other financial assistance opportunities, car maintenance, accessing local transportation, and other skills needed t
2849.purpose: This project would provide job placement services and/or additional independent living services to youth who are committed to the DJJ custody and who have obtained a high school diploma or equivalent and are not currently enrolled in post-secondary education. After the youth are released from custody, the project would assist with job transfers or finding employment in their home community.
2849.activities: For eligible youth: Assistance in seeking and obtaining employment, transportation to/from job sites, and independent living skills. For the greater community: Youth who receive services will be current commitments to the Department of Juvenile Justice. By receiving these services, eligible youth, will demonstrate a reduced risk of recidivism and be productive members of their community
2849.direct_services: For youth eligible for the program: Assistance in seeking and obtaining employment, transportation to/from job sites, and independent living skills.
2849.population: Youth who receive services will be current commitments to the Department of Juvenile Justice. It is anticipated that between 25 and 50 youth will be eligible for this program.
2849.outcome: By receiving these services, eligible youth, will demonstrate a reduced risk of recidivism and be productive members of their community thus increasing community safety. Outcomes would be measured through follow-up surveys at 6, 12, and 18 months after discharge to determine employment, postsecondary enrollment, and any new criminal activity. Alternatively, law enforcement data could be used to assess recidivism.

2839.organization: Livingstone Schools Inc. dba Florida Trade
2839.description: Project will expand and strengthen high school Career & Technical Education (CTE) programs in Pasco, Pinellas, and Polk Counties. The goal is to help districts implement and more importantly sustain programs aligned with Florida’s Master Credential List while also achieving high completion and job connection rates, preparing students for high- demand careers through certifications, pre-apprenticeship recognition, and workforce readiness support.
2839.purpose: Funds will expand and strengthen high school Career & Technical Education (CTE) programs in Pasco, Pinellas, and Leon Counties. The goal is to help districts implement and more importantly sustain programs aligned with Florida’s Master Credential List while also achieving high completion and job connection rates, preparing students for high- demand careers through certifications, pre-apprenticeship recognition, and workforce readiness support.
2839.activities: FTA will guide selected schools in designing, launching, and sustaining high-quality CTE programs. Activities include program development, compliance and funding guidance, career exploration for students, credential alignment, and partnerships with employers to strengthen local workforce pipelines.
2839.direct_services: Students will receive career assessments, hands-on training, and opportunities to earn industry-recognized certifications and pre-apprenticeship credentials. Schools gain technical assistance to implement sustainable, DOE- compliant CTE programs aligned with credit-bearing requirements and high-demand career pathways.
2839.population: High School Students, and HS youth who are not college bound
2839.outcome: The project will improve workforce participation in High school CTE programming, increase credential attainment, expand job opportunities post graduation, strengthen employer partnerships, and enhance participant economic self- sufficiency. Additional expected benefits include reduced recidivism and substance abuse, improved physical and mental health, and increased community safety. Outcomes will be measured through employment attainment tracking, credentialing data, partner agency reports, pre-/post-assessments, employer verification forms, surveys, attendance records, and follow-up evaluations conducted at multiple intervals through the certification process.

3615.description: The requested funding amount will be used to reimburse child welfare provider agencies who were not paid by Embrace Families prior to their contact with the DCF being withdrawn. These agencies have performed child welfare services, as a contract provider on behalf of the State of Florida, and are owed these funds.
3615.purpose: Support Abused, Abandoned, and neglected children
3615.activities: These funds will be used to reimburse agencies for services that have already been provided to vulnerable children and families, who are/were being served through the child welfare system during Embrace Families contract period.
3615.direct_services: Reimbursement for services already provided to vulnerable children and families.
3615.population: Youth, At-Risk Youth, Abused, Abandoned, and neglected children.
3615.outcome: The expenditure of funds requested will be used to reimburse child welfare providers agencies who provided child welfare services on behalf of the State of Florida. Unpaid services have resulted in a shortfall in the budgets of these provider agencies, having a negative fiscal impact on their agency, impacting their ability to continue to provide services to children in foster care.

Distributed through 34 selected partners, including the Boys & Girls Clubs, Kidsville provides fun, curriculum-aligned resources that support reading comprehension, civic awareness, and personal growth. Each monthly publication includes literacy enrichment, community connections, health and wellness content, and civic and cultural learning.

2837.activities: Funds will support a project coordinator; printing, materials/content, distribution and shipping to 34 partner sites.
2837.direct_services: The Kidsville Newspaper of Florida Project - an educational and youth-focused publication designed to engage, inform, and inspire young readers through literacy-based content, community highlights, and youth development stories. Distributed through 34 selected partners, including the Boys & Girls Clubs, Kidsville provides fun, curriculum- aligned resources that support reading comprehension, civic
2837.population: Elementary-aged youth throughout the state of Florida. An estimated 125,000 youth will be served.
2837.outcome: Some benefits include literacy enrichment, aligned to state academic standards; community connection; civic and cultural learning; and health and wellness skills development. The newspaper is provided in a printed copy to bridge the digital literacy divide for youth residing in low-income households. The impact will be measured by the number of newspapers distributed to elementary-aged youth across the state. An estimated 125,000 youth will be served.

It builds upon a partnership between Agricultural extension offices, present in every Fl County, and a central resource for rural communities, and Local Arts Agencies who are practiced in delivering high quality arts programs throughout the state. Working closely and in alignment with Ag Extension offices' mission and programs, LAA's will provide monthly arts programming including self-contained art- project kits, workshops and arts experiences led by rural Florida artists, traveling art exhibits, and community projects that foster engagement and connection to the rich cultural heritage of rural Florida. This request supports continuation of the pilot program in Desoto, Glades, Hardee and Hendry Counties and pote
3623.purpose: The goal of the program is to enrich the lives of rural Floridians through the arts via a partnership between County Agricultural Extension Offices and Florida Local Arts Agencies. Knowing that participation in the arts contributes to the overall quality of life, strengthens community vitality and contributes to the economy, the pilot program increases rural communities access to high quality arts experiences to provide rural communities with measurable social, economic and educational benefits
3623.activities: Local Arts Agencies, recognized by the Florida Department of State, Division of Arts and Culture, will work with Agricultural Extension offices and Florida artists living in or focused on rural communities to create and deliver an easily deployed, comprehensive arts program that reflects Florida's rural communities, their unique experience, cultural character and rich heritage. Available in English and Spanish, Kits include all necessary materials and easy-to-follow instructions, do not require any prior arts training and can be distributed for take home use or as part of a community activity. 2. Artist-led activities that bring the arts

Additional populations to be served include those with physical and mental health challenges - as experience with the arts provide benefits for both as well as disabled populations likely to benefit from access to the arts. Recognition that rural communities are vibrant and rich with artistic traditions: From family and friends who love to work leather, paint landscapes, weave baskets, sew quilts, tell stories or photograph rodeos, arts and creative talent are present and valued in rural communities. 3. 2916.description: The Keiser University Forensic Simulation Lab will enhance hands-on training for students and practitioners in forensics, criminal justice, and law enforcement. The lab will be equipped with modern forensic technologies used in real-world investigations, helping to expand the pipeline of skilled professionals and address workforce shortages in these critical fields. In addition to student instruction, the lab will be available for ongoing training for state and local law enforcement partners.
2916.purpose: The goal is to provide workforce, hands-on training for students, law enforcement, and first responders. Simulation will create opportunities for these professionals to reenact crisis situations with technology, tools, and processes. Current shortages of forensics laboratories, including Rapid DNA equipment, will continue to be required in Crime Scene Analytics and other Criminal Justice related professions. Our Simulation/ Forensics Lab should produce more workforce ready professionals.
2916.activities: The project will support hands-on forensic training for students and professionals, including evidence processing, forensic analysis, and investigative simulation using modern equipment aligned with industry and law enforcement standards.
2916.direct_services: The lab will directly support workforce training for students and law enforcement professionals, strengthening public safety capacity and improving investigative outcomes statewide.
2916.population: University students pursuing criminal justice and forensic-related degrees, as well as state and local law enforcement professionals receiving advanced training. Hundreds of practitioners and many graduates are expected to be served annually.
2916.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved workforce readiness, increased hands-on training capacity, and stronger partnerships with law enforcement agencies. Outcomes will be measured through student completion rates, skills assessments, employment and placement data, employer feedback, and participation levels from partner agencies.

3056.description: OATS is requesting $854,461 to support and maintain the operation of our new Senior Planet Center in Miami alongside the development of a network of community-based partner sites to serve as host locations for Senior Planet's award- winning digital literacy programming. The Senior Planet Center in Miami is a technology-themed community center for older adults that will welcome the region's residents with a complete range of mainstream technologies and a rich slate of multilingual programming.
3056.purpose: OATS is requesting $854,461 to support and maintain the operation of our new Senior Planet Center in Miami alongside the development of a network of community-based partner sites to serve as host locations for Senior Planet's award-winning digital literacy programming. The Senior Planet Center in Miami is a technology-themed community center for older adults that will welcome the region's residents with a complete range of mainstream technologies and a rich slate of multilingual programming.
3056.activities: This project will offer a range of tech-themed programs to individuals aged 60+ living in South Florida. OATS will offer technology access alongside programs designed specifically for older learners at the Senior Planet Center in Wynwood and at dozens of partner locations throughout the region. Programs are free and accessible virtually for those who are unable to attend.
3056.direct_services: OATS has an extensive library of proprietary curriculum covering all aspects of technology from device fundamentals to social media, privacy, job searching, AI and much more. OATS will use its library of multilingual materials (English, Spanish) and is translating many into Haitian. Most programs are delivered live, in-person by trained OATS instructors and are comprised of multiple sessions.
3056.population: The target population for this project is older adults living in the Miami area. More specifically, individuals aged 60 and older. With this funding, OATS anticipates serving approximately 5,000 individuals.
3056.outcome: Expected outcomes for older adult participants include: improving mental health (75% will feel more connected to others, 50% will feel less alone); improving quality of education (90% will report satisfaction with the quality of education they receive through Senior Planet); protecting the public from harm (70% will feel more confident about staying safe- and recognizing scams when using email or the internet); enhancing individuals’ economic self-sufficiency (80% will feel better equipped to find resources online to improve their life and save money.

3304.description: The Society, in support of efforts by the IRL NEP, will construct an innovative wastewater treatment system as part of the Bowen Aquarium and Conservation Center, to reduce effluent to the IRL and educate Floridians on the importance of innovative and effective wastewater treatment. In addition to treating effluent, the innovative wastewater system has been designed to highlight technologies and green infrastructure that can be replicated throughout the IRL to improve water quality.
3304.purpose: The purpose of this project is to construct an innovative wastewater treatment system as part of the Bowen Aquarium and Conservation Center, to reduce effluent to the IRL and educate Floridians on the importance of innovative and effective wastewater treatment. In addition to treating effluent, the innovative wastewater system has been designed to highlight technologies and green infrastructure that can be replicated throughout the IRL to improve water quality.
3304.activities: The construction of an innovative wastewater treatment system as part of the Bowen Aquarium and Conservation Center.
3304.direct_services: The Bowen Aquarium will provide cultural and educaitonal experiences for Floridians and visitors, as well as job oppourtunities.
3304.population: Visitors to the aquarium which is estimated to be roughly 575,000 annually and enhance the educational experience of approximately 53,000 students a year through STEM field trips and educational programs.
3304.outcome: The Bowen Aquarium will be pioneering a new combination of industrial waste water techniques that can be used on small sites to treat and use the waste water on site. This approach decreases pressure on existing waste water treatment programs, demonstrates innovative technology and will educate the public and industry about the process. We will be monitoring post-treatment parameters on our industrial wastewater and tracking the gallons diverted from local sewer treatments facilities through this process.

3281.description: The $5 million investment will support construction of a 20,000-sq-ft Community Health and Fitness Center on PHSC's West Campus in partnership with the YMCA of the Suncoast. The facility will serve students, faculty, staff and the community by enhancing health sciences programs and promoting wellness. By leveraging existing co-located space and new construction, the project maximizes state investment and strengthens student engagement and community partnerships.
3281.purpose: The funds will allow for the planning, design, and construction of a 20,000 sq.ft. facility on PHSC's West Campus in New Port Richey. Through a public-private partnership, the facility would be equipped and operated by YMCA of the Suncoast to allow their full offering of resources to the community.
3281.activities: This facility will have the ability to provide youth development programs, including after-school care, summer day camps, youth sports leagues and teen leadership programs that provide safe, supervised environments while promoting healthy habits. Health and wellness activities to include group exercise classes (yoga, aerobics, strength training), personal training, and wellness coaching programs designed to address chronic health issues and promote active lifestyles across all age groups.
3281.direct_services: Funds will allow for a fitness and recreation facility that includes cardio and strength training equipment, group exercise studios, and gymnasium space. Other structured programming such as youth after-school care, summer camps, sports leagues, and senior fitness classes, as well as wellness support services including fitness assessments, personal training, nutrition education, and chronic diseas
3281.population: Students, staff, faculty, and the community may all benefit from this project. The facility is projected to serve approximately 3,500-4,500 individuals annually through direct memberships and program enrollment, plus an additional 2,500+ individuals through community programming, special events, and day-use access. This represents reaching approximately 35-40% of the city's population with critical health, wellness, and food security services.
3281.outcome: Strengthening community partnerships and improving economic activity in this area of the county is an anticipated benefit. Impact will be determined by reviewing annual operational reports and partnership activities to assess community and economic impact, as well as tracking partnership agreements, joint initiatives, and participation data to assess the depth and effectiveness of community collaboration.

2945.description: The BSO Crime Laboratory needs a portable, compact, all-in-one Rapid DNA instrumentation that can perform DNA analysis on known samples (oral swabs, blood standards, bones, teeth, etc.) in a single-use cartridge. There are several critical incidents that warrant the need for this type of technology. This project is directly related to mitigation, response, and recovery from a natural disaster or other critical incidents. The Criminal Investigations Division is committed to aligning our goals and objectives with the agency's Strategic Plan by incorporating technological innovation, thus ensuring the highest standards of public safety for residents and victims throughout the State of Florida.
2945.purpose: The purpose of this project is to have a Rapid DNA program that is part of a Mass Disaster Response plan. The technology is deployable to field areas where a mass disaster occurs and there is a need to identify victims.
2945.activities: The Rapid DNA program will allow for the processing of DNA samples collected during disaster response effort. The Rapid DNA instrument is self-contained and deployable. Samples can be processed within 90 minutes to obtain results for comparison to family reference samples.
2945.direct_services: The services will be DNA processing for purposes of identification of unidentified human remains collected in situations of a mass disaster such as plane crash, hurricanes, etc.
2945.population: The target population is expected to primarily be the residents of Broward County; however, since the unit is capable of being transported within vehicles, the instrument can be used to assist other agencies and counties within the entire state of Florida.
2945.outcome: The benefit of this project will be the preparedness and response plan that will allow for the quick identification of human remains obtained from mass disasters that will occur in the future within the state of Florida and specifically within the Broward County area. This will help to provide closure to families and allow for human remains to be returned to the families for burial purposes.

2963.description: The requested funds will support the IDD Family Support & Navigation Pilot, expanding and strengthening The Arc Jacksonville’s Family Support program across Northeast Florida. The program provides personalized guidance, referrals, and resources, much like a helpline, for individuals with intellectual and developmental differences (IDD) and their families, helping them navigate complex systems of care and connect to vital community services.
2963.purpose: The requested funds will support the IDD Family Support & Navigation Pilot, expanding and strengthening The Arc Jacksonville’s Family Support program across Northeast Florida. The program provides personalized guidance, referrals, and resources, much like a helpline, for individuals with intellectual and developmental differences (IDD) and their families, helping them navigate complex systems of care and connect to vital community services.
2963.activities: The program will offer a regional helpline, individualized navigation, and educational workshops to help individuals with IDDs and their families access vital supports and services. Assistance will include navigating benefits such as the iBudget waiver and ICMC program, housing and financial planning while connecting families to trusted community resources and programs.
2963.direct_services: Direct services will include personalized guidance and support for individuals and families seeking help with IDD- related needs. Families will receive direct one-on-one assistance from trained staff to access services such as healthcare, housing, education, employment, and benefits—ensuring they are connected to the right resources at the right time to improve stability and quality of life.
2963.population: The target population includes individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) and their families, particularly those who are economically disadvantaged, in transition, or at risk of service disruption. The pilot will serve hundreds of individuals and family members annually, building on The Arc Jacksonville’s existing Family Support program and growing demand for navigation and benefits assistance.
2963.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved physical and mental health, increased access to essential services and benefits, enhanced economic self-sufficiency, and reduced reliance on crisis or emergency systems for individuals with IDD and their families. Outcomes will be measured through program tracking and reporting, including the number of individuals served, successful benefit and service linkages, follow-up resolution of needs, and reductions in repeat crisis requests, along with family feedback demonstrating improved stability.

3627.description: The Clearwater Harbor Marina sustained damage from Hurricane Helene in September 2025. During the storm, a sailboat destroyed a bridge in the Clearwater Harbor Marina’s North Basin. Funding will be used to bring the marina back to standard operations, which will allow for the docking of individually owned vessels at the marina and passenger ferry service vessels at the originally intended docking location behind the BayCare Sound venue.
3627.purpose: The City’s docks in Downtown Clearwater sustained damage following Hurricane Helene in September 2024. Rebuilding the docks will allow the Clearwater Ferry passenger ferry vessels to dock at the originally planned location behind the BayCare Sound. The dock location will connect riders coming from Clearwater Beach and Dunedin to the park’s primary venue and surrounding businesses.
3627.activities: Funds from this program will be utilized to pay for materials and labor to fully reconstruct the docks at the Clearwater Harbor Marina’s North Basin. This will allow passenger ferry vessels to make use of a new, reconstructed dock at a dock location behind the BayCare Sound stage at Coachman Park.
3627.direct_services: Following the reconstruction of this dock, citizens will be able to ride passenger ferry service from a new, optimally located dock behind the BayCare Sound stage at Coachman Park. Clearwater Ferry operates passenger ferry services that connect riders utilizing this Downtown Clearwater stop to the docks at Clearwater Beach and Downtown Dunedin.
3627.population: There is no specific target population who will be served. Passenger ferry services at this location are available to the general population. The Clearwater Ferry system currently provides over 2,000 trips a month.

3628.description: Focused on the large number of students who aren't on track to complete four-year degrees, the Future Career Academy model disrupts the cycle of dead-end or low-paying jobs and/or unemployment, and puts students on the path to in-demand, living wage entry-level jobs in their communities with long-term career growth and sustained employment. In partnership with School Districts, State Colleges, County and City Government, and leaders in the regional business community, this year-long, innovative program includes required state curriculum with a focus on workforce development, such as resume writing, interview skills, dressing for success, information on job training, etc. The result is a life-changing opportunity for students and their families, and an economic catalyst for businesses and the communities they serve.
3628.purpose: Focused on the large number of students who aren't on track to complete four-year college degrees, the Future Career Academy model disrupts the cycle of dead-end or low-paying jobs and/or unemployment and puts students on the path to in-demand, living wage entry-level jobs in their communities with long-term career growth and sustained employment. The result is a life-changing opportunity for students and their families, and an economic catalyst for businesses and the communities they serve.
3628.activities: In partnership with School Districts, County and City Governments, State Colleges, and leaders in the regional business community, this year-long, innovative program includes a supplemental weekly curriculum that complies with English state standards in the 12th grade year, as well as supplemental workforce lessons available 9th - 11th grades.
3628.direct_services: Students are educated about the community's thriving industries with details on the types of positions available including salaries, training, etc. Students complete financial literacy components, and participate in a business panel event, a business field trip, career fair, and signing day which highlights the students who have secured employment, enrollment, or enlistment opportunities.
3628.population: The target population includes jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, homeless persons, High School students, and employers who are struggling to find workforce. This program expects to serve over 15,000 individuals in the target population.
3628.outcome: This program will improve the quality of education, improve economic activity, create specific and immediate job opportunities, and enhance individual economic self-sufficiency. FCA does this by preparing and connecting students with great jobs in their communities. It will bridge the gap for non-college bound students by providing a targeted, integrated curriculum that includes specific soft and workforce development skills, access to certifications and apprenticeships, a solid pathway to directly enter the workforce, and the opportunity to identify a long-term career, not just a job. Our goal is for every graduating senior to have a clear and actionable plan for post-graduation success whe

3417.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
3417.description: Funds will be used to sustain 24/7 sexual assault forensic exams, crisis advocacy, and therapy for sexual assault victims in Duval, Nassau, and Baker Counties. Support will also expand professional training, strengthen multidisciplinary coordination, and enhance prevention education to promote healing, accountability, and a safer, more resilient Northeast Florida community.
3417.purpose: The purpose of these funds is to sustain and grow services in NE Florida during a time of reduced funding from State, local and Foundation resources. It is essential that we continue to provide 24-hour crisis intervention response to victims of sexual violence, their families, law enforcement and hospitals. Services include forensic exams, mental health therapy for victims, their families and first responders, as well as community education & prevention programs.
3417.activities: *24-hour Rape Crisis Hotline – Around the clock staff respond to victims and their families, as well as law enforcement and hospitals. *Forensics - Exams are conducted, evidence collected, and chain-of-custody is maintained. *Advocacy & Prevention – Certified Sexual Assault Advocates respond to all referrals of sexual violence, they also work toward the prevention of sexual assaults.
3417.direct_services: 24-hour crisis intervention response to victims of sexual violence, their families, law enforcement and hospitals. Services include forensic exams, mental health therapy for victims, family members and first responders, as well as community education & prevention programs.
3417.population: Target Population: Victims of sexual violence and their families and those impacted by sexual violence Individuals to be served: Approximately 5,000 (This number reflects calls to our Rape Crisis Hotline and the subsequent services we provide (Advocacy, Forensic Exams, Mental Health Therapy). This also reflects mental health therapy for first responders who often face secondary trauma as a result of their work. Education & Prevention services will also be offered in partnership with NE FL non-pr
3417.outcome: Benefit/Outcome: Improved physical, mental, emotional and economic wellbeing for victims of sexual violence and an improved understanding of how the community can work together for the prevention of sexual violence. Methodology: Electronic case records, pre/post trauma symptom checklists, client satisfaction, counseling progress notes, attendance logs, program evaluations, CRM and law enforcement tracking.

3097.description: The Sebring Community Redevelopment Agency, local businesses and community members are partnering with the Sebring Hall of Fame, a 501(c)(3) organization, to re-purpose a building at the entrance of beautiful downtown Sebring to house a permanent 12,000 square foot museum dedicated to the storied history of the racing event that has been a 12- hour endurance race since 1952. This Museum encapsulates the history of the cars, drivers, teams and individuals who made this the first and most historically significant endurance race in the U.S., and includes some of the most famous drivers and celebrity racers in the world.
3097.purpose: 1. Preserve and promote the history and importance of the Sebring Race and Florida's role in that history. 2. Highlight significant milestone events of cars, drivers, teams and people associated with the Sebring Race. 3. Attract additional investment for the City of Sebring, the Sebring Airport and track and Highlands County. 4. Generate significant incremental visitor trips and per capita spending, and Direct/Indirect area employment. 5. Underline the importance of the Sebring Race and prevent
3097.activities: 1. First quality museum exhibits on the history and events surrounding the Sebring Race. 2. Live lectures and video presentation on cars, drivers, teams, people and key events in its history. 3. Special annual events to celebrate cars, drivers, teams and people (e.g., astronauts, celebrities, champions). 4. Archival research important to the sport of endurance racing, both physical and digital. 5. Built local and state-wide awareness and pride in this important international event.
3097.direct_services: 1. Historical exhibits and presentations important to Sebring and Florida history, and to racing history. 2. Educational programs for both residents and students in the local area and statewide 3. Access to archival resources that would otherwise be inaccessible or lost to history. 4. Public events to celebrate the history of Sebring and its international stature. 5. Potential to attract investmen
3097.population: 1. Florida residents (annual) - 30,000 2. FIT Florida visitors (3 seasons) - 15,000 3. Annual race visitors (March) - 17,500 4. Track-time races (300 days/year) - 5,000 5. Destination visitors (collectors, writers) - 2,500 and 6. Student field trips - 1,000
3097.outcome: 1. Increase in visitor trips and per-capita spending in Sebring/Highlands County. 2. Direct and Indirect employment. 3. Local investment and promotion (i.e., build on "Home Town Makeover featured on HGTV). 4. Encourage investment in track facilities for racing and other automotive technology.

3286.description: This project funds a new National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) compliant fire station and training facility in Lake Placid, FL. It will replace two outdated buildings with a single, modern station in a growing area of town, improving access to U.S. 27 and reducing response times. The facility will also include a training center, eliminating the need for firefighters to travel to Avon Park, enhancing local readiness and public safety across southern Highlands County.

It will replace two outdated buildings with a single, modern station in a growing area of town, improving access to U.S. 27 and reducing response times. The facility will also include a training center, eliminating the need for firefighters to travel to Avon Park, enhancing local readiness and public safety across southern Highlands County.

3286.population: The general public I.E.: elderly persons, persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, at-risk youth, homeless persons, students ranging from preschool to univeristy, drug users, victims of crime. The entire population of Lake Placid and the surrounding area
3286.outcome: Provide the most efficient and effective fire and emergency medical responses to the Lake Placid area including quicker reponse times and higher quality training and facilities for first responders.

3078.description: The funds needed for the construction of a new bus station and improvements to the existing Metrorail station and garage. The bus stop will serve as a crucial transit hub, enhancing access and encouraging more ridership. This supports efforts to reduce congestion, address the housing shortage, and build a stronger transit network. A well- designed bus stop will also lay the foundation for subsequent phases, which include developing workforce housing, retail space, and day care facilities nearby.
3078.purpose: The funding will serve to assist in part with the redevelopment of a major public transportation facility located at Earlington Heights Station for the residents of Miami-Dade County.
3078.activities: Construction of new MetroBus drop off area (7 bus bays w/ concrete canopies & sitting areas, etc.), renovation of existing 1,000 space garage (repairing, cleaning, & painting exterior of garage; renovating restrooms & garage offices, etc.), renovating MetroRail Station (new exterior lighting; enhanced landscaping/irrigation including new public park plaza; covered walkways; etc.)
3078.direct_services: Upon completion, the redeveloped bus depot will offer a safe and accessible public transportation terminal with an all day parking facility. The development will include a new drop off and pick up area, safe covered walkways, a public park plaza, new sitting area. The station provides county wide transportation to the residents of Miami-Dade County.
3078.population: Economically disadvantaged persons, elderly person, and the general public
3078.outcome: Accessible public transportation will reduce road congestion, energy use, air pollution. Provide greater mobility and accessibility, improve employment opportunities and expand accessibility having a positive impact on area retail businesses. Measured by completion of construction of new bus station and station improvement, monitoring ridership activity and reduction in congestion

3344.description: Glades County and the City of Moore Haven through the City County Public Works Authority (CCPWA) continues to address protection of State waters - Lake Okeechobee, Caloosahatchee River Basin and Estuary and the Everglades West Coast Watersheds (Fort Myers area) and ultimately south into the Florida. Everglades. Funds needed to design and construct a gravity sewer collection system in the Country Side Meadows neighborhood, west of West Avenue and Leisure Boulevard. The project allows for the removal of 46 failing residential septic systems with connection to the centralized wastewater treatment system. These improvements will significantly reduce nutrient discharges entering into the Caloosahatchee River Basin, Lake Okeechobee Watershed BMAP areas. The project supports state water quality goals, improves life, public health, property and the environment, ground and surface waters.
3344.purpose: Goal is protection of life, health, safety, property, the environment and of State waters, improves water quality and quantity by reducing pollutants, nitrogen, phosphorus, TMDLs entering critical State waters with the installation of wastewater infrastructure, that allows for the removal of 46 failing septic systems in Country Side Meadows community located in Glades County, a designated Rural Area of Opportunity. Once completed, the project will reduce pollutant discharges, improve public heal
3344.activities: Glades County and the City of Moore Haven through the City County Public Works Authority (CCPWA) will seek contractual services through the procurements policies and procedures for preliminary engineering, design, permitting, bidding, project management/administration, engineering during construction, on-site construction observations and construction of a gravity sewer system in the Country Side Meadows community.
3344.direct_services: Direct services provided include modern, reliable wastewater services as the project allows for eliminating failing septic systems that create flooding, odor, health and contamination issues. Citizens will experience improved sanitation, lower maintenance costs, and healthier living conditions once connected to the regional system. The project provides for reduced pollutant discharges, improved pu
3344.population: Target population is the State, citizens, visitors, general public and residents in Glades County, which is designated as a Rural Area of Opportunity, financially disadvantaged community and surrounding areas within the Caloosahatchee River Basin and Estuary and the Everglades West Coast Watersheds (Fort Myers area) and ultimately south into the Florida Everglades.
3344.outcome: The expected benefits include improved wastewater management, cleaner groundwater, and reduced surface water pollution. The project will prevent 672 pounds of nitrogen and 269 pounds of phosphorus annually from entering water tables and state waters. Outcomes will be measured by project completion and certification, pollutant load reduction modeling, abandonment of 46 septic systems which is required within 90 days from the infrastructure being available.

3392.description: This local funding initiative request will help fund a center at Lubavitch Hebrew Academy in Margate that will holistically provide and streamline services to the student to ensure all their physical, emotional, social and educational needs are met and that they are reaching their maximum potential for success. It will do this through a whole host of programs ensuring that no child is slipping through the cracks.
3392.purpose: We are going to create a center where all the various physical, emotional, psychological, educational etc. services that are available to our students is streamlined and enhanced. Additionally, with a coordinator, we will be able to ensure that children don't fall through the cracks and there is full coverage of their needs.
3392.activities: All types of physical, emotional, psychological, educational etc. services that can benefit the students of the Chabad Hebrew Academy.
3392.direct_services: All types of physical, emotional, psychological, educational etc. services that can benefit the students of the Chabad Hebrew Academy.
3392.population: School aged children attending LHA are the target population. We expect to serve over 800 children in an ongoing manner.
3392.outcome: The expected benefit and outcome of this project is that our students will be able to achieve their full potential and not be held back by various challenges presented to them. We are able to measure student success as we track them through the year using our student information system.

3293.description: Telephone companies no longer support copper telephone lines resulting in frequent service outages and long repair times. The goal is to replace the aging telephone lines with microwave similar to the remaining Statewide Law Enforcement Radio System (SLERS) network.
3293.purpose: Improved dependability and reliability of communications for all Statewide Law Enforcement Radio System (SLERS) users working in Glades County.
3293.activities: Replacement of end-of-line and non-supported copper telephone lines with microwave link.
3293.direct_services: Improved dependability and reliability of communications for all Statewide Law Enforcement Radio System (SLERS) users working in Glades County.
3293.population: All residents, businessses, and vistors of Glades County.
3293.outcome: Improved dependability and reliability can be measured by L3Harris engineers and personnel from DMS through trouble tickets generated for outages.

3371.description: This project is to provide back up emergency storage for sludge at NWWRF in the event SWWRF cannot receive the sludge or there is an issue with conveyance. The scope will include retrofit of an existing and decommissioned digester a into sludge holding tank, demolition of existing and construction of new drying pads at an alternate site. The location of the existing drying pad at NWWRF, near 26th Ave N, makes the area vulnerable to overspill, which can enter the neighborhood. This project will benefit the City of St Petersburg residents as well as the wholesale customers of St Pete Beach, Treasure Island, South Pasadena, and unincorporated Pinellas County (Bear Creek).

The scope will include retrofit of an existing and decommissioned digester a into sludge holding tank, demolition of existing and construction of new drying pads at an alternate site. 3371.activities: This project provides construction phase funding to modify an unused tank into a sludge storage tank at the Northwest Wastewater Plant. This sludge storage tank would be utilized during emergency events where the sludge transfer pipe to the Southwest Wastewater Plant or the Plant itself has been compromised and cannot receive sludge. Construction would include relocation of the sludge drying pad away from a high traffic and residential area.
3371.population: General publix, approx. 91,000 including wholesale customers
3371.outcome: Improve process resiliency, particularly in the solids handling and biological treatment processes, during process upsets and emergencies. Improve process resiliency, particularly in the solids handling processes, during process upsets and emergencies. Minimize potential exposure of wastewater sludge to the public by relocating the drying pad. Reduce sanitary sewer overflows caused by drying pad overflows or sludge transfer disruptions.

3634.description: POC's Emergency Assistance (EA) Program serves low-income, economically disadvantaged individuals, families, and elderly residents in Pinellas County who are at risk of becoming homeless. The EA Program provides short-term emergency financial assistance for rent/mortgage, utilities, transportation, food, and clothing that enables this population to avoid homelessness.
3634.purpose: Our POC staff will evaluate clients' short- and long-term needs to create strategies that help reduce their reliance on recurring emergency assistance. Eligible clients will be referred to our Family Development/Wrap Around Program, which offers intervention services aimed at promoting financial stability and economic self-sufficiency. These services include financial literacy, budgeting, and education or training programs
3634.activities: The funding will provide emergency assistance for rent, utilities, transportation, food, clothing, and other essential needs for individuals, families, and the elderly in Pinellas County who are at risk of homelessness.
3634.direct_services: The EA Program provides short-term emergency financial assistance for rent/mortgage, utilities, transportation, food, and clothing to enable this population to avoid homelessness. Financial assistance for rent/mortgage, utilities, transportation, food, and clothing ranges from $750-$1,000 per client for a total of 500 clients.
3634.population: This project will serve 500 individuals, including the elderly, economically disadvantaged, and others in need of emergency assistance, throughout Pinellas County.
3634.outcome: Clients will create strategies to reduce their reliance on recurring emergency assistance. They will have the opportunity to participate in our Family Development/Wrap Around Program, which offers intervention services designed to promote financial stability and economic self-sufficiency. These services include financial literacy, budgeting, and education/training. Success will be measured by making payments, enabling them to maintain stable housing.

3415.description: The two-year pilot program would provide respiratory clinical services to individuals diagnosed with respiratory disease/COPD through in-home visits and telemedicine, with supporting behavioral health care pulmonary support services. The goals of the pilot project are to reduce hospitalizations and emergency department usage by 30%, and increase cost savings to the Medicaid program for persons diagnosed with respiratory disease/COPD.
3415.purpose: Reduce hospitalizations and emergency department usage by 30%, and increase cost savings to Medicaid program for persons diagnosed with respiratory disease/COPD. Enhanced Access to Specialized Care Coordination: Maximizing HCBS for the Aging Population. New Services and Enhanced Programs: Chronic Disease Management in SMMC 3.0 Managed Medical Assistance Program.
3415.activities: In-home respiratory care services provided by respiratory therapists and telemedicine based social services and pulmonary physician care. Patient management and continuity of care provided to persons diagnosed with respiratory disease/COPD through the provision of respiratory clinical services provided in the home, with supporting behavioral health and pulmonary services.
3415.direct_services: In-home respiratory care services provided by respiratory therapists and telemedicine based social services and pulmonary physician care.
3415.population: 300-500 Medicaid enrollees diagnosed with respiratory disease/COPD. Review hospitalization data compiled by AHCA to identify appropriate enrollees.
3415.outcome: Florida Medicaid in its analysis of Potentially Preventable Events of Florida Medicaid Enrollees; Winter 2018 report - shows that COPD was number one (18.7% of 100%) of the top ten conditions involved in potentially preventable hospital admissions/re-admissions. In AHCA's 2024 report, Cardiac disorders (heart failure; cardiac defibrillator, cardiac catheterization) were the largest contributor to PPAs followed by chronic disorders.

3399.description: This project includes the construction of a 5-foot-wide sidewalk along the north/east side of Shady Hills Road from Dr. Mary Giella Elementary School to Bosley Drive, a length of approximately 2.6 miles. The project includes a midblock crossing with pedestrian beacon on Shady Hills Road at Greenglen Lane with a 5’ sidewalk connection on the south side of Greenglen Lane west of Shady Hills Road to allow pedestrian access to Elsie Logan Memorial Park. Additionally, the project includes a 50-foot-long (+/-) section of 10’ multi-use path (MUP) on the south side of Shady Hills Road connecting the existing MUP to the Suncoast Trail. This project will provide a safe connection to Dr. Mary Giella Elementary School.
3399.purpose: The overall goal is to enhance transportation equity, reduce pedestrian risk, and support active transportation in a growing area of Pasco County. More specifically, the project will provide a continuous 2.6-mile sidewalk to ensure safe pedestrian access along a high-traffic corridor, create a safe school route for students and families traveling to and from Dr. Mary Giella Elementary School, provide a mid-block crossing with a pedestrian beacon to reduce pedestrian- vehicle conflicts and improv
3399.activities: This project includes Construction activities, safety and accessibility enhancements, and public services and community benefits.
3399.direct_services: Direct services include a safe route for users including pedestrians and students and also accessibility for all users.
3399.outcome: The project is expected to significantly improve pedestrian safety, accessibility, and connectivity along Shady Hills Road. This can be measured by crash and safety data analysis and community feedback. Pasco County Schools also may measure the amount of students who walk to school.

3508.description: Provide improved ADA access to the municipal dog park.
3508.purpose: Provide improved ADA access to the municipal dog park.
3508.activities: Install an ADA compliant concrete walkway at the dog park.
3508.direct_services: Provide improved ADA access to the municipal dog park.
3508.outcome: The benefit would be improved access to the park. The outcome will be measured by the replacement of the current walkway to an ADA compliant walkway through linear feet.

3453.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
3453.description: Florida consistently ranks as a top destination for human trafficking activity. The No More Foundation offers a FREE Anti-Trafficking Training to schools, businesses, churches, civic organizations, health care facilities & professionals, and law enforcement, educating them on how to spot the signs and report suspicious activity to protect their communities. We also provide outreach opportunities for the community to engage in serving survivors of human trafficking in meaningful ways.
3453.purpose: Many Floridians aren't aware of the trafficking issue in the state. Even if they know about it, they don't know what they can do about it. We have developed a short training session filled with information, solutions and conversation around the topic. So thousands of participants can know what is going on, how they can help, without putting themselves in danger.
3453.activities: Collaborating with leading programs in the area, No More offers human trafficking training to churches, schools, businesses, healthcare professionals, and law enforcement, educating them on how to spot the signs and report suspicious activity to protect their communities. We also provide outreach opportunities for the community to engage in serving survivors of human trafficking in meaningful ways.
3453.direct_services: Our training is available online and in person for any organization or individual.
3453.population: The target population is adults and teens in the state. The No More Foundation has trained over 133,900 individuals on the subject matter of human trafficking since July 1, 2022
3453.outcome: Participants will hear real stories, find out how they can prevent trafficking, protect their children and feel empowered and equipped. Outcomes will be measured by numbers of participants and feedback.

3668.description: Equip traffic signal cabinets with UPS battery backups to provide power during an outage. These systems are crucial for maintaining safe and continuous traffic signal operation during power failures caused by storms, accidents, utility work, or grid failures.
3668.purpose: Equip traffic signal cabinets with UPS battery backups to provide power during an outage. These systems are crucial for maintaining safe and continuous traffic signal operation during power failures caused by storms, accidents, utility work, or grid failures.

3668.direct_services: Operational traffic signals improve safety to the motoring public, decreases vehicle collisions, and frees up law enforcements need to control traffic.

Operational traffic signals improve safety to the motoring public, decreases vehicle collisions, and free’s up law enforcements need to control traffic (Measurement: Reduced vehicle collisions due to loss of power at the traffic signal cabinet)

3717.description: The IL Culinary Workforce Development Program aims to: 1) Provide supportive and rehabilitative services and training for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD), equipping them with practical culinary and workplace skills. 2) Facilitate community-based, competitive employment opportunities by connecting participants with on-site positions, local café partnerships, and broader employment networks. 3) Advocate for and expand supported competitive employment for adults with disabilities, enabling participants to achieve financial self-sufficiency and meaningful inclusion in the workforce.
3717.purpose: 1) Provide supportive and rehabilitative services and training for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD), equipping them with practical culinary and workplace skills. 2) Facilitate community-based, competitive employment opportunities by connecting participants with on-site positions, local café partnerships, and broader employment networks. 3) Advocate for and expand supported competitive employment.
3717.activities: Current participants will continue to hone their culinary skills in our program. New participants will complete an initial training program to learn the basics of working in a commercial kitchen (food handling, workplace safety, food prep, equipment operation, customer service, & teamwork). Once this training is completed, participants will move to food prep training, and finally customer service.
3717.direct_services: Utilizing a nationally accredited curriculum, residents of Independence Landing will be provided with employment training and be given the opportunity to learn and work in a commercial kitchen. Program will be expanded so other community members will be able to participate in the employment training as well.
3717.population: 50 - Unemployed and/or economically disadvantaged adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD).
3717.outcome: The program annually provides over 50 paid trainee positions, with 37% of graduates securing employment within six months. Participant skills are assessed quarterly using a comprehensive skills assessment tool, tracking competencies in food preparation, safety, equipment operation, customer service, and teamwork. Job placement outcomes are monitored through the Independence Landing database.

3593.description: Hillsborough County Schools will use SchooLinks to streamline Bright Futures tracking amid new, complex eligibility changes in this pilot. As the only platform built to keep districts, students, and families aligned, SchooLinks offers real- time insight into GPA, test score, coursework, and service hours. This ensures readiness while replacing fragmented tracking systems with a unified, data-driven approach that helps every student stay Bright Futures–ready.

3593.activities: The project will give families a clear Bright Futures tracker to support informed choices and expand scholarship opportunities. It provides real-time updates on GPA, coursework, test scores, and service hours, lets families upload missing documents, and offers verified service tracking and personalized planning to help more students qualify.
3593.direct_services: The funding will give families direct access to a Bright Futures tracker that increases awareness and participation in the scholarship. Students and parents will receive personalized updates, clear guidance on requirements, tools to verify service hours and upload documents, and an easy way to stay on track for eligibility.
3593.population: The target population is at-risk youth, grade school students, and high school students. It will serve more than 800 people.
3593.outcome: improved quality of education through increased Bright Futures readiness and clearer academic planning for students and families. Increased economic activity by expanding the number of students who qualify for Bright Futures, reducing college costs for families, and supporting a stronger, better-prepared workforce. Increased Workforce Readiness. Measurement: Track the percentage of students completing an annual eligibility check, the number of students meeting Bright Futures benchmarks, and increased accuracy and verification of coursework, test scores, and service hours.

3661.description: The funds requested will directly support Kappa League, a nationally recognized initiative that develops young men in grades 6–12 through a structured curriculum built around seven core phases. The program promotes academic excellence, provides college and career guidance, offers scholarships, and equips participants with the leadership and professional skills needed to excel in today’s workforce.

Through hands-on guidance, service, and networking, young men in grades 6–12 gain the skills needed for higher education, career success, and personal growth, preparing them to become future community leaders.

Rules about support animal use in Florida vary. A model procedure, supported by legal and psychological research, will continue to be developed for use in Florida for forensic interviews.
