3716.description: The University of Florida will leverage its institutional investment in artificial intelligence and world class facilities to bring to Florida the best medical researchers at the intersection of brain health and machine learning to build the next generation of medicine. In addition to cutting edge research, the program will develop new strategies to treat brain afflictions and diseases using the latest advancements in AI. The University of Florida will incorporate the many resources on hand, including students, faculty, and partnerships with other state institutions. The funds will be used to enhance existing facilities, making the absolute most of the state's existing investments.
3716.purpose: To establish a state of the art and world-class research program at the cutting edge of biology and artificial intelligence at the University of Florida.
3716.activities: Scientists will be researching improvement in the understanding of the brain and its related afflictions and diseases. Multiple clinical trials in the areas will establish strategies and treatments to cure and prevent maladies of the brain and its functions.
3716.direct_services: Such a program and its facilities will not only benefit patients with afflictions of the brain, however it will also benefit all citizens in its research of treatments that prevent illnesses and enhance the cerebral health of all. Further, it will benefit the education of students from across the broad section of disciplines whose study involves the brain by granting them access to the highest lev
3716.population: As stated, the target population is limitless as the objective is to bring together the best experts in the field of brain research to research, learn, and promulgate strategies and treatments across the spectrum of brain-related health.
3716.outcome: Each project will address specific research questions that are highly relevant to an important scientific problem using established technologies and experimental protocols. During the funding period, progress will be evaluated by written progress reports including qualitative and quantitative data related to the proposed specific aims. These findings will then be submitted to scientific journals.

3711.organization: North Miami Foundation for Senior Citizens
3711.description: Improved nutrition, social engagement, transportation, improved mental health, and overall improved health through access to home delivered meals, transportation, assessment and other services thereby stabilizing elder's risk; providing adequate nutrition and other in-home services are vital to the wellbeing of seniors; improved mental health functioning due to improved services and social interaction which are critical for elders facing isolation, depression - while improving quality of life.
3711.purpose: Improved nutrition, social interaction, transportation, improved mental health, and overall health through access to home delivered meals, groceries, transportation, assessments and other services thereby stabilizing risk; adequate nutrition and other in-home services are vital to the health and wellbeing of seniors; improved / stabilized mental health functioning due to improved services and social interaction which are critical for elders facing isolation and depression due to loneliness.
3711.activities: Home delivered meals, transportation, screening and assessments, telephone reassurance and other services to elderly residents who are at risk, and homebound.
3711.direct_services: Home delivered meals, seven days per week, to elderly residents at risk of hunger and malnutrition. Transportation, screening and assessments, social interaction, telephone reassurance and other services provided to at-risk and homebound elders.
3711.population: Elder persons at risk of malnutrition and food insecurity.
3711.outcome: Improved / stabilized mental health functioning due to improved nutrition, transportation, assessments, social interaction, telephone reassurance and other services for isolated elders at risk and elders facing isolation and depression due to loneliness.

3787.description: This project will improve public safety and provide law enforcement with tools to enable swift incident response, stronger protection, better crowd control, and heightened security along SR811 with significant tourist activity and regional traffic flow. This project would install barriers to protect pedestrials along the sidewalk from vehicle inspired attacls. Also includes purchase and installation of an integrated camera and survelliance system.
3787.purpose: Installation of barriers will help reduce the threat of and protect citizens from terrorist attacks involving motor vehicles inspired by recent attacks in New Orleans, Vancouver, Germany, et al.
3787.activities: Reduced threat level and enhanced protection allowing citizens to continue to attend popular events and continue to benefit from strong tourism.
3787.direct_services: Incident response, crowd control, heightened security, ensuring the safety of residents and visitors.
3787.population: City residents and visitors. 12,000 residents and 50,000+ visitors for various events.
3787.outcome: Installing bollards will improve safety by preventing vehicles from entering pedestrian areas. This is critical for protecting attendees at popular events from potential vehicle attacks, a concern heightened by recent events. Surveillance will improve incident response and heighten security in a main transportation corridor (SR811). Methodology involves attendance at events throughout the year. Incident response times, incident resolutions, threat detection and prevention, number of car plates detected, and number of infractions recorded.

3724.description: This program involves the replacement of outdated 9-1-1 dispatch consoles with modern, space-efficient units to improve operational effectiveness and support future growth. The project aims to reduce the physical footprint of console infrastructure within the communications center, while also expanding capacity from current levels to support up to 15 dispatch positions. This will enhance emergency response capabilities, provide greater flexibility for staffing during peak demand or special events, and ensure the system meets current ergonomic, technical, and public safety standards.
3724.purpose: To provide a modernized and efficient facility for processing 9-1-1 calls and dispatching Fire and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) services, ensuring improved reliability, functionality, and support for current and future operational needs.
3724.activities: Enhanced E9-1-1 call-taking and dispatching of EMS and Fire resources to ensure rapid, coordinated emergency response.
3724.direct_services: Enhanced E9-1-1 call-taking and dispatching of EMS and Fire resources to ensure rapid, coordinated emergency response.
3724.population: Citizens and visitors to Escambia County Florida. >350K
3724.outcome: The modernization of 9-1-1 facilities will enhance the speed and efficiency of emergency call processing, resulting in faster response times and improved public safety outcomes. Escambia County Administration ensures accountability and continuous improvement by monitoring 9-1-1 service performance through regular internal and external audits.

3745.description: This program is designed to strengthen the City’s capacity to address food insecurity by ensuring seniors have consistent access to nutritious meals.
3745.purpose: This program is intended to increase the City's ability to combat food insecurity among its most vulnerable population by providing the City's senior population with a stable source of meals.
3745.activities: Funding for this program will enable the City to provide a source of meals for its most vulnerable and food insecure seniors. For the seniors who will receive meals through this program, they will be able to experience more stability and security.
3745.direct_services: Increased access to food security for vulnerable seniors through the increased delivery of meals to the seniors in need in our community.
3745.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is reduced food insecurity and increased stability for vulnerable senior residents by providing consistent access to nutritious meals, thereby improving their overall health, well-being, and quality of life. Outcomes will be measured by tracking the number of seniors served, the number of meals distributed, program participation rates, and ongoing eligibility records. Additional evaluation may include participant feedback and periodic assessments of service consistency and delivery.

3765.description: The new community aquatic facility improvements will include a children’s interactive water feature element with a zero entry kiddie pool and water playground structure, new resort style pool with a lazy river and small water slide. Also due to the age of the current facility, a new expanded lap swim pool will be construction. The new facility will also include new locker rooms, office, storage area and family restrooms.
3765.purpose: Constructed more than thirty plus (30+) years ago, the pool has reached its ‘end of life’ and has reached its maximum capacity. The City fields daily requests for usage that go unfulfilled. Local swim clubs, neighborhood schools and local non-profits have lined up to request availability of the existing facility. The needs and requests are greater than the existing capacity can fulfill. Swim times are limited in order to accommodate as many residents as possible.
3765.activities: Constructed more than thirty plus (30+) years ago, the pool has reached its ‘end of life’ and has reached its maximum capacity. The City fields daily requests for usage that go unfulfilled. Local swim clubs, neighborhood schools and local non-profits have lined up to request availability of the existing facility. The needs and requests are greater than the existing capacity can fulfill. Swim times are limited in order to accommodate as many residents as possible.
3765.direct_services: Expanded swim classes/lessons for children and adults, extended free swim times, more recreational facilities (lazy river, kiddie pool, recreational play equipment), pool safety programs, lap swimming for leisure and competition, etc.
3765.population: Bonita Springs residents, both children and adults as well as residents from neighboring communities such as Estero, Fort Myers Beach and North Naples/Collier County. With the expansion of the aquatic facilities the City expects to serve well over 10,000 people per year.
3765.outcome: Swimming is a low-impact exercise that benefits cardiovascular health, muscular strength and endurance. Swimming also can help reduce stress, improve mental health and promote relaxation. Increased number of individual residents, swim clubs, swim classes, etc., utilizing the new facility.

3778.description: The Duval Street project would feature a new pump station to support increased performance of the stormwater system throughout the entire Lower Duval corridor and provide comprehensive flooding mitigation. The existing pump station serving the corridor would be replaced and this new pump station would manage expected increases in stormwater runoff to prevent Duval Street flooding. The project would also include a series of pipe upgrades within the Duval Street corridor itself and connecting it to the pump station to move water away from areas prone to flooding on Duval Street.
3778.purpose: The Duval Street and Mallory Square Area Stormwater Pump Station and Resilience Project is a comprehensive flood mitigation project designed to improve stormwater management, enhance infrastructure resilience, and reduce chronic flooding in Key West's critical economic and cultural corridor.
3778.activities: Funds will be allocated and awarded for construction and redevelopment of existing stormwater systems by structural hardening, resilience upgrades, stormwater wells to redirect runoff underground, water quality treatment features and storm drain inlets and pump station, tide valves to prevent stormwater intrusion, and upgrades to the underground stormwater infrastructure to increase drainage capacity.
3778.direct_services: Flood mitigation will protect public and private property, utility infrastructure, Key West's commercial economic core district from flood events, storm surges, and unusually high tidal events.
3778.population: A large portion of Key West's 17,000-member workforce relies on the project area for employment, including over 5,100 workers directly employed within the project footprint. Additionally, the area supports over 2.7 million annual visitors, who rely on transportation networks, accommodations, and commercial activity within the corridor.
3778.outcome: Capturing and treating stormwater will improve near shore water quality while mitigating flooding impacts and hazards. Methodology utilized to confirm this outcome will be the tax revenue generated by keeping Key West's critical commercial corridor accessible and resilient in storm and tidal events.

3801.description: The remaining funds from Fiscal Year 2023-2024 OCEARCH Mayport Research and Operations Center (Jacksonville University) (SF 2756) should revert from Jacksonville University and be reappropriated to the City of Jacksonville for capital improvements to the City of Jacksonville property being utilized for the OCEARCH Mayport Research and Operations Center.
3801.purpose: Funds will support the construction of a purpose-built facility (OCEARCH’s Global Headquarters). This facility will consolidate all OCEARCH operations and research activities, greatly expanding public access and providing colleges, universities, K–12 schools, and research entities with unprecedented opportunities to engage in ocean science, conservation, and applied research. The facility will also serve as a new workforce development hub for maritime operations.
3801.activities: This complex will include building(s) for public education and displays, public meetings, workforce development partnerships and OCEARCH ship operations. The facility will host public education opportunities (K-12, undergraduate, graduate, and life-long learning) centered around sharks and other marine life in Florida as well as partnerships with local industry partners in the maritime realm.
3801.direct_services: Education and career development will play a critical role in the facility. We will work with local school districts and state college to host experiential education opportunities, both locally and virtually. Further, we will work with local industry partners that focus on maritime career development. Outcomes will be measured by number of students served.
3801.population: The target population includes over 1M residents in Duval County and the 22M overnight and day trippers who visit Duval County annually. Nearly 28,000 people visit Jacksonville every night and another 30,000 day-time visitors. As an international leader in shark and ocean research, the facility will also attract visitors from around the state of Florida and other other states and countries. With Mayport's rich maritime history, our target audience includes residents and visitors of Duval County,
3801.outcome: The OCEARCH Headquarters and marine science research facility will provide economic benefits to Mayport, Jacksonville, and Florida at large through generated tourism, with outcomes measured by annual visitors, and overall economic impact. Expanding scientific knowledge of sharks will play a key role in the facility's overall mission. Outcomes will be measured by number of research efforts hosted, papers published, and overall impact in driving datacentric maritime policy efforts. Local education outreach will be measured by number of students served and career development will play a critical role in the facility. Additionally, the general public will develop a better understanding of public

2311.description: Polk State College seeks $25,389,752 to renovate Building #3 (LLC) on the Lakeland Campus, a central hub for student learning and support. LLC houses classrooms, laboratories, faculty and staff offices, the campus library, and the testing center—facilities that serve thousands of students each year. The project will replace the aging roof, upgrade HVAC and technology systems, and modernize classrooms, labs, and offices to meet current instructional and safety standards. Expansion of the library and testing center will increase access to academic resources and improve service capacity for a growing student population.
2311.purpose: The funds will be used to renovate and modernize Building #3 (LLC) on the Lakeland Campus, replacing failing infrastructure and upgrading instructional and student support spaces. This project will extend the facility’s useful life, improve energy efficiency, and expand access to library and testing services, directly enhancing student learning and success.
2311.activities: Project activities include replacing the existing roof; upgrading HVAC, electrical, and technology systems; modernizing classrooms, laboratories, and offices; and expanding the library and testing facilities within Building #3 on the Lakeland Campus. These improvements will provide modern instructional spaces, expanded student study and testing areas, and upgraded technology infrastructure to support high-quality teaching and learning.
2311.direct_services: Polk State's mission is to provide accessible, affordable, quality higher education and training to the Polk County community. With 92% of Associate in Science graduates and 85% of baccalaureate degree graduates employed or continuing their education, some of the highest percentages in the state, Polk State consistently produces graduates who are well-prepared for the workforce. Projects such as t
2311.population: The target population includes the more than 9,300 students served annually on Polk State College’s Lakeland Campus, who will directly benefit from enhanced classrooms, laboratories, and academic support spaces. Building #3 also houses the campus library, testing center, and tutoring services, which serve both enrolled students and members of the public pursuing workforce certification or continuing education.
2311.outcome: While this project is not expected to immediately increase the total number of degrees or certificates awarded, it will enhance student retention, completion, and academic performance by improving access to library, tutoring, and testing services. Renovation and expansion of these areas in Building #3 will provide modern, technology-enabled study spaces and flexible learning environments that better support students’ academic needs. Success will be measured by tracking student usage of library and tutoring services, monitoring testing center capacity and throughput, and analyzing retention and course completion rates.

1926.description: Funds will support design and permitting for Phase 3 of Lady Lake’s Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) expansion. The project will increase capacity to 3.0 MGD, implement advanced wastewater treatment (AWT), and expand reclaimed water capabilities. These upgrades address rapid growth and capacity constraints, enhance nutrient removal, and ensure compliance with the Silver Springs (SILV) and Upper Ocklawaha (OKLA) BMAPs, protecting regional water quality and supporting sustainable development.
1926.purpose: The funds will support design and permitting for Phase 3 of the Town’s Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) expansion, which will increase capacity to 3.0 MGD, implement advanced wastewater treatment (AWT), and expand reclaimed water capabilities. The improvements are needed to address rapid population growth, meet regulatory nutrient limits, and ensure long-term compliance with the Silver Springs (SILV) and Upper Ocklawaha (OKLA) BMAPs.
1926.activities: Activities will include engineering design, environmental and regulatory permitting, process and hydraulic modeling, site investigations, development of construction plans and technical specifications, cost estimating, and preparation of bid documents. These services will advance the project to construction readiness and ensure all regulatory requirements are addressed.
1926.direct_services: The project will provide the community with a fully designed and permitted expansion of the WRF, enabling the Town to move forward with construction of additional treatment capacity, AWT processes, and reclaimed water improvements. This will support reliable wastewater service, protect groundwater and springs, and ensure adequate capacity for existing and future customers.
1926.population: The project will serve the Town of Lady Lake’s approximately 17,000 residents, as well as future residential and commercial developments in the Town’s rapidly growing utility service area. Beneficiaries also include surrounding communities and users of the regional springs and surface waters protected by improved wastewater treatment.
1926.outcome: Expected Outcomes: Improved wastewater treatment performance, increased capacity to 3.0 MGD, enhanced nutrient removal to support BMAP compliance, and expanded reclaimed water capabilities to reduce potable water demand. Method of Measurement: Evaluation of projected treatment capacity, modeled AWT effluent concentrations, BMAP compliance tracking, and updated reclaimed water utilization and potable-offset estimates.

1675.description: This project will retrofit, harden, increase the capacity of the existing pump station, and enable the optimization of its operation. It will improve storage and conveyance capabilities by mitigating flooding and reducing nutrient loading in the drainage basin, thereby improving the flood quantity and water quantity level of service. Project location: NE 26 Avenue between NE 204 Terr to NE 205 Street.
1675.purpose: The goal is to mitigate flooding by increasing and enhance the capacity of the existing stormwater pump station (NE 26 Avenue Stormwater Pump Station), by optimizing its operation, prevent pollutants from entering the stormwater systems, and impact the water quantity and quality in the nearby C-9 watershed basin in Miami-Dade County. Project location: NE 26 Avenue between NE 204 Terr to NE 205 Street.
1675.activities: Addition of an emergency generator at the pump station; and upgrade, hardening, and elevation of pump station's electrical and mechanical components.
1675.population: General—thousands of individuals will be served.
1675.outcome: Mitigate flooding by increasing and enhancing the capacity of the existing stormwater pump station (NE 26 Avenue Stormwater Pump Station)——measured by decrease in flooding incidents and reduction in the number of flood complaints received.

3370.description: Design design (planning/engineering) for improvements necessary for the rehabilitation/replacement of the Cove Stormwater Pump Station and critical infrastructure to reduce flooding and harden utilities.
3370.purpose: Design for the rehabilitation/replacement of the City's Cove Stormwater Pump Station that corresponds to the Mutli- Basin Assessment.
3370.activities: Planning and Engineering services to replace the Cove Stormwater Pump Station.
3370.direct_services: Design for future stormwater and other critical infrastructure improvements to enhance resiliency of the neighborhood.
3370.population: Directly impacts approximately 1,500 residents residing within the neighborhoods of Basin III (477 acres) as well as community establishments.
3370.outcome: Reduce infrastructure failures and minimize risk of flooding, and maintain emergency access within areas (Basin III) serviced by the Cove Stormwater Pump Station. Visual observations, loss of property reports associated with flooding within the Basin III area; includes road closure logs and incident response times.

1804.description: The construction of Fire Station 17 will enhance public safety and emergency response in an underserved, economically disadvantaged community by reducing response times, improving fire suppression, and expanding emergency medical services. It will also serve as a community resource, offering fire prevention education, emergency preparedness programs, and a 160-person community room, maximizing resources while strengthening public safety and economic growth.
1804.purpose: The requested funds will be used to construct a new fire station in an underserved community that experiences over 5,000 emergency calls annually. This investment will improve response times, enhance fire suppression and medical services, and provide fire prevention education and community engagement opportunities, ensuring greater public safety and support for residents and businesses.
1804.activities: The funds will support the construction of a new fire station that will provide fire suppression, emergency medical response, fire prevention education, and community engagement services. This facility will house fire responders, prevention teams, and a 160-person community room, ensuring faster response times, improved public safety, and enhanced emergency preparedness for an underserved area.
1804.direct_services: The funding will provide critical fire suppression, emergency medical response, and fire prevention education to residents in an underserved area with over 5,000 emergency calls annually. The new fire station will ensure faster response times, improved life-saving capabilities, and enhanced public safety programs while serving as a community resource for education and engagement.
1804.population: The target population includes underserved and economically disadvantaged residents and the general population in Tallahassee’s Southside, ensuring equitable access to fire suppression, emergency medical response, and public safety resources. The new fire station will serve thousands of residents, businesses, and visitors, addressing over 5,000 emergency calls annually and enhancing community-wide safety and resilience.
1804.outcome: The new fire station will improve response times, fire suppression, and medical services in an underserved area with over 5,000 emergency calls annually, while also lowering insurance costs, attracting businesses, and supporting fire prevention education. Success will be measured through response time data, emergency call volumes, fire damage reduction, and community engagement metrics.

3487.description: State support for care at the Steven A. Cohen Military Family Clinics at Centerstone and Aspire Health Partners will continue to provide critical expansion of behavioral health services for Military Veterans, National Guard and Reserve and military connected families of all ages. Too often our countries military and their families struggle to cope with mental health concerns related to a life of military service and experience barriers to care such as ability to pay, access to childcare during therapy or transportation to and from appointments. Our Cohen Clinics will continue to provide evidence based, culturally competent, targeted therapy for all mental health concerns, couples & family relationship issues, transition challenges and children's behavioral concerns. Services will include assessment, diagnosis, outpatient treatment both in-person or via tele video as well as case manageme
3487.purpose: Cohen Military Family Clinics at Centerstone and Aspire Health Partners will provide critical ongoing expansion of behavioral health services for Veterans, National Guard and Reservists and military family members of all ages across the state. This population struggles with the side-effects of a life of service to our country; moves, deployments, relationship and parenting stressors, trauma, other mental health concerns. Aspire and Centerstone provide evidenced based, culturally competent, perso
3487.activities: Veterans and military families of all ages will be provided initial assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning and outpatient mental health therapy tailored to the identified needs of the individual, couple and/or family to both target the concerns and improve quality of life for our military-connected families. These clinics also offer whole-person support via case management. All care is available across the state of Florida, either in-person or via telehealth as described in Ch. 65D-30 and in
3487.direct_services: Veterans, National Guard and Reserve and their families of all ages will be provided services to include initial assessment, treatment planning, suicide screening and intervention (as appropriate), crisis intervention, case management (to provide wrap-around community resources and referrals), individual, couples, family and/or group outpatient therapy both in-person and via televideo across Flori
3487.population: Military Veterans, National Guard and Reserve and their family members of all ages. We expect to serve between 401-800 individuals yearly across both Cohen Clinics at Centerstone and Aspire Health Partners.
3487.outcome: We will improve the mental health of those served by the reduction of depressive and anxiety symptoms by 25%, reduction of PTSD by 25%, improved quality of life by 10%, reduction in suicidal ideation by 20%. Outcome measures will be collected for each client served at initial assessment and monthly throughout each client's episode of treatment. Outcome measures include: PHQ-9 (for Depression), GAD-7 (for Anxiety), C-SSRS (for suicide risk), PCL-5 (for PTSD) and QLES (quality of life rating scale) at baseline and discharge.

3389.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3389.description: The purpose of this program is to reimburse the school for the additional cost of providing Kosher meals over what the Federal Government is reimbursing under the National School Lunch Program.
3389.purpose: These funds will enable the school to continue to serve our students Kosher meals and snacks during school. These funds specifically make up the difference between what the Federal Government is paying and what the meals actually cost.
3389.activities: Breakfast, Lunch and snacks will be served daily to the student of Chabad Hebrew Academy.
3389.direct_services: Breakfast, Lunch and snacks will be served daily to the student of Chabad Hebrew Academy.
3389.population: School Aged children are the target population, over 800 individuals are expected to be served.
3389.outcome: The expected benefits are that when students receive healthy and nutritious meals following the USDA guidelines, they are statistically more likely to be successful academically. The methodology we use to measure the outcome is both attendance and standardized testing scores.
